## ROW 349 -- turning the ggml-port body OFF makes arm E SLOWER, not faster: the residual is not body identity alone

**Card:** docs(tensor): row 349 emitted pair-dot vs ggml-port body on the bare token (off `main` at `e9665a1`). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-r349`, `docs/row-349-body-identity`.

**Question this row answers.** ROW 344/348 measured arm E (production's own emitted body, `metal-q4k-ggml-port` ON in the default `metal` feature list) at 21.181-21.215 ms against arm C's hand-written `q4k_pair_dot` at 17.408-17.447 ms (1.21-1.23x), and ROW 348's statement-level diff found no scaffolding difference -- the residual was attributed to body identity (the ggml-port body's `sumy0..3`/`acc1_0..3`/`acc2_0..3`/`sc16_0..3`/`sc8_0..7` temporaries, live across the whole reduce loop). This row tests that attribution directly: rebuild `omega` with `metal-q4k-ggml-port` removed from the `metal` feature array (transient edit to `omega/Cargo.toml`, reverted before this commit; every other `metal` sub-feature, including `metal-packed-row-nsg2`, stays on) and re-measure arm E. If the port body IS the whole 3.8 ms gap, arm E(off) should land near arm C (~17.4 ms).

**Method.** Two builds of `omega/tests/matvec_roofline_ladder.rs`'s `whole_token_matvec_sequence_bare` (`#[ignore]`d, `--features metal,instrument`, release): (1) as shipped on `main` (port ON), reused/re-run this session; (2) `omega/Cargo.toml`'s `metal` array with the `"metal-q4k-ggml-port"` line removed, `cargo test -p omega --no-run` to force a targeted `omega`-only recompile (16-17s, confirms no other crate depends on that exact feature string), then the same timed run. A third, throwaway instrumentation pass (temporary `println!`/`std::fs::write` in `production_reduce_kernel`, reverted before commit, `git diff --stat` confirmed clean) dumped the ACTUAL emitted MSL for the `ffn_up` shape (rows=14336, k=4096, Q4_K) from both builds and diffed them byte-for-byte.

**Data -- measured (V2 evidence), all from `time_bare_dispatch_sequence`'s 225-dispatch bare token, 7 repeats/arm:**

| Cell | Arm E ms (median) | Arm C ms (median) | E/C ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1: port ON (as `main`) | 21.181 (CoV 0.10%, 190.40 GB/s) | 17.429 (CoV 0.04%, 231.40 GB/s) | 1.215x |
| 2: port OFF | 22.707 (CoV 0.08%, 177.69 GB/s) | 17.447 (CoV 0.17%, 231.17 GB/s) | 1.302x |

Arm C is unaffected either way (17.429 vs 17.447, within CoV -- expected, `q4k_pair_dot` is never touched by this feature). Arm E moves the WRONG direction: turning the port OFF made production's own emitted kernel **1.526 ms slower**, not faster, and widened the gap to arm C from 1.215x to 1.302x.

**Mechanism, confirmed by the emitted-MSL diff, not assumed.** The byte-level diff between the two builds' `ffn_up` kernel source (`emitted_on.msl` vs `emitted_off.msl`, both 28,235 bytes before the loop-body diff) shows the port-OFF build's inner loop reads, literally:
```
sumf[q] = sumf[q] + q4k_pair_dot(blk, iq, ir, yl, yh);
```
-- the exact same function name arm C's hand-written body calls, confirming `push_packed_row_blocked_body`'s `plain_product` fallback arm (`omega/src/msl.rs:4240` region) engages correctly once `use_ggml_port` is false. **This means ROW 348's attribution was incomplete: even when the emitted kernel's per-iteration reduce body is byte-identical in intent to arm C's own `q4k_pair_dot` call, arm E(off) is still 1.30x slower than arm C** -- slower, in fact, than arm E(on)'s deferred-scale ggml-port body. Dispatch geometry is not the answer either: `packed_row_nsg_factor()` (`msl.rs:5677-5688`) keys off `any(metal-packed-row-nsg2, metal-q4k-ggml-port)`, and `metal-packed-row-nsg2` alone (still on in both builds) already forces `nsg=2` -- confirmed identical `threadgroup_width=Some(64)` and `grid_threads` per shape in both dumps. The residual therefore lives OUTSIDE the reduce loop's per-element body and OUTSIDE dispatch geometry: in the per-thread preamble every emitted kernel pays that arm C's hand-written harness does not (the `coord_q_cache` decode, `weight_base`/`other_base` address computation from `u.operand_strides`, the uniform-buffer read path itself) -- ROW 343's own coord_q cache landing already amortizes part of this, but ROW 349 shows a real cost still remains, sized differently for the `plain_product`/`q4k_pair_dot` fallback than for the ggml-port body's own address math.

**This directly conflicts with ROW 316's in-program measurement** (2026-09-05, 3 clean rounds, port ON beat the default body by -6.8% `gpu_exec_ms` in the full decode step) -- ROW 316 found the port HELPS in-program, this row finds turning it OFF makes the same bare-token sequence's arm E get WORSE, not better. Both cannot be read as "the port costs X%" from either measurement alone: ROW 316 compared port-on against production's OWN prior default body (which may not be the `plain_product`/`q4k_pair_dot` fallback this row's port-off build takes -- `omega`'s in-program default body prior to `metal-q4k-ggml-port` landing is not re-confirmed here), while this row compares port-on against the CURRENT fallback on the SAME bare harness. **Per the brief's own stop condition, the oracle A/B (port on vs off, in-program, current `main`, same 3-round discipline ROW 316 used) is the next slice this row identifies, not a flip decided here.**

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) No disassembly/occupancy evidence for WHY the preamble costs more per-thread in one fallback than the other -- this row is a source-level + measured-delta result, not a register-pressure result. (2) 1 round, 7 repeats/arm, no repeat-round CoV cross-check (ROW 344/348's own posture). (3) The Q6K head shape's own port-on/off body swap was not separately isolated -- the 1.526 ms delta is the WHOLE 225-dispatch token's movement, not attributed between the 7 Q4_K FFN families and the 1 Q6K head dispatch.

## ROW 350 -- the wrapper property is the generic N-D coordinate decomposition; removing it for this shape closes 98.7% of the gap

**Card:** test(omega): arm E wrapper rewrite cells + docs(tensor): row 350 the wrapper property behind the emitted-body gap (off `main` at `43cfc59`). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-r350`, `test/bare-wrapper-bisect`.

**Question this row answers.** ROW 349 proved the port-OFF emitted kernel calls the SAME `q4k_pair_dot` arm C's hand-written ladder body calls, yet is 1.302x slower (22.71 ms vs 17.43-17.45 ms) -- a difference ROW 349 located "outside the reduce-loop body and outside dispatch geometry" but did not name. This row names it: a whole-kernel diff of the two texts (`ladder_l3_body.msl`'s `q4k_matvec_l3_shape` vs `r349-logs/emitted_off.msl`'s `omega_reduce_r3_o2_n2_multiply_add_zero`) against every property the brief listed.

**Whole-kernel diff, every difference found:**
1. **Thread-index attributes**: ladder declares 3 (`[[thread_index_in_threadgroup]]`, `[[threadgroup_position_in_grid]]`, `[[threads_per_threadgroup]]`) and derives `simdgroup_index`/`group_first` from them with only power-of-2 divisions (`tid/32u`); the emitted kernel declares 1 (`[[thread_position_in_grid]]`) and derives the same values via `gid/32`/`gid%32`. Numerically equivalent for this dispatch's linear grouping (`gid = tgid*64 + tid`, confirmed identical `threadgroup_width`/`grid_threads` both bodies per ROW 349) -- NOT the source of the gap.
2. **`[[max_total_threads_per_threadgroup(N)]]`**: present in NEITHER kernel's text (`grep` of both `msl.rs` and the ladder test found zero occurrences; `metal.rs:5598` only READS `pipeline.maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup()` post-compile, never sets it). N/A -- not a real difference in this pair.
3. **Uniform buffer address space**: both `constant` (`constant uint64_t& blocks_per_row [[buffer(3)]]` vs `constant Uniforms& u [[buffer(3)]]`). N/A -- not a real difference.
4. **Loop bound / counter signedness**: ladder's `ib`/`q` loops are `uint`, the emitted kernel's are `int`; ladder's bound is `(uint)blocks_per_row` (one runtime scalar), the emitted kernel's is `(int)u.reduction_total / 256` (one runtime division, done ONCE before the loop, not per-iteration). Cell-tested in combination with (5) below; not separable from it in this bisection (see residual).
5. **Per-thread address preamble (the property that matters)**: the emitted kernel computes `weight_base[q]`/`other_base[q]`/the output offset through a GENERIC N-D coordinate decomposition -- `coord_q_cache[q][2] = remaining_q % u.output_extents[1]; remaining_q /= u.output_extents[1]; coord_q_cache[q][0] = remaining_q % u.output_extents[0]; remaining_q /= u.output_extents[0];` -- then multiplies each coordinate by a runtime stride. This machinery is generic over arbitrary rank/strides; for THIS shape the output is rank-2 `[1, rows]` (`production_head_program`'s own `sd->sdv` shape, a 1-token matvec), so `output_extents[0]` is always `1` and `flat < output_extents[1]` always -- every one of the 4 mod/div pairs per `q` (16 division-class GPU instructions per thread total, since `q` runs 0..4) is a PROVABLE no-op that the Metal compiler cannot fold away because `output_extents`/`operand_strides` are runtime uniform-buffer reads, not compile-time constants. The ladder's hand-written kernel never does this: `group_first = simdgroup_index * 4u; row_sums[group_first + q]` is direct single-axis addressing with zero division.

**Cell table (7-repeat bare-token arm, 225 dispatches, `whole_token_matvec_sequence_bare`, `MTLMathMode::Relaxed`, `nsg=2`):**

| Cell | Edit | Arm E ms (median) | CoV | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | none (port OFF, byte-identical to `omega::emit`'s own output) | 22.709 | 0.10% | reproduces ROW 349's 22.707 exactly in a fresh worktree |
| rewrite | [`row350_direct_addressing_rewrite`] replaces the `coord_q_cache` decomposition with `weight_base[q] = u.operand_base[1] + flat * u.operand_strides[1][2]` (same for `other_base`/`out_offset`), applied to the 7 Q4_K family kernels only (Q6K's head kernel does not share this exact wrapper text, 1 of 225 dispatches) | 17.670 | 0.29% | closes 98.7% of the 5.28 ms `22.709 - 17.43` gap |

Arm C (ladder, unaffected either way): 17.43-17.45 ms (ROW 349). Rewrite cell lands 0.24 ms above arm C, inside both arms' own CoV band.

**Mechanism, confirmed by measurement, not assumed.** The 5.28 ms gap ROW 349 located "outside the reduce loop and outside dispatch geometry" is the per-thread cost of decomposing a coordinate that is already known, structurally, to decompose to `(0, flat)` for every thread in this dispatch -- 16 division-class instructions per thread that exist only because the row-blocked reduce emitter (`omega/src/msl.rs`'s `push_packed_row_blocked_body`, the `plain_product`/`else` arm around line 4239) is generic over arbitrary output rank and never special-cases a leading unit extent. Removing that generic path for this shape and using direct single-axis addressing (mathematically identical when `output_extents[0]==1`, which the emitter already KNOWS at bind time from `resolved.extents`) is not a shape-specific hack -- it is a legitimate rank-collapse optimization the emitter could apply to every matvec-shaped reduce, not just this test's.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) Item 4 (signed vs unsigned loop counters, one extra division for `super_blocks`) was never cell-tested in isolation -- the single rewrite cell changes both the coordinate decomposition AND leaves the `int`/`(int)u.reduction_total/256` form untouched, so the 0.24 ms remaining above arm C could contain a real (if small) contribution from that counter-type/loop-bound difference, or could be pure noise (both arms' CoV is 0.1-0.3%, i.e. ~0.02-0.05 ms band, smaller than 0.24 ms -- this residual is NOT fully absorbed by CoV and is left open). (2) 1 round, 7 repeats/arm, no repeat-round cross-check. (3) Q6K's head kernel (1/225 dispatches) was excluded from the rewrite entirely because its wrapper text does not byte-match the Q4K pattern; its own preamble was not separately audited for the same defect. (4) A genuine Cargo feature-graph coupling was found and is NOT this row's subject: `metal-wide-cooperative-reduce`, `metal-plan-stable-buffers`, `metal-packed-row-nsg2`, and `metal-output-placement` are each declared `= ["metal"]`, so none of them can be selected from the CLI without re-pulling the FULL `metal` bundle (including `metal-q4k-ggml-port`) -- there is no way to get a "metal-core + nsg2, port off" build without editing `omega/Cargo.toml`'s `metal` array directly (as ROW 349 and this row both did, transiently).

**Smallest emitter fix for the next slice (not landed here).** `omega/src/msl.rs`'s row-blocked reduce body generator (`push_packed_row_blocked_body`, the `plain_product`/generic `else` arm starting at `msl.rs:4239`, specifically the per-`q` preamble around `msl.rs:4280-4307` that this row's rewrite targeted) should detect, at bind time from `resolved.extents`/`out_layout`, when every axis but one has extent 1 (the matvec/reduce-to-vector shape every one of `production_head_program`'s callers produces) and emit the direct single-axis form instead of the generic `coord_q_cache` decomposition -- generic to every row-blocked reduce, not gated to this test's specific shapes.

**Gates.** `omega/tests/matvec_roofline_ladder.rs` gained [`row350_direct_addressing_rewrite`] + the `ROW350_CELL` knob, shipped default-`0` (inert, byte-identical to `main`'s emitted output) -- `cargo clippy -p omega --tests --features metal,instrument -- -D warnings` clean. The `omega/Cargo.toml` "port off" feature-list edit used to reach the baseline/rewrite cells was reverted before commit (`git diff --stat` against `main` shows only the test file and this docs file).

## ROW 351 -- the emitter now specializes row addressing at bind time; arm E beats the ladder

**Card:** `perf(omega): packed-row rows address directly when the output is one axis` + `docs(tensor): row 351 direct row addressing in the emitter` (off `main` at `a8f5c02`). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-addr`, `perf/packed-row-direct-addressing`.

**The fix, landed default-on, not a knob.** ROW 350 named the smallest emitter fix for the next slice: `push_packed_row_blocked_body`'s row-base preamble (`omega/src/msl.rs`) should detect, at bind time from `resolved.extents`/`output_axes`, when every output axis but one has extent `1` (the decode-matvec shape `production_head_program` always produces) and emit direct single-axis addressing instead of the generic N-D `coord_q_cache` decomposition. This row lands that fix as `packed_row_direct_output_axis` (pure predicate: walks `output_axes`, returns the sole axis with `resolved.extents[axis] > 1`, `None` on zero or more than one) plus `push_packed_row_group_bases` (the ONE preamble helper every row-blocked body variant already shared before this change -- the default/mask-fma `else` arm, `push_q4k_ggml_port_body`, `push_q6k_ggml_port_body` all run this same preamble before branching on which reduce body to render, so one helper edit threads to all three with no per-body copy). When the predicate finds a single axis, the helper hoists `weight_row_stride`/`other_row_stride` once and renders `weight_base[q] = u.operand_base[weight] + flat * weight_row_stride` (same for `other_base`/`coord_q_cache[q][axis] = flat`) -- zero `%`/`/` against `u.output_extents`/`u.operand_strides`. Every other shape (multi-row `M` blocks, more than one non-unit output axis) keeps the exact prior generic form, unchanged text.

**Kernel identity folds the new axis.** `identity.rs`'s `MetalOnlyExtras` gained `packed_row_block_direct_axis: Option<u16>`, rendered as `_da{axis}` (mirroring `cooperative_width`'s own `_w{width}` token) — the axis index, not just a bool, because two bindings sharing rank/`output_axes` but disagreeing on which axis is non-unit bake different literals into the row-base source text and must never share a pipeline-cache entry. `msl.rs::kernel_cache_key` computes it via a new `packed_row_block_direct_axis(resolved, quantized)` (mirrors `packed_row_block_stride_is_one`'s own shape: `None` when no `packed_row_block` match, or the multi-row `token_total > 1` case, else `packed_row_direct_output_axis`).

**Before/after (the `packed_row_blocked_s1_byte_identical` fixture, `packed_row_blocked_s1_q4k.msl`, 512-wide/24-row Q4_K matvec, `rows=4`):** before 643 lines, preamble carried 2 `%` + 2 `/` per `q` against `u.output_extents[0..2]` (rows=4 → 8 mod + 8 div = 16 division-class instructions/thread, exactly ROW 350's count); after 637 lines (-6), preamble carries `weight_row_stride`/`other_row_stride` hoisted once plus 4 straight-line `weight_base[q] = u.operand_base[..] + flat * ..._row_stride` assignments, zero `%`/`/`. Fixture regenerated from `omega::emit`'s own new output (the documented mechanism: the test's `kernel.source` is the ground truth, `include_str!` fixture is the snapshot) — the s=1 fixture text changed as expected; the s>1 multi-row tests (`packed_row_multi_activation_parity`) are unaffected, confirming the generic path still renders for that shape.

**Bare arm E, one round, quiet gate PASSED (names-only pgrep empty, `while true` pgrep empty, load-1 3.72-4.89) immediately before build and again before the timed run:** E (production's own emitted body, direct addressing now default-on) = 16.378 ms median (CoV 0.30%, 246.27 GB/s) vs C (ladder, hand-written) = 17.477 ms median (CoV 0.08%, 230.78 GB/s) -- **E is now 6.3% FASTER than C**, not merely within 3% of it. This beats ROW 350's own post-emit string-rewrite cell (17.670 ms) by a further 1.29 ms: the emitter's hoisted `weight_row_stride`/`other_row_stride` locals (computed once outside the `q` loop) are a strictly smaller edit than the rewrite's own per-`q` inline expression, and the emitter also carries every other already-landed hoist (blk_step/blk_ptr pointer-increment, `other_stride_is_one` stride-free arm) that the standalone rewrite test never combined with this one in the same body before.

**Parity, all default features, quiet run:**
- `cargo nextest run -p omega --features metal -E 'test(byte_identical) or test(q4k) or test(q5k) or test(q6k) or test(q3k) or test(packed_row)'` -- 57 tests run: 57 passed, 154 skipped.
- `cargo nextest run -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument` -- 111 tests run: 111 passed, 32 skipped.
- `cargo nextest run -p proxima-model-interop --features std` (tier check) -- 96 tests run: 96 passed, 25 skipped.
- Decode fixture (`bind::real_openchat_file::runs_the_cached_decode_loop_on_the_metal_backend_and_reports_the_plan_cache`, `--release --features metal,instrument --lib`, `PROXIMA_MAX_TOKENS=8`): `generated_text="Here is a simple Python function that returns"` -- byte-identical to every prior row's own fixture string.
- `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features metal,instrument -- -D warnings` -- clean.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) `push_q4k_single_fetch_body` (the `metal-q4k-single-fetch` default-off arm) is fully self-contained and does NOT route through `push_packed_row_group_bases` -- it never paid the generic decomposition cost in the first place (own doc: "fully self-contained, not routed through the lane-spread preamble"), so this fix does not touch it; not a gap, a pre-existing exclusion this row did not widen. (2) Q6_K's head kernel (ROW 350's own residual item 3) DOES route through the shared preamble (`push_q6k_ggml_port_body` is called after the same `weight_base`/`other_base` setup, unlike ROW 350's post-emit string rewrite which explicitly excluded it for text-pattern reasons) -- this fix reaches it structurally, but no isolated Q6_K-only bare-token cell was measured this row to confirm its own gap closed the same way arm E's whole-sequence number implies. (3) 1 round, 7 repeats/arm; no repeat-round cross-check on this exact build. (4) The `metal-q4k-split-k`/`metal-q4k-mask-fma` non-default arms were not separately re-measured with direct addressing on -- they still call into `push_packed_row_group_bases` (structural, not behind those features), so the byte-identity fixture's own exclusion of those features (unrelated to this change) is unaffected, but no bare-token number exists for that combination.

## ROW 352 -- ROW 351's direct row addressing confirmed on the full decode loop, not just the bare token: -17% `gpu_exec_ms` at every window, output unchanged

**Card:** none (measurement only; ROW 351's `perf(omega): packed-row rows address directly when the output is one axis` already landed on `main` before this row). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-r352`, `docs/row-352-scoreboard`, off `main` at `2a94e30`. Comparison arm built from a second worktree, `proxima-wt-par`, detached at `a8f5c02` (ROW 351's own parent, the last commit carrying the generic `coord_q_cache` preamble in every packed-row body).

**Question this row answers.** ROW 351 measured direct row addressing on the isolated bare-token roofline ladder (arm E, 22.71 ms -> 16.38 ms, the 16 division-class instructions/thread gone). Does the same fix move `gpu_exec_ms`/`step_wall_ms` on the full cached-decode loop (`bind::real_openchat_file`'s own harness, the same one ROW 342/343/345/347 used), and is the 64-token generated text unchanged?

**Method.** Same harness as ROW 342/343/345/347 (`bind::real_openchat_file::runs_the_cached_decode_loop_on_the_metal_backend_and_reports_the_plan_cache`, `--features metal,instrument`, `PROXIMA_MAX_TOKENS=64`, `--exact --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1`). Two release test binaries built `--no-run` from two separate worktrees (`cargo test -p proxima-model-interop --release --features metal,instrument --no-run`): A = `2a94e30` (direct row addressing, ROW 351's own commit), B = `a8f5c02` (ROW 351's parent, generic `coord_q_cache` decomposition). Binaries copied to `r352-logs/oracle-A`/`oracle-B`. 3 rounds interleaved A, B, A, B, A, B.

**Quiet gate.** THREE-check gate (names-only `pgrep -l 'llama-bench|llama-cli|proxima_model_i|device_streamin|matvec_roofline|omega-|^cargo$|^rustc$|nextest|cargo-nextest'`, `pgrep -fl 'while true' | grep -v pgrep`, load-1 < 10), rechecked immediately before every timed invocation. Failed once on load-1 alone (15.78, no matching process) immediately after both release builds finished, cleared after one 30 s wait (load-1 9.64). Held quiet (both pgrep checks empty, load-1 1.96-5.28) through all 6 timed runs and the `llama-bench` denominator run.

**Data -- `gpu_exec_ms` pooled over 3 rounds (15 datapoints at 3..7, 72 at 8..31, 96 at 32..63):**

| arm | steps 3..7 (ms) | steps 8..31 (ms) | steps 32..63 (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A (2a94e30, direct addressing) | mean 21.271, sd 0.105, CoV 0.49% | mean 21.520, sd 0.201, CoV 0.93% | mean 21.666, sd 0.446, CoV 2.06% |
| B (a8f5c02, generic `coord_q_cache`) | mean 25.787, sd 0.229, CoV 0.89% | mean 26.001, sd 0.403, CoV 1.55% | mean 26.213, sd 0.389, CoV 1.48% |

`generated_text` (md5 over the `generated_text=` field alone, isolating it from the per-run `total_wall_clock_ms`/timestamp noise in the same log line) is byte-identical across all 6 runs: `66ee9ae375fad2df739d426b69765563` every time -- `"Here is a simple Python function that returns the nth Fibonacci number using recursion:\n\n\`\`\`python\ndef fibonacci(n):\n    if n <= 0:\n        return \"Invalid input\"\n    elif n == 1:\n        return 0\n    elif..."`, matching ROW 347's own fixture text.

**Result.** A beats B at every window, in every round (12/12 per-round comparisons check out, not shown row-by-row here for space -- see `r352-logs/round{1,2,3}-{A,B}.log`), by margins several multiples of either arm's own CoV: 3..7 A-B = -4.516 ms (-17.51%); 8..31 A-B = -4.481 ms (-17.23%); 32..63 A-B = -4.547 ms (-17.35%). The full-decode-loop win (-17.2 to -17.5%) is smaller in relative terms than ROW 351's own bare-token win (-27.9%, 22.71 -> 16.38 ms isolating just the packed-row matvec), consistent with the fix touching one op family (packed-row matvec) inside a step that also pays attention, KV upload, and dispatch-encode overhead that this fix does not touch.

**`step_wall_ms` corroborates, with the same reproducible step-34 CPU-side outlier ROW 341/347 named.** Pooled step_wall_ms: A 21.978 ms (CoV 0.42%) at 3..7, 22.264 ms (CoV 0.72%) at 8..31, 22.427 ms (CoV 1.74%, step 34 excluded, n=93) at 32..63; B 26.494 ms (CoV 0.78%) at 3..7, 26.769 ms (CoV 1.34%) at 8..31, 26.962 ms (CoV 1.29%, step 34 excluded, n=93) at 32..63. Step 34 spikes reproducibly in all 6 runs (A: 65.29/37.49/37.60 ms; B: 42.58/42.02/41.94 ms, against a ~22/27 ms neighborhood every other step) while `gpu_exec_ms` at step 34 is unremarkable in both arms (21.13-21.17 ms for A, in-band) -- confirming, as ROW 341/347 already established, that the outlier is CPU-side bookkeeping, not kernel cost. Including step 34, pooled 32..63 CoV balloons to 21.00% (A) / 9.79% (B); excluding it, CoV drops to 1.74%/1.29%, consistent with every other window.

**Same-session denominator (`llama-bench -m openchat-3.5-1210.Q4_K_S.gguf -p 0 -n 32 -r 5 -b 2048 -ub 512 -t 8 -o md`, quiet gate empty, load-1 1.96 immediately before):** 56.87 +/- 0.31 t/s (CoV 0.545%) = 17.5847 ms/token.

**Scoreboard.** `step_wall_ms` A at 3..7 = 21.978 ms = **1.2499x llama**; at 32..63 (step-34 excluded) = 22.427 ms = **1.2755x llama**. Per LLAMA-IS-NOT-THE-FLOOR this is a fresh same-session denominator, not a floor claim -- no device-ceiling/bytes-per-token derivation was run this row.

**Owner rule applied.** A (`2a94e30`) is less work: zero `%`/`/` per thread against `u.output_extents`/`u.operand_strides` in the packed-row preamble, versus B's generic N-D decomposition (16 division-class instructions/thread at the fixture's `rows=4`, ROW 350/351's own count). Output is byte-identical over all 64 tokens across both arms and all 3 rounds, and wall is not worse -- it is measurably better at every window, beyond CoV, in every round. **A (direct row addressing, already landed as ROW 351) stays as the default.** This row is confirmatory (the fix landed before this row started), extending ROW 351's bare-token result to the full decode loop.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) The relative win shrinks from -27.9% (bare token, packed-row matvec isolated) to -17.2/-17.5% (full decode step, attention + KV + dispatch overhead included) -- expected given the fix touches one op family inside a step that pays other costs, not independently decomposed into per-op contributions this row. (2) Step 34's CPU-side outlier remains unexplained as a root cause, as it was in ROW 341/347; it reproduces in both A and B, all 3 rounds, at magnitudes that scale with each arm's own baseline (A's spike is larger in absolute ms and in ratio to A's own smaller baseline), which is new information but not a mechanism. (3) No per-round table is shown above (12 individual round x window x arm cells); the pooled means and the byte-identity claim are backed by the 6 raw logs in `r352-logs/`, not transcribed cell-by-cell into this row. (4) This row measures one shape (openchat 3.5, 64-token decode, single prompt) -- no claim is made about longer contexts or other packed-row shapes (multi-row `M` blocks, more than one non-unit output axis) that ROW 351 itself noted keep the generic path unchanged.

**Gates.** Docs-only row confirming an already-landed commit; no functional source change in this row's own diff. `git status --porcelain` in the worktree, before the docs commit, shows only this file's edit.

## ROW 353 -- fast math in the decode oracle: text byte-identical, wall flat, quality gate UNMEASURED (harness never reads the env var) -- NO FLIP

**Card:** none (measurement only). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-r353`, `docs/row-353-fast-math`, off `main` at `19010e8` (ROW 352's own commit; base sha confirmed identical to `r352-logs/oracle-A`, so that release binary was reused rather than rebuilt).

**Question this row answers.** `PROXIMA_MATH_MODE=fast` (`MathMode::Fast`, `proxima-model-interop/src/test_support.rs`'s `math_mode_from_env`) is selectable at the `bind.rs` test edge (`math_mode_from_env` called at `bind.rs:3666`/`4432`, default `relaxed` on unset/unparseable). Does flipping the decode-loop oracle from `relaxed` to `fast` change the 64-token output, move `gpu_exec_ms`/`step_wall_ms`, and hold quality within ROW 316's `R` baseline (exact >= 0.906, kl_max <= 0.048)?

**Method.** Same harness as ROW 342/343/345/347/352 (`bind::real_openchat_file::runs_the_cached_decode_loop_on_the_metal_backend_and_reports_the_plan_cache`, `PROXIMA_MAX_TOKENS=64`, `--ignored --nocapture --test-threads 1`), against `r352-logs/oracle-A` (release binary built at `19010e8`, reused unmodified since `git rev-parse --short main` == `19010e8` in this worktree too). Six cells, interleaved R, F, R, F, R, F (`PROXIMA_MATH_MODE=relaxed|fast`), logs at `r353-logs/round{1,2,3}-{R,F}.log`.

**Quality gate: UNMEASURED, not "held" -- traced to a real gap in the harness, not skipped.** `PROXIMA_MATH_MODE`/`math_mode_from_env` is read at exactly two call sites, both in `bind.rs` (`bind.rs:3666`, `bind.rs:4432`); `grep -rn math_mode proxima-model-interop/src/*.rs` shows the quality harness's own path never touches it. `quality::tests::metal_vs_cpu_reports_real_drift` (`quality.rs:826`) calls `quality_report` (`quality.rs:353`) -> `score_prompt` (`quality.rs:238`) -> `supported_serving_config` (`generate.rs:1397`), which builds every `ServingConfig` as `..ServingConfig::default()` (`generate.rs:1406`), and `ServingConfig::default`'s own body hardcodes `math_mode: MathMode::Relaxed` unconditionally (`serving.rs:221`). Reporting those numbers as an "F" quality score would be a fabricated measurement (principle 18: a DERIVED/assumed number may never stand in for a mechanism); this row declines to run it rather than misreport it, and instead states the gap: plumbing `math_mode` into `quality_report`'s config requires either a public-signature change (`quality_report` is `pub fn`, consumed by 3 test sites including `q3_k_m_variant_against_q4_k_s_reference_reports_real_drift`) or a parallel test-only config-builder in `quality.rs`'s own `mod tests` -- neither is a same-row fix inside a 30-minute measurement budget without risking an unreviewed API change.

Quality within baseline -- UNMEASURED (mechanism proven above: the harness structurally cannot exercise Fast math without a source change). The owner rule requires ALL THREE to hold before flipping the default; one is unmeasured, so **NO FLIP**. `MathMode::Fast` is not made the default plan value in `omega/src/metal.rs` this row.

## ROW 354 -- nsg sweep of the emitted body bare, on the new direct-addressing kernel: nsg8 beats the production nsg2 default by 1.70%, past the noise bar

**Card:** none (measurement only, test-file addition). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-r354`, `perf/row-354-nsg-sweep`, off `main` at `4b3a91f` (ROW 351's direct-addressing fix, ROW 353's docs row).

**Question this row answers.** ROW 351 rewrote `push_packed_row_group_bases` to emit direct single-axis row addressing, dropping arm E (production's own emitted body) from 22.71 ms to 16.38 ms. That sweep never revisited `nsg` (`omega::sized::PACKED_ROW_NSG`, `metal-packed-row-nsg2`/`metal-q4k-ggml-port`'s shared width) itself -- the production default of 2 simdgroups/threadgroup was chosen by ROW 296/302's sweep against the OLD generic-decomposition preamble. With the preamble gone, is nsg=2 still the best cell for the emitted body, bare?

**Method.** `whole_token_matvec_sequence_bare` (`omega/tests/matvec_roofline_ladder.rs`) already builds arm E from `production_reduce_kernel` -- production's real `infer`/`bind`/`correct_packed_matmul_layouts`/`omega::emit` path, whose `nsg` is the build-time constant `PACKED_ROW_NSG` (`omega/build.rs`, overridable per-build via `OMEGA_PACKED_ROW_NSG_WIDTH` without touching `omega-runtime.toml`, `require_power_of_two_le_32`-checked). Two test-file changes, both additive and default-inert: (1) `ROW354_EMITTED_ONLY=1` skips arms A-D's hand-written-kernel loop so each sweep cell times only arm E's 225-dispatch sequence, not five; (2) arm E's own log line now names its actual compiled `PACKED_ROW_NSG` (`arm=E_production_emitted_body_nsg{N}_relaxed`) instead of a hardcoded `nsg2`, so a build's own output self-documents which cell it ran. Four separate `cargo test -p omega --release --features metal,instrument --test matvec_roofline_ladder -- --ignored --nocapture whole_token_matvec_sequence_bare` invocations, each with a distinct `OMEGA_PACKED_ROW_NSG_WIDTH` (1, 2, 4, 8) forcing a fresh `build.rs` run (env-var-changed rerun, not a feature toggle), warm-up + median-of-7 every cell, same reporting (ms/CoV/GB/s) `whole_token_matvec_sequence_bare` already emits.

**Quiet gate.** THREE-check gate (names-only `pgrep -l 'llama-bench|llama-cli|proxima_model_i|device_streamin|matvec_roofline|omega-|^cargo$|^rustc$|nextest|cargo-nextest'`, `pgrep -fl 'while true' | grep -v pgrep`, load-1 < 10) run once before setup (both pgrep empty, load-1 1.63), and again before each of the 4 timed cells (one 30s retry cleared load-1 each of the 3 times it briefly cleared 10 between back-to-back builds -- all self-inflicted by this brief's own prior build, no foreign process observed either pgrep pattern at any check).

**Data (1 round, 7 repeats/cell, this session, same host):**

| nsg | median_ms | min_ms | max_ms | CoV % | median GB/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 17.660 | 17.647 | 17.708 | 0.11 | 228.39 |
| 2 (production default) | 15.845 | 15.788 | 15.890 | 0.21 | 254.55 |
| 4 | 15.651 | 15.604 | 16.175 | 1.49 | 257.71 |
| 8 | **15.576** | 15.549 | 15.608 | 0.11 | **258.95** |

**Result.** nsg=1 is a clear loser (17.660 ms, +11.4% vs nsg=2) -- one simdgroup/threadgroup under-occupies every packed-row dispatch this shape takes, consistent with why `metal-packed-row-nsg2` landed default-on in the first place (ROW 311). nsg=4 sits 1.22% faster than nsg=2 (15.651 vs 15.845), but that delta is smaller than 2x the two cells' combined CoV (sqrt(0.21^2+1.49^2)=1.50%, 2x=3.01%) -- nsg=4's own 1.49% CoV (one of its 7 samples, 16.175 ms, is a visible outlier the other 6 do not share) swallows the signal; **not distinguishable from noise**. nsg=8 sits 1.70% faster than nsg=2 (15.576 vs 15.845 ms) with a tight 0.11% CoV matching nsg=2's own tightness -- combined CoV is sqrt(0.21^2+0.11^2)=0.24%, so 2x=0.47%, and the observed 1.70% delta is **more than 3x past that bar**, a real, CoV-exceeding win, not noise. nsg=8 also beats ROW 351's own reported E figure (16.378 ms, a prior session, different box state) by 4.9% -- consistent direction, though that comparison crosses sessions and is not the load-bearing one here (the in-session nsg=2 vs nsg=8 comparison is).

**nsg=8 is the next oracle A/B candidate**, not a landed change: this row is bare, single-shape-family, single-round, and never checked with production's real hazard tracker/plan cache/arena in the loop (ROW 339's own reason arms A-E exist at all -- the in-program number can differ from the bare one, as ROW 344 -> ROW 352 already showed for the direct-addressing fix itself). The production default (`omega-runtime.toml`'s `[packed_row_nsg] width = 2`) is **not changed in this slice**.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) One round, 7 repeats/cell -- no repeat-round cross-check confirming nsg=8's win holds session-to-session the way ROW 351/352's two-stage bare-then-in-program confirmation did. (2) nsg=4's single 16.175 ms outlier (vs its own other 6 samples clustered 15.60-15.74 ms) is unexplained -- could be a transient scheduling hit from this brief's own back-to-back builds sharing the box, not investigated further under the 30-minute budget. (3) No in-program (real hazard tracker/plan cache/decode loop) measurement of nsg=8 -- ROW 352's own confirmation pattern for the direct-addressing fix (bare win -> in-program win, same direction, -17% `gpu_exec_ms`) has not been run for nsg here; the bare win could compress or invert once dispatch overlap/barriers are back in the loop. (4) Only the whole-token FFN family shapes + one Q6_K head were exercised (this test's own fixed shape set) -- no claim extends to other row/k combinations. (5) `metal-q4k-split-k` (which overrides `packed_row_nsg_factor` to 1 regardless of `PACKED_ROW_NSG` -- `msl.rs:5769-5786`) was not compiled in for any cell; this sweep is scoped to the default `metal-packed-row-nsg2`/`metal-q4k-ggml-port` path only.

## ROW 355 -- ROW 354's bare nsg8 win does not survive the full decode loop: gpu_exec beats nsg2 in direction but not past the noise bar -- NO FLIP

**Card:** none (measurement only). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-r355`, `docs/row-355-nsg8-oracle`, off `main` at `9bb97c2` (ROW 354's own commit). Comparison arm built from a second worktree, `proxima-wt-n8`, detached at `9bb97c2` with `OMEGA_PACKED_ROW_NSG_WIDTH=8` forcing a fresh `build.rs` run.

**Question this row answers.** ROW 354 swept `PACKED_ROW_NSG` on the bare, isolated `whole_token_matvec_sequence_bare` roofline ladder and found nsg=8 beating production's nsg=2 default by 1.70%, past a 0.47% 2xCoV bar, naming nsg=8 "the next oracle A/B candidate". Does that bare-kernel win carry into the full cached-decode loop (`bind::real_openchat_file`'s own harness, the same one ROW 342/343/345/347/352/353 used), the way ROW 351's direct-row-addressing fix did in ROW 352?

**Method.** Same harness as ROW 342/343/345/347/352/353 (`bind::real_openchat_file::runs_the_cached_decode_loop_on_the_metal_backend_and_reports_the_plan_cache`, `--features metal,instrument`, `PROXIMA_MAX_TOKENS=64`, `--exact --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1`). `git diff --stat 19010e8 main -- omega/src proxima-model-interop/src proxima-tensor/src omega/omega-runtime.toml omega/build.rs` is empty, so oracle A is ROW 352's own already-built release binary (`r352-logs/oracle-A`, `2a94e30`/nsg2, reused unmodified rather than rebuilt), copied to `r355-logs/oracle-A`. Oracle B is a fresh `cargo test -p proxima-model-interop --release --features metal,instrument --no-run` from `proxima-wt-n8` (`9bb97c2`) with `OMEGA_PACKED_ROW_NSG_WIDTH=8` on the build command; B's own `resolve_int`/`SizingSource` mechanism (`proxima-build/src/sizing.rs`, `OMEGA_packed_row_nsg_width` override naming) picked up the env var (confirmed by a different md5 than A despite an identical binary size, and a distinct, successful build log). Binaries copied to `r355-logs/oracle-A`/`oracle-B`. 3 rounds interleaved A, B, A, B, A, B.

**Quiet gate.** THREE-check gate (names-only `pgrep -l 'llama-bench|llama-cli|proxima_model_i|device_streamin|matvec_roofline|omega-|^cargo$|^rustc$|nextest|cargo-nextest'`, `pgrep -fl 'while true' | grep -v pgrep`, load-1 < 10) run once before setup (both pgrep empty, load-1 5.74), and once before the timed runs: load-1 alone briefly failed (14.68, no matching process, self-inflicted by this brief's own just-finished release build), cleared after one 30s wait (8.96). Held quiet (both pgrep checks empty) through all 6 timed runs; no foreign process observed either pattern at either check.

**Data -- pooled over 3 rounds (15 datapoints at 3..7, 72 at 8..31, 96 at 32..63; `step_wall_ms` 32..63 excludes the reproducible step-34 CPU-side outlier ROW 341/347/352 already named, n=93 of 96):**

| arm | gpu_exec 3..7 (ms) | gpu_exec 8..31 (ms) | gpu_exec 32..63 (ms) | wall 3..7 (ms) | wall 8..31 (ms) | wall 32..63 excl. step34 (ms) |

| B (nsg8) | mean 20.5375, CoV 1.62% | mean 21.1962, CoV 2.21% | mean 21.2848, CoV 1.65% | mean 21.3285, CoV 1.28% | mean 21.9577, CoV 1.91% | mean 22.0456, CoV 1.44% |

`generated_text` (md5 over the `generated_text=` field alone) is byte-identical across all 6 runs, both arms: `ca0c632379ab85cc6205a837f2b32300` -- no divergent token to name.

**Result -- NO FLIP.** The rule this row applies (nsg8 is the same work -- same bytes, same dispatches -- so it flips only if text identical AND `gpu_exec_ms` is better beyond 2x combined CoV at BOTH 3..7 and 32..63): text identity holds (6/6 byte-identical), but the `gpu_exec_ms` delta clears neither required window. At 3..7: B beats A by 2.54% (21.0724 -> 20.5375 ms), combined CoV = sqrt(1.73^2+1.62^2) = 2.37%, 2x bar = 4.74% -- the 2.54% delta is inside the bar, not past it. At 32..63: B beats A by 1.75% (21.6629 -> 21.2848 ms), combined CoV = sqrt(1.59^2+1.65^2) = 2.29%, 2x bar = 4.58% -- again inside the bar. (At 8..31, shown for completeness though not part of the flip rule: B beats A by 0.69%, combined CoV 3.04%, 2x bar 6.07% -- also inside.) `step_wall_ms` shows the same pattern, direction-consistent with `gpu_exec_ms` at every window (B faster by 2.27%/0.74%/1.62% at 3..7/8..31/32..63 excl. step 34) but likewise inside its own combined-CoV bars. B is directionally faster in all 6 window x metric cells, in every round (not shown round-by-round here for space -- see `r355-logs/round{1,2,3}-{A,B}.log`), but the full decode loop's own noise floor (CoV 1.28-2.21% here) is roughly an order of magnitude noisier than ROW 354's bare-kernel isolation (CoV 0.11-0.21% for the nsg2/nsg8 cells there), and that added noise swallows a delta that was real in isolation.

**Why the gap between bare (1.70%, past bar) and in-program (2.54% at best, inside bar).** Same mechanism ROW 352 already named for the direct-addressing fix: the bare ladder isolates exactly the packed-row matvec dispatches nsg controls, with nothing else running, so a small per-dispatch win reads clean. The full decode step also pays attention, KV upload, dispatch-encode, and CPU-side bookkeeping (`prepare_ms`, `pipeline_compile_ms`, block-upload accounting) that nsg does not touch and that vary step-to-step independent of the kernel change -- inflating both arms' CoV from ~0.1-0.2% (bare) to ~1.6-2.2% (in-program) and burying a delta of the same absolute order (a few tenths of a ms) that the bare test could still resolve.

**Owner rule applied.** Text identical -- YES (measured, 6/6 runs). `gpu_exec_ms` better beyond 2x combined CoV at both 3..7 and 32..63 -- NO at either window (2.54% vs 4.74% bar; 1.75% vs 4.58% bar). Per this row's own stated rule, both conditions are required to flip; the second fails at both windows. **`[packed_row_nsg] width = 2` stays the production default.** `omega/omega-runtime.toml` is not changed this row.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) B is directionally faster at every window and metric across all 3 rounds, a consistent signal the noise bar (correctly) treats as unproven rather than as absent -- a higher-round-count rerun (5-10 rounds instead of 3) would narrow the CoV and could still resolve the direction into a real, sub-bar win; not run here under the 30-minute budget. (2) No per-dispatch profile isolates how much of the in-program step's own CoV (1.6-2.2%) is attention/KV/CPU-bookkeeping variance vs packed-row matvec variance itself -- the mechanism paragraph above is a plausibility argument from ROW 352's precedent, not a decomposed measurement. (3) Only the whole-token FFN family + openchat 3.5's fixed shape/prompt were exercised (this harness's own fixed shape set); no claim extends to other shapes. (4) `metal-q4k-split-k` (overrides `packed_row_nsg_factor` to 1 regardless of `PACKED_ROW_NSG`, per ROW 354's own residual) was not compiled in for either arm.

## ROW 357 -- Metal System Trace of one token: the ~5ms gap between program (21.07ms) and bare (15.85ms) is invisible below encoder granularity -- one MTLComputeCommandEncoder per command buffer means Instruments cannot resolve any of the ~225 packed-row dispatches individually

**Card:** none (measurement only, discovery row). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-r357`, `docs/row-357-metal-trace`, off `main` at `988df34` (ROW 356's own commit). No source change to kernels or driver: `git diff --stat 19010e8 main -- omega/src proxima-tensor/src` is empty (the only diff in that range is `proxima-model-interop/src/{bind,generate,quality}.rs`, interop-only, unrelated to the Metal encode path).

**Question this row answers.** ROW 355 (arm A, production nsg2) measured `gpu_exec_ms` 21.07ms mean at steps 3..7 in the full decode loop; ROW 354 measured the same ~225 packed-row dispatches bare (isolated, nothing else running) at 15.85ms. Where does the program spend the extra ~5ms? Prior rows (309, 329) tried to hand-build sampling for this; this row uses the platform profiler instead, per the U3 brief.

**Method.** `xcrun xctrace record --template 'Metal System Trace' --launch -- <oracle> bind::real_openchat_file::runs_the_cached_decode_loop_on_the_metal_backend_and_reports_the_plan_cache --exact --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1` with `PROXIMA_MAX_TOKENS=8`. Binary: `r352-logs/oracle-A` (sha `19010e8`, ROW 352's build, nsg2/production, reused unmodified). One recording, `r357-logs/token.trace`. Exported via `xcrun xctrace export --input token.trace --toc` to enumerate tables, then `--xpath '/trace-toc/run[@number="1"]/data/table[@schema="..."]'` per candidate schema, parsed with `xmllint --format` + `awk`/`grep` (no python). Tables tried: `metal-gpu-intervals`, `metal-application-encoders-list`, `metal-application-command-buffer-submissions`, `metal-gpu-execution-points`, `metal-application-intervals`, `metal-shader-profiler-intervals`, `metal-shader-profiler-shader-list`, `metal-driver-intervals`.

**Finding 0 (governs all four asks): the trace has no per-dispatch resolution for this workload.** `metal-application-command-buffer-submissions` narrates, verbatim, `Committed "Command Buffer 0" with 1 encoders` for every one of the 8 command buffers in the run -- our driver batches all ~520 `encode_dispatch_calls` (per the in-app `token_breakdown_metal` line) into a single `MTLComputeCommandEncoder` before commit. Instruments' GPU timeline (`metal-gpu-intervals`, `metal-gpu-execution-points`, `metal-driver-intervals`) attributes GPU execution at encoder granularity only: each of those tables shows exactly one "GPU Execution" / "Command Buffer 0:Compute Command 0" row per command buffer for `oracle-A (47474)`, with no child rows or event-depth >0 entries underneath. `metal-shader-profiler-intervals` (the one schema that would carry per-dispatch, per-PSO timing via GPU hardware counters) exported its schema with **zero `<row>` elements** -- GPU counter sampling was not active in this capture (Metal System Trace's default template does not enable it; that is a separate recording mode). `metal-shader-profiler-shader-list` has rows, but they are one-time pipeline-compile/load events near t=1.07s (warmup), not per-invocation dispatch records -- 1177 rows total, none tied to steady-state steps 3..7.

**(1) Command buffer's GPU span vs sum of dispatch durations.** GPU span is measurable (below); the sum of dispatch durations is not -- there is no per-dispatch row to sum, per Finding 0. The 8 command buffers' `metal-gpu-intervals` "Duration" (GPU Execution span): buffer 0 (prefill+compile, warmup) 10.79s; buffer 1 (first post-warmup decode step, transient) 28.07ms; buffers 2-6 (steady state) 20.58ms, 20.64ms, 20.72ms, 20.78ms, 20.84ms -- mean 20.71ms, directionally consistent with ROW 355 arm A's pooled 21.07ms (single run here, not pooled over rounds, so the ~0.36ms difference is expected run-to-run noise, not a new finding). CPU-side "Encoder Time" (`metal-application-command-buffer-submissions`, time to populate the encoder before commit) for those same 5 buffers: 715.88us, 730.21us, 725.42us, 724.12us, 710.33us (~0.72ms) -- an order of magnitude smaller than the ~5ms gap and already inside the step, not additive to it.

**(2) Dispatch count and inter-dispatch gap distribution.** Not obtainable. Per Finding 0, no table exposes individual dispatch start/end times inside the single encoder; there is exactly one interval per command buffer, so a gap distribution across ~225 (or ~520 total op-setup) dispatches cannot be computed from this trace. `metal-gpu-execution-points` (248 rows total, 2 per encoder = start+end marker) confirmed this is a start/end pair at the *encoder* level, not per-dispatch.

**(3) Ten longest dispatches with kernel names, including the Q6_K head.** Not obtainable for the same reason -- no per-dispatch row carries a kernel/PSO name paired with a duration for steady-state steps. `metal-shader-profiler-shader-list` names individual kernels (e.g. `omega_constant_r0_v39800000`, `omega_iota_r1`, and by extension the packed-row-matvec and Q6_K head kernels) but only as one-time compile events at load time, with no execution duration or per-step recurrence -- it answers "which kernels exist" not "how long did kernel X run at step 5".

**(4) Total non-matvec dispatch time and its share of the span.** Not obtainable, same reason: no per-dispatch attribution exists to split attention/norm/elementwise/rope/softmax time from packed-row-matvec time within the single-encoder span.

**Named mechanism for the ~5ms.** None of the four candidates (dispatch gaps, non-matvec dispatch time, slower-than-bare matvec dispatches, the head) can be *named* from this evidence -- the trace cannot see inside the encoder to distinguish them. What the trace DOES establish: the encoder-level GPU span it reports (20.6-20.8ms steady state) matches the in-app `gpu_exec_ms` instrumentation ROW 355 already trusted (21.07ms pooled), so this row is a **cross-check that confirms the existing measurement, not a new decomposition of it**. The residual ~5ms remains exactly where ROWs 309/329 left it: inside one opaque encoder. Resolving it mechanically requires either (a) a capture mode with GPU hardware counter sampling enabled (a different Instruments recording configuration, `metal-shader-profiler-intervals` populated instead of empty), or (b) the app itself inserting `MTLCounterSampleBuffer` boundaries around dispatch groups (which changes the encode pattern and would need its own before/after perf check), or (c) splitting the single encoder into multiple encoders/command buffers per token so Instruments' existing per-encoder granularity becomes per-dispatch-group granularity (also a driver change, also perf-sensitive). None of those is a docs-only measurement; each is its own card.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) Single run, 8 tokens, no pooling/CoV -- this row is a discovery of the tool's resolution floor, not a statistically-backed number; the GPU-span figures above are illustrative cross-checks against ROW 355's pooled numbers, not a replacement for them. (2) GPU counter-sampling capture mode was not attempted (out of the 30-minute budget for this row) -- unmeasured whether it would even attach cleanly to a `cargo test` binary or require the `gguf_generate` example instead; the brief's fallback (`--attach` by name, or `examples/gguf_generate`) was not needed because `--launch` against the test binary worked directly and produced a complete recording. (3) `metal-driver-event-intervals`, `metal-driver-event-per-thread-intervals`, `metal-object-dependency-chain-*`, and `metal-gpu-counter-intervals`/`metal-gpu-counter-profile` schemas were listed in the toc but not exported -- plausible by name to carry finer detail, not checked here.

**Gates.** Docs-only row; no functional source change. `git status --porcelain` in the worktree, before this commit, shows only this file's edit and the untracked `r357-logs/` review directory (`token.trace` plus the exported/parsed XML).

**Card:** none (source fix + measurement). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-r356`, `fix/quality-math-mode`, off `main` at `8f796ce` (ROW 355's own commit).

**Defect fixed (ROW 353's own residual (4)).** `quality::real_openchat_file::metal_vs_cpu_reports_real_drift` (`quality.rs:826`) -> `quality_report` (`quality.rs:353`) -> `score_prompt` (`quality.rs:238`) -> `supported_serving_config` (`generate.rs:1397`) built every `ServingConfig` as `..ServingConfig::default()` with no `math_mode` field of its own, and `ServingConfig::default`'s body hardcodes `math_mode: MathMode::Relaxed` (`serving.rs:221`) -- so `PROXIMA_MATH_MODE=fast` (read by `math_mode_from_env`, `test_support.rs:14`, otherwise only consumed at `bind.rs:3666`/`4432`) silently measured Relaxed regardless of what was asked for. `quality_report` never took a math mode at all.

**Fix.** `math_mode: omega::MathMode` threaded as a `#[cfg(all(feature = "metal", target_os = "macos"))]`-gated parameter (mirroring the field's own gate on `ServingConfig`, since `omega::MathMode` itself is only re-exported under that same `cfg` in `omega/src/lib.rs`) through `supported_serving_config` (`generate.rs:1405`) -> `score_prompt` (`quality.rs`, both `reference_config`/`variant_config` use the SAME mode) -> `quality_report` (`quality.rs:368`). Every non-quality caller of `supported_serving_config` (`LoadedModel::generate` at `generate.rs:2013`, `forward_node_values_on_backend` at `generate.rs:3161`, and `bind.rs`'s own `real_openchat_file` CPU decode-loop setup at `bind.rs:3604`) passes `omega::MathMode::default()` at the call site, so their behavior is unchanged -- only `quality_report`'s three `real_openchat_file` test call sites now read `math_mode_from_env()` at the test edge, the same function `bind.rs:3666`/`4432` already use. No new type: `omega::MathMode` (already `omega`'s own public surface) is the only type in the diff, and the `#[cfg]`-on-parameter/argument mechanism used to gate it (verified to compile: a bare `rustc` smoke test with a `#[cfg]`-gated parameter and a `#[cfg]`-gated call argument) is standard Rust, not a wrapper. A regression test (`generate.rs`, `supported_serving_config_tests::threads_the_requested_math_mode_into_the_serving_config`, `cfg(all(test, feature = "metal", target_os = "macos"))`) asserts `supported_serving_config(0, Safe).math_mode == Safe` and `..Fast).math_mode == Fast` structurally, since the end-to-end quality numbers below turn out identical between Relaxed and Fast on this kernel/checkpoint and would not, by themselves, distinguish "the fix works and Fast==Relaxed here" from "the fix silently no-ops."

**Diff.** `proxima-model-interop/src/generate.rs` (+61/-8): `supported_serving_config`'s new parameter, its 2 non-quality call-site updates, the new regression test module. `proxima-model-interop/src/quality.rs` (+69/-10): `score_prompt`/`quality_report` new parameter and threading, 3 `real_openchat_file` test call sites now passing `math_mode_from_env()`. `proxima-model-interop/src/bind.rs` (+6/-1): the one remaining `supported_serving_config` call site's new argument. Commit `d1ae033`, `fix(interop): quality harness takes the math mode`.

The regression test above proves the plumbing itself is live (`Safe`/`Fast` produce distinct `ServingConfig.math_mode` values through the exact same call path), so the R/F identity here is read as that documented per-kernel property reproducing on openchat-3.5's decode path, not as evidence the fix is a no-op.

**Rule applied (owner's: F is within baseline iff `exact >= R.exact` AND `kl_max <= 2 * R.kl_max`).** `exact`: 0.906250 >= 0.906250 -- HOLDS (equal). `kl_max`: 0.026294 <= 0.052588 (2x R) -- HOLDS (equal). **F WOULD HAVE QUALIFIED** on this 8x8 sample. Per the brief, this row does NOT flip `ServingConfig::default`'s `math_mode` away from `Relaxed` -- ROW 353 already found no wall-clock signal for Fast on this same decode path, so there is no benefit to trade the now-provably-safe quality result against; this row only closes ROW 353's own gap and records what Fast's quality gate would have shown.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) R and F being bit-identical, not just "within baseline," means this sample cannot distinguish Fast from Relaxed at all on this checkpoint/kernel path -- the rule is satisfied trivially, not by a close call, so "F qualifies" is weaker evidence than a close-but-passing measurement would be. (2) Only one checkpoint (Q4_K_S openchat-3.5), one 8x8 sample, one kernel family (whatever `metal-q4k-ggml-port` compiles by default on this main) were exercised; no claim extends past this shape, consistent with every prior quality row's own residual. (3) `math_mode`'s effect on `DispatchType`-adjacent kernels or non-default feature combinations (`metal-packed-row-nsg2`, `metal-q4k-ggml-port` held off, etc.) was not swept -- ROW 296/297's own measured bandwidth gap between `Safe`/`Relaxed` (179 vs 240-247 GB/s) shows the modes DO diverge on some kernels; this row only proves quality parity on the one path openchat-3.5's default decode actually exercises.

## ROW 358 -- kind-filter ablation cannot isolate the packed-row matvec kind through this harness (prefill has zero of it); the three ablatable kinds close only half of ROW 357's ~5ms gap

**Card:** none (measurement only, docs-only row). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-r358`, `docs/row-358-kind-ablation`, off `main` at `d5b741e` (ROW 357's own commit).

**Question this row answers.** ROW 357's Metal System Trace could not resolve the ~5ms gap between the in-program `gpu_exec_ms` (21.07ms, ROW 355 pooled) and the bare packed-row-matvec-only sequence (15.85ms, ROW 354) below encoder granularity -- one `MTLComputeCommandEncoder` per command buffer. `PROXIMA_METAL_KIND_FILTER` (`omega/src/metal.rs:1771-1795`, `ablation_skip`, instrument builds only, vocabulary at `omega/src/metal.rs:1459-1470`) can skip dispatches by kind from inside the program instead. Which kind carries how much of that gap, and does the per-kind decomposition close against FULL?

**Method.** Same harness as ROW 342/354/355 (`bind::real_openchat_file::runs_the_cached_decode_loop_on_the_metal_backend_and_reports_the_plan_cache`, `--features metal,instrument`, `PROXIMA_MAX_TOKENS=8`, `--exact --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1`). `git diff --stat 19010e8 main -- omega/src proxima-tensor/src` is empty, so ROW 352/355/357's own `r352-logs/oracle-A` (`19010e8`, nsg2/production) is reused unmodified -- confirmed still an `instrument` build by running it with a bogus kind (`PROXIMA_METAL_KIND_FILTER='!bogus_kind_xyz'`), which errors `Metal(UnknownKindFilterTerm { term: "bogus_kind_xyz" })` rather than silently ignoring it (a non-instrument build has no `KindFilter` parsing at all). One release binary, one round per cell (FULL, `!cached_attention`, `!elementwise`, `!reduce-cooperative`, `!iota`, `!reduce-packed-row-blocked`), 8 tokens, `gpu_exec_ms` at steps 3..7. Dispatch counts per kind read from the plan itself via the existing `PROXIMA_METAL_OP_PROFILE_STEP=3` diagnostic (`generate.rs:186`, `report_op_timings`/`op_profile_bucket`), which runs `evaluate_op_timed` (per-op command buffers) for exactly one step and prints an exhaustive `op_count`/`gpu_ms` table keyed by `classify_kind`'s own bucket -- the count is asserted from this table, not inferred from a flag.

**Quiet gate.** THREE-check gate (names-only `pgrep -l 'llama-bench|llama-cli|proxima_model_i|device_streamin|matvec_roofline|omega-|^cargo$|^rustc$|nextest|cargo-nextest'`, `pgrep -fl 'while true' | grep -v pgrep`, load-1 < 10) run once before the 6 timed cells (both pgrep empty, load-1 1.87) -- PASSED, no retry needed. Re-checked after the timed runs and again before the docs commit (both pgrep empty, load-1 2.38).

**`!reduce-packed-row-blocked` is infeasible through this harness -- not a text-degeneration case, a hard `Result::Err` before any decode step runs.** The run panics immediately (`finished in 0.12s`, no `token_breakdown` line ever printed) with `Metal(KindFilterMatchesNothing { filter: "!reduce-packed-row-blocked" })`. `validate_kind_filter` (`metal.rs:1543-1567`) runs on EVERY call to `execute_plan_with_placements`, including the harness's own PREFILL call (`new_count=31`, the first token) before any of steps 3..7 are reached, and rejects a filter that removes 0 or all of that call's own `prepared.resolved` ops. The prefill step batches 31 tokens through the SAME weight matrices the single-token decode steps use, but `classify_kind`'s `Reduce{keep:Reduce}` arm (`metal.rs:2993-3040`) checks the emitted kernel body's source markers, checking `"reduce-tiled-gemm"` (the `simdgroup_multiply_accumulate` marker) BEFORE `"reduce-packed-row-blocked"` (the `acc1_0`/`q4k_run8`/etc. markers) -- a batched matmul emits the tiled-gemm body, not the packed-row-blocked one, so prefill's own op population contains zero ops of the kind this cell asks to remove, independent of the fact that steps 3..7 (single-token decode) contain 224 of them. This is a real, load-bearing finding about the tool, not a workaround-needing bug: the filter is validated per-call against that call's own plan population, and prefill and decode steps populate different kind buckets for the identical weight set.

**Dispatch count per kind, FULL, step=3 (`PROXIMA_METAL_OP_PROFILE_STEP=3`, `op_profile_bucket` lines, `r358-logs/op-profile-step3.log`):**

| kind | op_count | bare gpu_ms (op-timed mode, not comparable to the ablation ms column below) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cached_attention | 32 | 1.699 |
| constant | 2 | 0.008 |
| elementwise | 194 | 2.040 |
| iota | 2 | 0.008 |
| reduce-cooperative | 66 | 1.150 |
| reduce-packed-row-blocked | 224 | 18.229 |
| **total** | **520** | **23.133** |

Counts sum to `op_count=520`, matching the total the FULL/ablated logs' own `op_setup_calls=520` (or the reduced count after a kind is skipped) already report. **The Q6_K output head classifies as `reduce-cooperative`, not `reduce-packed-row-blocked`** (`op_profile_top` rank=1: `node=2586 kind=reduce-cooperative weight_name=Some("output.weight")`) -- the brief's assumption that `!<packed-row matvec kind>` would include the head does not hold on this plan; the head's kernel body ends in `simd_sum(` (the cooperative-reduce marker) rather than the packed-row-blocked body's own markers, per `classify_kind`'s own precedence.

**Data -- one round, 8 tokens, `gpu_exec_ms` at steps 3..7:**

| cell | steps 3..7 (5 values, ms) | mean (ms) | FULL − cell (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FULL (no filter) | 20.536, 20.561, 20.579, 20.547, 20.503 | 20.5452 | -- |
| `!cached_attention` | 19.485, 19.516, 19.589, 19.614, 19.052 | 19.4512 | **+1.0940** |
| `!elementwise` | 19.519, 20.117, 20.035, 20.081, 20.295 | 20.0092 | **+0.5360** |
| `!reduce-cooperative` | 19.731, 19.875, 19.773, 19.844, 19.867 | 19.8181 | **+0.7271** |
| `!iota` | 21.552, 21.645, 21.758, 21.810, 21.638 | 21.6807 | **-1.1355** |
| `!reduce-packed-row-blocked` | infeasible (see above) | -- | -- |

**Closure check -- does NOT close.** Summing the three kinds with a real, positive, above-noise delta (`cached_attention` 1.094 + `elementwise` 0.536 + `reduce-cooperative` 0.727 = **2.357 ms**) against ROW 357's own named gap (FULL 21.07ms pooled, ROW 355, minus bare 15.85ms, ROW 354, = **4.70ms**, and this row's own single-round FULL of 20.545ms minus bare = **4.70ms** also, coincidentally near-identical): the three ablatable non-matvec kinds account for barely half (2.357 / 4.70 = **50.1%**) of the gap. `!iota`'s -1.1355ms delta is noise, not a real cost -- `iota` is 2 ops at 0.008ms bare (op-timed table above), so a -1.14ms swing from removing it is two to three orders of magnitude larger than its own bare cost and is this row's own single-round, single-sample variance (no repeat rounds were budgeted; ROW 355's in-program CoV for `gpu_exec_ms` is 1.3-2.2% per round, i.e. roughly +/-0.27-0.45ms at this mean, which does not by itself explain a 1.14ms swing either -- named, not resolved, under this row's 30-minute budget). `constant` (2 ops, 0.008ms bare) was not separately ablated -- its own bare cost is negligible by the same op-timed measurement.

**The residual, ~2.34-2.35ms (4.70 - 2.357), is the term the brief asked to name and this row's method cannot independently attribute to the packed-row matvec kind** -- `!reduce-packed-row-blocked` could not be run (see infeasibility finding above), so there is no ablation-based measurement of "matvecs slower in program" to set against ROW 354's bare 15.85ms. A DERIVED estimate (FULL 20.545 minus the three real per-kind deltas minus iota's own bare 0.008ms = **18.180ms** implied packed-row-blocked in-program cost, vs ROW 354's bare 15.85ms = **+2.33ms/+14.7%** implied slowdown) is arithmetically consistent with the residual by construction (it IS the residual, relabeled) and is NOT independent evidence -- it is reported as DERIVED, not MEASURED, per principle 18, and should not be read as a second confirmation of the same number.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) The packed-row matvec kind's own in-program cost is UNMEASURED by this row's method -- the one ablation that would isolate it directly (`!reduce-packed-row-blocked`) cannot run through this harness because prefill's own plan population contains none of that kind (see the infeasibility finding); a fresh row would need either a harness that can skip prefill's own `validate_kind_filter` call (a source change, not attempted here) or a different isolation method entirely. (2) Single round, single 8-token run per cell -- no CoV, no repeat-round check; `!iota`'s -1.14ms delta is flagged as noise but not independently re-run to confirm. (3) Whether the ~2.34ms residual is barrier/hazard overhead between kind-adjacent dispatches that no single-kind ablation removes (the brief's own named hypothesis), CPU-side bookkeeping variance step-to-step (ROW 355's own named source for the full loop's higher CoV vs the bare ladder's), or packed-row-blocked dispatches genuinely running slower in-program than bare, is NOT decided by this row -- all three remain open. (4) `constant`'s 2 ops (0.008ms bare) were not separately ablated; folded into the "no further real cost" reading by inspection of its own bare `gpu_ms`, not by a dedicated ablation cell.

## ROW 359 -- llama's own perf harness exposes exactly one of our eight decode shapes; on that shape llama's bare kernel beats ours 1.55x, and llama's full-token bare-matvec sum is UNMEASURED, not ~0 or ~13-14ms

**Card:** none (measurement only, docs-only row). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-r359`, `docs/row-359-llama-bare`, off `main` at `256f8a4` (ROW 358's own commit). No source change in proxima; nothing in `/Users/brianbruggeman/repos/others/llama.cpp` modified (confirmed: only invocations of already-built binaries, no edits, no rebuild).

**Question this row answers.** ROW 352's llama-bench denominator (17.58 ms/token) minus our own bare packed-row-matvec sequence (ROW 354, 15.85 ms) minus our full in-program token (ROW 355/358, 20.55-21.07 ms) leaves us ~4.70 ms of in-program overhead over our own bare kernels. Is llama paying a comparable structural tax (bare sum ~13-14 ms, implying the gap is shared program overhead), or does llama's bare matvec sum already account for nearly its whole token (~17 ms, implying our 4.70 ms is a structural defect specific to our own program)?

**Method.** `test-backend-ops perf -b Metal -o MUL_MAT -p <regex>` (binary at `/Users/brianbruggeman/repos/others/llama.cpp/build/bin/test-backend-ops` -- `build_mac/bin` holds only Metal shader headers, not the binary; `build/bin` is the real build tree, confirmed by `find`). Real per-tensor quant types read from the openchat-3.5-1210.Q4_K_S.gguf header (`llama-gguf <path> r n`) by matching each tensor's reported byte size against `elements * block_bytes / block_size` for each candidate quant (Q4_K = 144/256 B/elem, Q5_K = 176/256, Q6_K = 210/256) -- NOT assumed from the brief's own hedge that some may be Q5_K/Q6_K in a `_S` quant:

| shape | m (rows) | k (cols) | byte size | bytes/elem | **actual type** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| attn_q | 4096 | 4096 | 9,437,184 | 0.5625 | **Q4_K** |
| attn_k | 1024 | 4096 | 2,359,296 | 0.5625 | **Q4_K** |
| attn_v | 1024 | 4096 | 2,883,584 | 0.6875 | **Q5_K** (not Q4_K) |
| attn_output | 4096 | 4096 | 9,437,184 | 0.5625 | **Q4_K** |
| ffn_gate | 14336 | 4096 | 33,030,144 | 0.5625 | **Q4_K** |
| ffn_up | 14336 | 4096 | 33,030,144 | 0.5625 | **Q4_K** |
| ffn_down | 4096 | 14336 | 40,370,176 | 0.6875 | **Q5_K** (not Q4_K) |
| output head | 32000 | 4096 | 107,526,720 | 0.8203 | **Q6_K** |

`attn_v` and `ffn_down` are Q5_K, not Q4_K as the brief's default assumption had it -- this Q4_K_S quant mixes attention-value and ffn-down projections at higher precision than the rest, matching llama.cpp's own known `Q4_K_S` mixing rule for `.attn_v.` / `.ffn_down.` tensors (not re-derived here, just observed from the byte sizes).

**Reading `make_test_cases_perf` (`tests/test-backend-ops.cpp:4603-4664`) before spending an invocation on a shape it cannot run.** The only MUL_MAT case at real-model scale is `tests/test-backend-ops.cpp:4628-4634`: `m=4096, k=14336, n in {1,2,3,4,5,8,512}`, swept over every quant type in `all_types`. No other case in this function uses `k=4096`, `m=1024`, `m=14336`, or `m=32000` -- the perf-mode CLI (`-p <params regex>` filters `make_test_cases_perf`'s own fixed list, it does not accept arbitrary shapes, confirmed by reading `filter_test_cases` at `test-backend-ops.cpp:4666-4682`) has **no path to attn_q/attn_k/attn_v/attn_output/ffn_gate/ffn_up/head's shapes without editing the source**, which this row does not do. The one case it does have is an **exact match** (not merely "nearest") for `ffn_down`'s own shape (`m=4096, k=14336`).

**Quiet gate.** THREE-check gate (names-only `pgrep -l 'llama-bench|llama-cli|proxima_model_i|device_streamin|matvec_roofline|omega-|^cargo$|^rustc$|nextest|cargo-nextest'`, `pgrep -fl 'while true' | grep -v pgrep`, load-1 < 10) run before both timed invocations: both pgrep empty, load-1 3.10 before the `test-backend-ops` sweep, load-1 2.78 before `llama-bench`. No retry needed.

**Invocation 1/2 -- `test-backend-ops perf -b Metal -o MUL_MAT -p 'type_b=f32,m=4096,n=1,k=14336'`, one round each type (`r359-logs/perf-all-types-m4096-k14336.log`):**

| type_a | us/run | GFLOPS | derived GB/s (weight bytes / time) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| q4_K | 104.53 | 1120 | 315.9 |
| q5_K (**ffn_down's real type**) | 144.48 | 812.84 | 279.4 |
| q6_K | 213.43 | 550.25 | 189.2 |

**Invocation 2/2 -- `llama-bench -m openchat-3.5-1210.Q4_K_S.gguf -p 0 -n 32 -r 5 -b 2048 -ub 512 -t 8 -ngl 99 -o md` (`r359-logs/llama-bench-n32.log`, same-session denominator):** 57.22 +/- 0.68 t/s (CoV 1.19%) = **17.4764 ms/token**.

**The one directly comparable shape -- llama's bare kernel beats ours 1.55x.** Ours (ROW 336, `ffn_down_q5k` arm, median 180.08 GB/s, weight bytes 40,370,176, DERIVED us/run = bytes / GB/s = 224.17 us) vs llama's MEASURED 144.48 us/run at the identical shape and type (Q5_K, m=4096, k=14336, n=1): **llama's ffn_down bare kernel is 1.55x faster than ours on this one shape.** This is the only per-shape apples-to-apples comparison this row's tool can produce.

**Full per-shape table -- ours (DERIVED from ROW 336's GB/s x this row's byte sizes) vs llama (MEASURED where the tool has the shape, UNMEASURED elsewhere):**

| shape | type | ours us/run (DERIVED, ROW 336 GB/s) | llama us/run (MEASURED) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| attn_q | Q4_K | 77.09 | UNMEASURED (no `k=4096` case in `make_test_cases_perf`) |
| attn_k | Q4_K | 24.86 | UNMEASURED |
| attn_v | Q5_K | 29.99 | UNMEASURED |
| attn_output | Q4_K | 72.06 | UNMEASURED |
| ffn_gate | Q4_K | 179.71 | UNMEASURED (no `m=14336,k=4096` case) |
| ffn_up | Q4_K | 176.72 | UNMEASURED |
| ffn_down | Q5_K | 224.17 | **144.48 (MEASURED)** |
| head | Q6_K | 463.53 | UNMEASURED (no `m=32000` case) |
| **per-layer sum (7 shapes)** | -- | **784.60** | UNMEASURED |
| **x32 layers + head** | -- | **25,107.2 + 463.5 = 25,570.7 us = 25.571 ms** | UNMEASURED |

**Answer to this row's own question: UNMEASURED, not ~0 and not ~13-14ms.** llama's full bare-matvec-token sum cannot be computed from this tool -- 6 of 7 per-layer shapes plus the head have no matching case in `make_test_cases_perf`, and this row does not edit llama.cpp to add one (out of scope, explicitly disallowed). The brief's own framing ("if llama's bare sum is ~17ms its overhead is ~0; if ~13-14ms, the gap is in the kernels") presumed all eight shapes were reachable through `-p`; reading the source first (guiding-principles principle 6) shows only one is. This row reports the one shape it CAN measure rather than extrapolating the other seven from it (a DERIVED extrapolation across shapes of very different `m`/`k` ratios would not be a measurement of llama's kernels, it would be a guess wearing a number).

**A second, unplanned residual: our own DERIVED per-shape sum (25.571 ms) does not match our own MEASURED whole-token bare sequence (ROW 354, 15.845 ms).** Summing ROW 336's isolated per-shape arms overshoots ROW 354's directly-measured, single-sequence bare token by 9.7 ms (61%) -- the isolated-arm ladder (one shape run alone, its own command buffer/dispatch setup, `run_shape_arm`'s own fixed per-arm cost per ROW 336's own text) does not compose additively into the real packed sequence's cost, where all ~225 dispatches for all shapes across all 32 layers share one execute-plan call and one command-buffer-commit cadence. This is a mechanism gap this row surfaces, not one it resolves: it means neither this row's own DERIVED per-shape "ours" column, nor a hypothetical llama per-shape sum built the same way, would be a trustworthy proxy for either program's real bare-token cost -- ROW 354's own directly-measured 15.845 ms remains the only number in this document that MEASURES our whole-token bare kernel time, and there is no llama equivalent measurable through `test-backend-ops`' CLI (llama-bench measures the full in-program token, 17.4764 ms, not a bare-kernel-only number).

**What the one comparable shape says about where our gap is.** On `ffn_down` -- the only shape both programs can be measured on with the same tool-adjacent method -- llama's bare kernel (144.48 us) beats ours (224.17 us, DERIVED) by 1.55x. If that ratio held across all seven per-layer shapes (an assumption, not evidence -- `ffn_down`'s K=14336 read pattern differs from the K=4096 attention/ffn-gate/ffn-up shapes and from the head's M=32000 pattern), it would place a meaningful part of the residual gap in the **kernels themselves**, not purely in program structure -- consistent with, not contradicting, ROW 358's own finding that only half (2.357/4.70 ms) of our full-token in-program overhead traces to non-matvec dispatch kinds (attention/elementwise/reduce-cooperative), leaving the other half attributed to the packed-row matvec kind itself (ROW 358's own DERIVED 18.180 ms implied in-program packed-row-blocked cost vs its own 15.85 ms bare figure). Both rows point the same direction -- kernel-level cost, not just program overhead -- but neither is a full per-shape decomposition on both sides, so this reads as a **plausible, not proven**, direction for the residual.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) llama's own per-layer bare matvec sum is UNMEASURED for 6 of 8 shapes -- this row's central question is answered "cannot be computed with this tool," not with a number, and no extrapolation from the one measured shape is reported as if it were. (2) The `ffn_down` 1.55x llama-over-ours comparison is one shape, one round, no CoV -- `test-backend-ops`' own perf mode reports a single number per invocation with no repeat-count control exposed via CLI in this build; a multi-round rerun was not budgeted. (3) The 25.571 ms vs 15.845 ms internal inconsistency in our own numbers (previous paragraph) is reported and not resolved -- closing it (does `run_shape_arm`'s isolation add fixed per-arm cost, or does the real packed sequence share dispatch/barrier cost across shapes that the isolated arms each pay alone) is its own future row. (4) `ours` us/run figures in the main table are DERIVED (bytes / ROW 336's GB/s), not independently timed this row -- they inherit ROW 336's own residuals (attn_k/attn_v/attn_v_q5k sit lowest, a per-dispatch fixed-cost floor at small tensor size, per ROW 336's own text). (5) No GPU-hardware-counter or per-dispatch decomposition of llama's own `ffn_down` 144.48 us was attempted -- it is reported as a single opaque bare-kernel number, the same granularity ROW 354 reports for ours.

**Gates.** Docs-only row; no functional source change in proxima, no modification to llama.cpp. `git status --porcelain` in the worktree, before this commit, shows only this file's edit and the untracked `r359-logs/` review directory.
