`ours us/run` is DERIVED from `ours GB/s` (the harness's own MEASURED median) and this row's own MEASURED byte sizes (`us = bytes / (GB/s * 1000)`), same convention ROW 359 used for its one comparable shape; `ours GB/s` itself is a first-class MEASUREMENT this row adds (ROW 336's own numbers, pre-direct-addressing, are not reused anywhere in this table).

**Sum x32 layers + head, both programs:**

- llama: per-layer sum (7 shapes) = 446.49 us; x32 + head = 446.49*32 + 387.47 = 14,675.15 us = **14.6752 ms**.
- ours: per-layer sum (7 shapes) = 688.72 us; x32 + head = 688.72*32 + 454.74 = 22,493.62 us = **22.4936 ms**.

**Overheads.**
- llama: full-token denominator (ROW 359, llama-bench) 17.4764 ms − bare per-shape sum 14.6752 ms = **2.8013 ms overhead** (structural: KV-cache indexing, RoPE, softmax, sampling, and every non-matvec dispatch around the 8 bare kernels).
- ours: full in-program token (ROW 355/358) 20.55 ms − bare per-shape sum 22.4936 ms = **−1.9436 ms** -- NEGATIVE. Our isolated per-shape sum exceeds our own real whole-token time. This is not a measurement error in either number (both are independently MEASURED elsewhere: ROW 355/358's 20.55 ms is the real in-program token, this row's 22.494 ms is eight independently-isolated bare-kernel arms) -- it means isolated single-shape dispatch pays a per-arm fixed cost (own command buffer, own `execute_plan` call, no sharing with a neighboring dispatch) that the real packed sequence, which shares one execute-plan call and one command-buffer-commit cadence across all ~225 dispatches (ROW 359's own note), does not pay per shape. An "overhead" number computed this way is not meaningful for our program; it is reported as the direct answer to the brief's own question, together with why it is negative, rather than silently reframed to look positive.
- Against ROW 354's own MEASURED whole-token bare-kernel sequence (15.845 ms, a single shared-dispatch run, not eight isolated ones): this row's per-shape sum (22.494 ms) overshoots it by **6.649 ms (42.0%)**. **This is smaller than ROW 359's own 61% overshoot on the same comparison** (25.571 ms vs 15.845 ms, DERIVED from stale ROW 336 numbers) -- consistent with direct addressing (landed after ROW 336, before this row) closing part of the isolated-arm gap, but the sum still does NOT compose additively into the real packed-sequence number. The mechanism ROW 359 named (isolated dispatch cost != shared-sequence dispatch cost) still holds; direct addressing improved the per-arm kernel body, not the isolation-vs-sharing gap itself.

**Where the gap is, per shape, and what the bytes say about the ceiling.** Device ceiling (ROW 296) is 381.24 GB/s. llama's own GB/s sits in a comparatively narrow, high band across every shape size (187-319 GB/s, 49-84% of ceiling) -- even its smallest tensors (`attn_k`/`attn_v`, ~2.4-2.9 MB) hold 187-197 GB/s. Ours spans a much wider, lower band (103-236 GB/s, 27-62% of ceiling), and the width tracks tensor size directly: the four SMALLEST-tensor shapes (`attn_q`/`attn_k`/`attn_v`/`attn_output`, 2.4-9.4 MB) are where the ratio is WORST (1.76x-1.91x, `attn_v` worst at 1.91x) and where our own GB/s (103-159) is furthest below llama's (187-280) -- both programs pay a per-dispatch fixed cost on small tensors, but ours is proportionally larger. The four LARGEST-tensor shapes (`ffn_gate`/`ffn_up`/`ffn_down`/`head`, 33-108 MB) are where the ratio is BEST (1.17x-1.58x, `head` best at 1.17x) -- transfer time dominates over per-dispatch overhead for both programs at this size, so the gap narrows toward parity. This reads as a per-dispatch fixed-cost gap concentrated at small tensor sizes, not a uniform per-byte throughput gap -- consistent with, and sharpening, ROW 359's single-shape (`ffn_down`, mid-size, 1.40x here vs its own 1.55x with slightly different rounding) finding into a size-dependent pattern across all eight shapes.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) The negative "our overhead" number above is the headline residual of this row: isolated per-shape sums cannot answer "what fraction of our real token is non-matvec overhead" the way llama's positive 2.80 ms answer can, because our own isolation methodology inflates the denominator past the real token. Closing this (measuring bare per-shape cost WITHOUT isolating each shape into its own dispatch/command-buffer, i.e. inside the real shared-sequence harness ROW 354 already runs) is the direct next-row question this one surfaces but does not answer. (2) One round per llama shape (no CoV, `test-backend-ops`' own limitation, same as ROW 359); one full run per our-side shape (CoV 0.86-7.15% across arms, `attn_output` highest at 7.15%, still under this file's own 10% ROW-335 threshold for 6/10 arms historically, here 7/8 of the shapes this row uses are under 10%). (3) `attn_v`/`ffn_down` each have two real codec variants in this checkpoint (Q4_K and Q5_K); this row uses the REAL-codec arm (`attn_v_q5k`, `ffn_down_q5k`) for both, matching the byte sizes ROW 359 read from the gguf header, and does not report the Q4_K variant of either (available in the same log, not part of this checkpoint's real mix). (4) No hardware-counter or per-dispatch decomposition of either program's kernels was attempted this row -- both sides are reported at the same opaque bare-kernel granularity ROW 354/359 already use.

**Gates.** Docs-only row; harness (`omega/tests/matvec_roofline_ladder.rs`) unchanged (all eight shapes already covered by `DECODE_SHAPES`), so no clippy/nextest gate applies per this brief's own instruction ("only if the harness changed"). `git status --porcelain` in this worktree, before this commit, shows only this file's edit and the untracked `r360-logs/` review directory.

## ROW 361 -- correction to ROW 360's framing: `decode_shape_roofline_ladder` already batches one shape's dispatches into a single command buffer; the real difference this row measures is bare llama-style encoding vs production's `plan`/`execute_plan` machinery, plus a device-side GPU-time split and a same-tensor-repeat control

**Card:** none (measurement only, docs-only row). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-r361`, `perf/row-361-amortized`, off `main` at `8976b63` (ROW 360's own commit).

**Correction to this row's own original brief (owner review, verified against source before any cell ran).** The brief's premise -- that ROW 360's "ours" column is an isolated, one-dispatch-per-command-buffer measurement, unlike llama's own `n_runs`-duplicated-into-one-graph number -- is WRONG. `decode_shape_roofline_ladder`'s own kernel path, `omega::metal::execute_plan`, opens ONE command buffer before its op loop and `endEncoding()`s once after every op (`omega/src/metal.rs:912-924`), the SAME batching discipline llama's `test-backend-ops` uses (`tests/test-backend-ops.cpp:675-677`, duplicating the op into one graph; `:704`, one `ggml_backend_graph_compute` call). ROW 360's 42% per-shape-sum overshoot against ROW 354's whole-token bare measurement is therefore NOT a one-dispatch-per-buffer artifact. What ROW 360's own timer (`run_shape_arm`'s wall bracket around `execute_plan`, `omega/tests/matvec_roofline_ladder.rs:1994`) DOES conflate is host-side preparation and output readback (`finish`, called after `waitUntilCompleted` inside `execute_plan`, `omega/src/metal.rs:1030`) together with device execution time, with no separate device-side reading. This row does not use the phrase "amortized for the first time" anywhere below -- that framing from this row's own original brief is retracted.

**What this row actually measures.** Three things, each additive to `omega/tests/matvec_roofline_ladder.rs`'s `whole_token_matvec_sequence_bare` (`ROW361_FAMILY=<name>` restricts its 225-dispatch, one-command-buffer construction to ONE family, `ROW361_SAME_TENSOR=1` swaps distinct per-layer tensors for one tensor repeated): (1) the SAME bare, hand-encoded construction (no plan cache, no hazard tracker, no uniform arena) arm E already uses for the real 225-dispatch token, restricted to one family, so the number is directly comparable to that whole-token construction rather than to `decode_shape_roofline_ladder`'s `plan`/`execute_plan` path; (2) a device-side GPU-time reading (`command_buffer.GPUEndTime() - command_buffer.GPUStartTime()`, `omega::metal`'s own pattern at `omega/src/metal.rs:2144-2145`) beside the wall bracket, so host-encode/submit share is visible; (3) a same-tensor-repeat control for the two shapes where a working-set difference from llama's own harness could plausibly matter -- `test-backend-ops` duplicates the SAME tensor reference `n_runs` times into one graph (`tests/test-backend-ops.cpp:674`), so its small shapes (2.4-9 MB) may be served from SLC on every repeat, while this ladder's default synthesizes `dispatch_count` DISTINCT tensors per cell (`synth_weight_bytes_parallel`'s own per-tensor `Lcg` seed).

**Six cells (owner-corrected set, replacing this row's original six): `attn_k` distinct, `attn_k` same-tensor, `ffn_gate` distinct, `ffn_gate` same-tensor, `ffn_down` distinct (`Q5_K`), `head` (`Q6_K`)** -- `attn_q` dropped (same shape/codec as `attn_output`, already in ROW 360) and `attn_v` dropped to make room for the two same-tensor cells within the six-cell cap. Warm-up + median-of-7 each, `--release --features metal,instrument`, nsg2/relaxed (production's compiled default). Quiet gate: names-only pgrep empty, `while true` pgrep empty; load-1 19.97 -> one 30s retry (this row's own allowance) -> 13.48, still above the file's usual <10 bar but with zero contending measurement processes on the names-only/`while true` checks -- proceeded, noting the elevated background load rather than silently treating it as quiet.

**Ratio (ours-gpu / llama), and what moved vs ROW 360's own ratio (which used `decode_shape_roofline_ladder`'s `plan`/`execute_plan` path, not this row's bare arm-E-style path):**

- `attn_k` distinct: 21.50/12.60 = **1.71x** (ROW 360: 1.77x -- nearly unchanged; consistent with this row's own correction that ROW 360's path was ALREADY batched into one command buffer, so switching construction style should not, and did not, move this ratio much).
- `attn_k` same-tensor: 33.49/12.60 = **2.66x** -- WORSE than distinct, not better. The SLC-residency hypothesis this cell was built to test is NOT supported by this measurement: repeating the SAME synthesized tensor 32 times measured SLOWER (33.49 us/dispatch, CoV 9.94%, seven samples tightly clustered) than 32 distinct tensors (21.50 us/dispatch, CoV 24.77%). Read plainly, not reframed: on this host, for this shape, same-tensor repetition does not reproduce llama's own construction's advantage, and ROW 360's small-shape ratio is NOT shown to be a benchmark-mismatch artifact by this cell -- it stands as measured.
- `ffn_gate` distinct: 112.74/103.45 = **1.09x** (ROW 360's `plan`/`execute_plan`-path ratio for this shape was 1.58x/1.48x, `ffn_gate`/`ffn_up`). The bare bare-encoded construction is markedly closer to llama than `decode_shape_roofline_ladder`'s own production-path (`plan`/`execute_plan`, hazard tracker, uniform arena, plan cache) number for the SAME shape -- a real, measured difference between the two dispatch mechanisms this repo ships, not noise (CoV 13.76%, ratio delta far exceeds it).
- `ffn_gate` same-tensor: 107.66/103.45 = **1.04x**, closest to parity of any cell -- a small (~4.5%) same-tensor benefit here, opposite in direction from `attn_k`'s. A 33 MB tensor is unlikely to fit any Apple Silicon SLC tier the way a 2.3 MB `attn_k` tensor does, so if this delta is SLC-driven at all it would have to work through a different mechanism (allocator/paging locality, not SLC residency) -- unmeasured, named as a residual, not asserted.
- `ffn_down` distinct: 174.13/143.88 = **1.21x** (ROW 360's `plan`-path ratio: 1.40x) -- narrower with the bare construction, same direction as `ffn_gate`.
- `head`: 1173.63/387.47 = **3.03x** (ROW 360's `plan`-path ratio: 1.17x) -- dramatically WORSE with the bare construction. `head` has `dispatch_count=1`; no amortization is possible at N=1 regardless of construction, so this cell reproduces an isolated single dispatch either way -- the finding is that the BARE hand-encoded single-dispatch path (`setComputePipelineState` + four `setBuffer_offset_atIndex` calls, no plan cache, `time_bare_dispatch_sequence`'s own per-op cost) is measurably more expensive for this one huge dispatch than `decode_shape_roofline_ladder`'s `plan`/`execute_plan` path is for the same shape. llama's own `n_runs` for `head` could not be re-read from the saved log (teardown-clobbered), so llama's own amortization depth for this shape is unverified by this row.

**Wall vs GPU split (host-encode/submit-and-wait share of the wall bracket, per cell):** `attn_k` distinct 24% of wall time is outside the GPU-time window (28.24 vs 21.50 us/dispatch); `attn_k` same-tensor 20%; `ffn_gate` distinct 6.5%; `ffn_gate` same-tensor 6.7%; `ffn_down` distinct 4.6%; `head` 17.3%. The two small-tensor cells (`attn_k`, `head`) carry the largest host/GPU-boundary share, consistent with a per-dispatch or per-command-buffer fixed CPU-side cost (ROW 289's own ~0.5 ms empty-dispatch finding) that a small payload cannot dilute -- the same mechanism ROW 360 already named for isolated arms, now visible as a wall-minus-GPU delta rather than inferred from an isolated/shared contrast.

## ROW 362 -- attention chunk sizing oracle: `keys_per_chunk` 64 -> 16 clears its 2x-combined-CoV bar on the earliest decode window, not on the two longer ones, with byte-identical output text across every arm

**Card:** none (a single-line config tweak, `omega/omega-runtime.toml:217`, `ab4433e`). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-r362`, `docs/row-362-attn-chunks`, one commit ahead of `main` at `4b09ec5` (ROW 361's own commit).

**What changed and why it is a build-time constant, not a runtime read.** `[attention_context_chunks]` in `omega/omega-runtime.toml` feeds `omega/build.rs:281-292`'s `ATTENTION_CONTEXT_KEYS_PER_CHUNK` / `ATTENTION_CONTEXT_CHUNK_CAP` generated constants (per principle 12: build-time-tunable, no magic numbers, `OMEGA_ATTENTION_CONTEXT_CHUNKS_KEYS_PER_CHUNK` / `_CAP` env overrides). `context_chunks_for` (`omega/src/msl.rs:2956-2960`) is `context_length.div_ceil(KEYS_PER_CHUNK).clamp(1, CHUNK_CAP)`, called at bind time from the same static `cached_key_rows + new_key_rows` fields the kernel already bakes as `constexpr` (`msl.rs:2950-2955`'s own doc comment) -- never a runtime read, so this is a per-build shape decision: A = `keys_per_chunk=64` (`main`'s prior value), B = `keys_per_chunk=16` (this row's candidate), `cap=4` unchanged in both (`omega/omega-runtime.toml:218`).

**Build evidence that oracle-A and oracle-B are genuinely distinct binaries** (`r362-logs/oracle-A`, `r362-logs/oracle-B`, same 3,865,616-byte size): `cmp` finds the first byte divergence at offset 217 (`cmp oracle-A oracle-B` -> `differ: char 217, line 3`); `md5(oracle-A)=60621baa55a30635522fd4a59b06300d`, `md5(oracle-B)=1ee3b01df1dc465012a8c9769eb910fb` -- two independently-linked artifacts, not one binary reused across arms. `omega-runtime.toml:217` at B's checkout reads `keys_per_chunk = 16`.

**Partitioning explanation, corrected (owner finding, post-ROW-366).** This row originally derived a per-step chunk count from `cached_len_before`/`new_count` read out of the round logs (34, 38, 39, 62, 63 across the three windows below) and asserted those values fed `context_chunks_for` directly. That is wrong: ROW 366 (`discipline.md:25904`) traces `context_chunks_for`'s actual input to a static bind-time field, `cached_key_rows + new_key_rows`, which the (buggy, pre-ROW-366) merged-KV bind duplicated to `2 * bucketed_capacity` regardless of the live per-step context -- at this row's own decode fixture that bucketed capacity was 39, so the compiled `context_length` `context_chunks_for` actually saw was `39 + 39 = 78`, not the growing 34-63 range this row read from the log's own `cached_len_before`/`new_count` fields. The correct partitioning derivation for this row's own timed arms is therefore from that recorded historical binding, not a new measurement: `keys_per_chunk` 64 -> 16 at `context_length = 78` is `div_ceil(78, 64) = 2` chunks (A) -> `clamp(div_ceil(78, 16), 1, 4) = 4` chunks (B) -- not the per-step `3`/`4` split this row originally derived from the log's `cached_len_before`/`new_count` fields. The timing observations and the table below are unchanged; only the partitioning explanation for what those timings measured is corrected here. ROW 366 has since fixed the underlying bind-time duplication bug: post-fix, this same fixture's live 39-key context correctly resolves to `ceil(39/16) = 3` chunks, not this row's `4`.

**Three decode windows, `gpu_exec_ms` and `step_wall_ms`, mean +/- CoV across all 3 A/B rounds combined** (`r362-logs/round{1,2,3}-{A,B}.steps.tsv`, recomputed directly with `awk` over `token_breakdown`/`token_breakdown_metal` log lines, not taken from the prior agent's summary):

The chunk-sizing change does not alter the greedy-decoded token sequence at any of the three windows measured.

**Flip decision: FLIPPED.** The change clears its bar on the earliest decode window (3..7, -4.9%, byte-identical text) and is directionally consistent (never worse) on the other two, which fail only the noise bar, not the sign. `keys_per_chunk=16` (this row's `B`) is kept as `main`'s value; `omega/omega-runtime.toml:217` already carries it (`ab4433e`).

**Interop gate, capped** (thermal rule: `-j 2` on nextest already sets `--test-threads 2` in this nextest version -- `-j`/`--test-threads` are the same flag, aliased as `jobs`; passing both is a CLI error, not two independent knobs): `cargo nextest run -j 2 -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument` -> `r362-logs/nextest-interop-final.log` -> **112 tests run: 112 passed, 32 skipped** (0 failed). The 32 skipped are the `#[ignore]`d real-GGUF fixtures (`bind::real_openchat_file::*`), which is where the six timed A/B round logs and their identical `generated_text` above are already the evidence for "the decode fixture reproduces byte-identical text," separately captured before this gate ran.

**Host-loadout note.** The previous agent's own uncapped interop nextest invocation (no `-j`, default parallelism) ran 7 real-model debug processes concurrently and was killed mid-run by SIGTERM after 75s of thermal contention (`r362-logs/nextest-interop.log`: "SIGTERM [ 75.695s] proxima-model-interop bind::real_openchat_file::..." repeated across four tests, `Summary [ 75.713s] 11/14 tests run: ... 7 failed`). That overheating event happened AFTER the timed A/B rounds this row's table is built from -- `round1-3-{A,B}.log` and their `.steps.tsv` derivatives were produced under the passing, capped three-check gate, not the run that later overheated the box. No `load-1`/`pgrep` quiet-gate lines are present inside the round logs themselves (those are the model's own stdout, not the shell harness), so this row cites the failed nextest log as the after-the-fact overheat evidence rather than a load figure captured during the timed cells.

## ROW 363 -- numeric policy: a typed permission ladder gates every bit-changing rewrite at bind/plan time, and `ServingConfig` declares it explicitly; behavior-preserving at the shipped default (`ReassociationPermitted`), byte-identical decode text and gpu_exec at parity across two A/B rounds

**Card:** none. **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-policy`, `feat/numeric-policy`, rebased onto `main` at `bb90cac` (ROW 362 plus the RoPE-construction-sharing refactor), landed as `004d25e` (top commit after one correction commit this row adds).

**What changed and why it is a RISC primitive, not a bag of per-rewrite flags.** `proxima_tensor::numeric` (`proxima-tensor/src/numeric.rs:1-99`) adds `NumericPolicy` -- a `#[non_exhaustive]`, `Ord`-derived total order `BitExact < FusedNoReassociation < ReassociationPermitted < FastMath` (`NumericPolicy::default()` is `BitExact`, the most conservative rung: `numeric.rs:22-29`) -- and `NumericRewrite`, one variant per rewrite class this crate or a GPU backend applies that changes which float bits come out (`IdentityElimination`/`ChainFusion`/`ReduceEpilogueFusion` at `BitExact`, `FmaContraction` at `FusedNoReassociation`, `TreeReduce`/`ContextChunkMerge`/`DequantScaleFactoring` at `ReassociationPermitted`, `FastMathApprox` at `FastMath`; `NumericRewrite::minimum_level`, `numeric.rs:66-80`). `admit(policy, rewrite)` (`numeric.rs:89-99`) is the one gate every rewrite site calls: `Err(TensorError::NumericPolicyTooStrict { rewrite, minimum, granted })` when `policy < rewrite.minimum_level()`, `Ok(())` otherwise -- a typed error at bind/plan time, never a silent numerics change and never a second parallel boolean check per rewrite (`op.rs`'s `is_associative` had exactly one caller before this row, `numeric.rs`'s own module doc). This is the RISC answer to "should this fusion/reassociation fire": one enum, one order, one admission function, reused by every future bit-changing rewrite rather than a per-rewrite `bool` flag threaded through every call site that wants to gate it.

**Where it binds today: the attention context-chunk merge.** `omega::msl::context_chunks_for(context_length, policy)` (`omega/src/msl.rs:2978-2985`) now takes the policy: `admit(policy, NumericRewrite::ContextChunkMerge).is_err()` falls back to `1` (the single-pass kernel `render_cached_attention` already renders for `chunks<=1`) rather than failing the plan, the same "reject/fallback at bind time" shape `fuse_cached_attention: false` already gives wgpu/cuda. Below `ReassociationPermitted` the cross-simdgroup merge (a reassociation of the online-softmax reduce, ROW 362's own `keys_per_chunk` sizing) never fires; at or above it, `context_length.div_ceil(ATTENTION_CONTEXT_KEYS_PER_CHUNK).clamp(1, ATTENTION_CONTEXT_CHUNK_CAP)` runs exactly as ROW 362 shipped it. Proven directly by `omega::msl::context_chunk_merge_is_gated_by_numeric_policy_for_a_real_64_key_context` (`msl.rs:8429-8444`): `context_chunks_for(64, BitExact) == 1`, `context_chunks_for(64, ReassociationPermitted) > 1` -- and by `render_cached_attention_omits_the_merge_block_under_bit_exact_policy` (`msl.rs:8452+`), which checks the rendered MSL source itself, not just the chunk count. Both passed in this row's own `-p omega` gate (211/211, see Gates below).

**Where the policy is admitted, plumbed, and folded into cache identity.** `omega::metal::Plan::set_numeric_policy` (`omega/src/metal.rs:676`) stores it on the `Plan`; `Plan::set_math_mode` (`metal.rs:660`) narrows `numeric_policy` to `MathMode`'s own coarser projection UNLESS the caller calls `set_numeric_policy` afterward, so `build_placed_plan` (below) calls `set_math_mode` then `set_numeric_policy` in that order -- the caller's own declared policy wins over `math_mode`'s narrower guess, not the reverse (this row's fix commit `f60b98e`, "relaxed math projects to reassociation permitted; identity folds the policy"). `omega::identity::numeric_policy_cache_token` (`identity.rs:135-142`) maps each of the four rungs to one cache-key character (`'B'`/`'N'`/`'R'`/`'F'`, wildcard `'F'` for any future rung above `FastMath`), and `MetalOnlyExtras::numeric_policy_token` folds that single character into `kernel_identity`'s cache-key string (`identity.rs:415-423`) -- this REPLACES the coarser `MathMode` token the pipeline cache used before, so two `Plan`s that agree on every structural field but disagree on numeric policy never collide on one `PIPELINE_CACHE` entry (`all_four_rungs_produce_distinct_tokens`, `identity.rs:441+`, part of this row's 211-test omega pass). `resolve_steps` (`metal.rs:5987`) and the plan's own `numeric_policy` field are the two places a caller can observe what's bound; `kernel_cache_key` (`msl.rs`, called from `metal.rs:795`) folds the policy into the structural cache key the same way.

**`ServingConfig::numeric_policy` is the explicit, per-invocation default -- not an implicit derivation from `math_mode`.** `proxima-model-interop/src/serving.rs:191` adds `pub numeric_policy: NumericPolicy`, defaulting to `NumericPolicy::ReassociationPermitted` (`serving.rs:242-245` and its two other default-construction sites) alongside `math_mode: MathMode::Relaxed`/`dispatch_type: DispatchType::Concurrent` -- `ReassociationPermitted`, not the crate-wide `NumericPolicy::default()` (`BitExact`), because `MathMode::Relaxed`'s own projection already lands there and ROW 362's chunk merge is meant to be reachable at the shipped default (`numeric_policy_agrees_across_literal_and_default_override`, `serving.rs:681+`, config-as-mirror per guiding principle 4: literal construction and `..Default::default()` override agree). `BackendRuntime::new` (`generate.rs:1550-1559`) reads all three fields off `&ServingConfig` once at construction.

**Correction commit, this row (class fix, not instance patch).** The branch's own `build_placed_plan` (`generate.rs`, the shared closure body every `placed_plans` cache-miss builds through, ROW 329's own class fix for the math-mode-forgetting defect) had grown to 8 positional parameters and carried `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "...")]`. Commit `004d25e` ("refactor(interop): build_placed_plan takes the serving config") replaces the three trailing `math_mode`/`numeric_policy`/`dispatch_type` parameters with one `&PlanNumerics` reference -- a plain `Copy` struct grouping exactly the three `ServingConfig` knobs every one of the three call sites (`evaluate_with_placements`, `evaluate_op_timed_with_placements`, `evaluate_dispatch_timed_with_placements`) already copies off `self` in one statement before the plan-cache build closure. `build_placed_plan` is at 6 parameters now (under clippy's `too_many_arguments` default of 7), so the `#[allow]` is deleted, not silenced. `ServingConfig` itself was not threaded through directly: `BackendRuntime` has no lifetime parameter today, and `ServingConfig<'model>`'s `model_path: &'model str` field would force one onto it and every signature downstream -- `PlanNumerics` is the minimal grouping that answers "what does `build_placed_plan` actually need" without that ripple, while still being one reference instead of three positional copies at the call site.

**A/B oracle guard -- the policy is meant to be behavior-preserving at the shipped default, not a silent default change hiding behind green tests.** Oracle-A: `main` (`bb90cac`, ROW 362's chunk sizing already applied, built in a detached worktree `proxima-wt-a363`) -- NOT `r352-logs/oracle-A` (`19010e8`), which predates ROW 362 and is not comparable. Oracle-B: this row's rebased `feat/numeric-policy` top (`004d25e`). Both `cargo test --release -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument --no-run`, same test binary hash (`proxima_model_interop-7e054ae5518b199e` both sides -- coincidental hash collision across separate builds, confirmed distinct by `md5`: A=`797b4682280b61ccca2b53ba2b318106`, B=`b721d6c08b61dd81b7f48d7d8fcf9d35`). Two rounds, interleaved A,B,A,B, `RUST_LOG=info PROXIMA_MAX_TOKENS=64 <oracle> bind::real_openchat_file::runs_the_cached_decode_loop_on_the_metal_backend_and_reports_the_plan_cache --exact --nocapture --test-threads=1 --ignored`, quiet gate passed before the rounds (names-only pgrep empty, `while true` pgrep empty, load-1 6.94 -> spiked to 22.08 on a re-check before the run -> one 30s retry -> 7.29, no contending cargo/nextest/measurement process at any point, the spike traced to `mediaanalysisd`/`mds_stores`/`iTerm2`, not a competing build):

| window | A gpu_exec_ms mean (round1, round2) | B gpu_exec_ms mean (round1, round2) | A step_wall_ms mean | B step_wall_ms mean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| step 3..7 (n=5/round) | 20.427, 19.915 | 19.969, 20.471 | 21.150, 20.755 | 20.768, 21.199 |
| step 32..63 (n=32/round) | 21.066, 20.880 | 20.988, 20.891 | 23.113, 22.131 | 22.205, 22.194 |

The two rounds' ranges overlap at both windows: step 3..7 gpu_exec spans A 19.915-20.427 ms and B 19.969-20.471 ms; step 32..63 gpu_exec spans A 20.880-21.066 ms and B 20.891-20.988 ms (full table above). Overlapping ranges alone do not establish non-regression; no combined-CoV comparison across rounds was computed, and none is claimed here. **Text identity:** `grep -o 'generated_text="[^"]*"'` on all four round logs (`round1-A.log`, `round1-B.log`, `round2-A.log`, `round2-B.log`) and `md5`-summed -- all four produce the identical hash `84c7519e6bffea98476fefd9d545a0fc` (64 greedy-decoded tokens, the same Fibonacci-function completion). **Chunk merge activation is a configuration claim, not an observation of the live decode -- named precisely, not as a substitute for the missing measurement:** the test harness's `install_stdout_telemetry` hardcodes its `EnvFilter` to `"debug"` (`bind.rs:3146-3148`, ignores `RUST_LOG`), so the `trace!(cache_key = ..)` line at `metal.rs:4202`/`4207` that would show the `'R'` policy token inside a live pipeline cache key never surfaces from either oracle binary without a source change this row declines to make (would itself be a behavior change to the artifact under test). What was actually observed: the A/B decode text is byte-identical across all four logs and `gpu_exec_ms` sits inside normal round-to-round spread (both above); `context_chunk_merge_is_gated_by_numeric_policy_for_a_real_64_key_context` (`msl.rs:8429`) -- part of this row's own 211-test `-p omega` pass below -- asserts `context_chunks_for(64, ReassociationPermitted) > 1` as a standalone unit test of the sizing function, not against a captured plan from either oracle run; and `ServingConfig::default().numeric_policy == ReassociationPermitted` is inspected as the config both oracle binaries construct, not read back from a resolved plan mid-decode. None of these three observations is a captured per-plan chunk count from the live decode pipeline -- no such capture was taken this row, and this evidence supports the intended configuration, not an observation of chunk activation during decode. It also does not establish that chunking regressed: the A/B parity above holds regardless of which chunk count fired.

**Flip decision: FLIPPED.** `NumericPolicy`/`admit` land as the permission-ladder primitive; `ServingConfig::numeric_policy` lands as its explicit per-invocation default; the correction commit removes the `#[allow]` this row introduced. Behavior at the shipped default is unchanged (text byte-identical, gpu_exec at parity across two A/B rounds) -- the row adds the gate and the explicit declaration, it does not change what the gate currently permits.

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- `NumericPolicy`'s four-rung total order (no new numeric constant; the ladder itself is the axis). structural -- `ServingConfig::numeric_policy` is a new config field with an explicit default (`ReassociationPermitted`), config-as-mirror verified (`numeric_policy_agrees_across_literal_and_default_override`); pipeline cache identity gains one character of key space (`numeric_policy_cache_token`) in place of the coarser `MathMode` token it replaces, not in addition to it. **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** N/A -- `admit` is a pure, alloc-free, no_std comparison (`Ord` on two `Copy` enums) called from existing bind/plan-time state machines, not a new sans-IO component.

**Residuals, named not hidden.** (1) The cache-key policy-token grep the original brief asked for could not be produced from either oracle binary's own log because the test harness's telemetry filter is hardcoded to `"debug"` and never reads `RUST_LOG` -- confirmed via a fifth, non-timed diagnostic invocation (`trace-B-diagnostic.log`) that produced zero `trace!`-level lines at any filter string tried; the unit-test proof (`msl.rs:8429`) substitutes for it but is one level removed from a live pipeline-cache key observed in a real decode. (2) `FusedNoReassociation` and `FastMath` are not yet reached by any shipped rewrite site (`FmaContraction` and `FastMathApprox` exist as `NumericRewrite` variants with no caller today) -- the ladder is proven at its `BitExact`/`ReassociationPermitted` boundary only, the boundary ROW 362's chunk merge actually exercises. (3) `admit`'s cost is one `Ord` comparison per rewrite site per call, not cached or hoisted -- unmeasured whether this matters at any rewrite site hotter than the per-decode-step context-chunk-merge gate (called once per plan build, not once per token).

## ROW 365 -- an iteration axis's declared extent (`AxisIndex::len`) is a fact distinct from its address term, honored (or typed-rejected) at every term shape `unify_iteration_space` and `fold_iteration_extents` touch

**Card:** none. **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-domain`, `feat/iteration-domain`, rebased onto `main` at `8573265` (ROW 363's numeric policy plus `feat(omega): pipeline-cache miss logs the attention chunk lowering choice`, clean rebase, zero conflicts), landed as `0f995fc`/`2847649`/`b83d815`/`c618ad2` (four commits, base `078ba95`).

**The bug this closes.** `AxisIndex` conflated two independent facts into one bit pattern: "how to compute this axis's address" (`terms`/`offset`) and "how many iterations this axis has" (previously inferred *only* from a plain `coeff == 1, offset == 0` term reading the operand's own on-disk width). A caller reading a genuine narrower slice of a wider operand at a nonzero offset — RoPE's split-half pairing, `attn_head_dim` rotary channels narrower than the full head — had no way to state its true extent directly, so `RopePairing::SplitHalf` faked it by spelling the address `"i+0*i"`: an algebraically-identical but differently-shaped expression whose only purpose was to make the single-term match fail so the axis fell through to bounds-checking instead of wrongly anchoring on the operand's full width. This is the shifted-declaration defect the owner traced: a **declared `len` on a shifted or scaled term (`i+1@2`, `2*i@4`) was silently dropped**, because `unify_iteration_space` only ever consulted `axis.len` inside the `coeff == 1, offset == 0` branch — the one shape of term that never needed narrowing in the first place, since that branch already reads the operand's own on-disk width unconditionally.

**The contract.** `AxisIndex::len: Option<Extent>` (`map.rs`) states an axis's true iteration extent directly, independent of `terms`/`offset`. `AxisIndex::len_target_axis()` (`map.rs:95-116`) names which iteration axis a declared `len` describes: unambiguous for a single term regardless of its `coeff`/`offset`, and for a multi-term axis (convolution's `2*i+p`) only when exactly one term carries `coeff == 1` — the "plain" contribution as opposed to a stride/dilation-scaled one; zero or more than one such term (`i+j@2`) returns `None`. `unify_iteration_space` (`shape.rs:221-264`, rewritten this row) now resolves `defines: Option<(target_axis, extent)>` up front for *every* term shape: a declared `len` (via `len_target_axis`, erroring `TensorError::AmbiguousLenAxis { node, dim }` if it returns `None`) takes priority over the old sole fallback (a pure, unshifted, `coeff == 1` projection reading the operand's own width) — both routes write into the same `resolved` slot and disagree the same way, so a declared `len` conflicting with another operand's anchor for the same axis rejects via the existing `TensorError::ExtentMismatch { node, dim, left, right }`, never silently prefers one. `spec.rs::parse_axis_expr` (`spec.rs:255-310`) adds the `@length` grammar (`"i@4"`, `"i@{pairs}"` for a symbolic extent) as a trailing, syntactically distinct suffix on the address expression — parse-time rejects (via the same `AmbiguousLenAxis` path, `spec.rs:302`) a notation like `"i+j@2"` whose two equally-plain terms give `len` no unique target, rather than silently guessing one. Bounds checking is preserved exactly: a `len`-marked axis is never treated as the old "pure projection, skip the bounds check" case (`shape.rs:286-293`, `is_pure_projection` now requires `axis.len.is_none()`), so it always routes through `bounds_check` the same way a nonzero offset already forces a bounds check instead of a definer match — `a_len_that_exceeds_the_operands_own_width_is_still_rejected` proves a declared `len` wider than the operand's real storage still rejects as `TensorError::IndexOutOfBounds`.

**Before/after, the RoPE spelling.** `RopePairing::SplitHalf`'s dead-term address hack, `"i+0*i"` (an algebraically-identical-but-differently-shaped expression that existed solely to defeat the single-term match), becomes a direct declaration: `"i@{pairs}"` (`spec.rs:660`) states `pairs` as the axis's true extent while the paired odd-half address stays a plain `"i+{pairs}"` — the fact ("this axis is `pairs` wide") is now spelled once, as data, rather than encoded indirectly in how the address term is shaped.

**The owner's traced example, as the test.** `a_shifted_len_declaration_disagrees_with_an_unshifted_anchor` (`shape.rs:868-901`) reproduces the shifted-declaration defect exactly: `left`'s `i+1@2` (shifted, `len` declared 2) against `right`'s plain unshifted `i` (anchoring the same axis at its own on-disk width, 3) — before this row's fix, `left`'s declared `len` never entered the `coeff==1, offset==0`-only branch and was silently dropped, `infer` returned `Ok([1, 3])`; after, both routes compete for the same `resolved` slot and disagree, `infer` returns `TensorError::ExtentMismatch { dim: 1, left: 2, right: 3 }`. `a_shifted_len_declaration_with_no_conflicting_anchor_resolves` (same shape, no competing anchor) proves the fix resolves the declaration cleanly, not merely detects a conflict. `a_multi_term_axis_resolves_len_onto_its_unit_coefficient_term` and `a_len_on_two_unit_coefficient_terms_is_ambiguous` cover `len_target_axis`'s multi-term resolution and its `None` (ambiguous) case respectively.

**Why the contract lives on `AxisIndex` (per-axis), not threaded through the `Reduce`/op level.** `fold_iteration_extents` (`shape.rs`, called from `bind.rs`'s reduce-building path) re-derives a `Reduce`'s iteration extents from its already-*resolved* operand `Shapes`, specifically to avoid re-threading the symbol table (`self.symbols`) that `resolve_extent` needs to turn a symbolic `Extent` into a concrete `u64` into a function that runs after shape inference is done. Honoring a `len`-marked axis there would need that thread, and `bind.rs` does not carry it. Rather than silently fold from the operand's own on-disk width whenever `len` narrows it (wrong exactly when it matters), this row's own first commit (`b83d815`) makes `fold_iteration_extents` take `node: NodeId` and return `Result<Vec<u64>, TensorError>`, rejecting a `len`-marked reduce axis with the new `TensorError::ReduceLenAxisUnsupported { node, dim }` instead — both call sites in `bind.rs` (`build_reduce_op`'s two callers) now propagate the `?`. `fold_iteration_extents_rejects_a_len_marked_axis` (`shape.rs`) proves it. This is a typed, explicit gap (a reduce operand cannot yet narrow its own iteration axis via `len`) rather than a silent correctness hole — closing it fully is not this row's scope.

**Flip decision: FLIPPED.** `AxisIndex::len` and `len_target_axis` land as the primitive; `unify_iteration_space` and `parse_axis_expr` honor it for every term shape (not just the one branch that used to silently swallow it); the reduce-fold gap is closed by typed rejection, not left silent. `RopePairing::SplitHalf` moves off the `"i+0*i"` address trick onto direct `@length` declaration.

**Axes (principle 8):** structural -- `AxisIndex` gains one field (`len: Option<Extent>`, `#[derive(Default)]` keeps every existing struct-literal site compiling with `len: None` for free; the two commits ahead of this row's own diff added zero new `AxisIndex` literal sites needing an explicit update, confirmed by diffing main's two post-merge-base commits, neither of which touches `map.rs`/`spec.rs`/`shape.rs`). No new numeric/build-time-tunable axis. **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** N/A -- `len_target_axis` and the `unify_iteration_space` change are pure, alloc-free, no_std comparisons over already-owned `Copy`/`SmallVec` data (proven by this row's own `cargo check -p proxima-tensor --no-default-features --features alloc` gate, below), not a new sans-IO component.

**Residuals, named not hidden.** (1) **The oracle guard (A/B on real decode text + gpu_exec) was not run.** Between the rebase and the gate window, `pgrep` twice found live `cargo`/`cargo-nextest`/`rustc` processes belonging to other agents' worktrees (`proxima-wt-rms`, `proxima-wt-kv`) and load-1 at 13-19 -- measured, not assumed (both pgrep outputs and `uptime` captured live during this row). The THERMAL RULE's "never more than ONE agent running cargo at a time" and this row's own 30-minute hard budget made a two-sided release build (main baseline + rebased branch, each `cargo test --release -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument --no-run`, both several minutes cold) incompatible with waiting out the contention. The static gates (clippy x2, nextest x5, check x2, all below) are the only evidence this row carries for correctness; no gpu_exec range, no text-identity md5, and no A/B table are claimed. This is a gap, not a "not worse" verdict — a future row should re-run the guard once the box is quiet. (2) `fold_iteration_extents`'s reduce-level gap (residual (see above): a reduce operand's iteration axis cannot narrow via `len`) is typed and tested but not closed; the fix threads no symbol table into `bind.rs`. (3) `len`'s only shipped caller today is `RopePairing::SplitHalf`'s rewritten address; no other spec site was migrated off an equivalent address trick this row, because none was found using the same `grep -n '+0\*'` sweep across `spec.rs` (unverified beyond that one grep; a broader sweep for other narrowing-via-address-shape tricks was not performed).

## ROW 366 -- merged-KV attention was iterating a fabricated cached half and a doubled capacity; the bind now declares that half empty, and the stride loop's own bound tracks the live key count, not the compiled capacity

**Card:** none. **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-kv`, `fix/merged-kv-attention-bounds`, rebased onto `main` at `873fdaa` (ROW 365, clean rebase, zero conflicts), landed as `fix(tensor): merged-kv attention binds no cached half` + `perf(omega): attention strides to the live key bound, not the capacity` (base `8573265`).

**The bug this closes, traced on `main` at `8573265` (`chunk-length.md`).** The Mistral-style single-range (merged-KV) cached-attention fusion (`bind.rs`'s `cached_attention_single_range_candidates`) has no separate cached/new tensor pair — one merged KV buffer serves both. To fit the one `BoundOpKind::CachedAttention` shape the renderer knows, the old bind duplicated the SAME bucketed-capacity key/value shape (`key_shape[0]`, `kv_extent`'s bucketed extent — `proxima-model-interop/src/generate.rs:817-822`) into BOTH `cached_key_rows` and `new_key_rows`, and neutered the "cached" half with an unreachable `[i64::MAX, i64::MAX]` band (`cached_lower_inclusive: i64::MAX`). Consequence, live-traced on the real openchat decode fixture at step 2 (`cached_len_before=32`, capacity bucket 39): `context_length = cached_key_rows + new_key_rows = 39 + 39 = 78` (`metal.rs:4218` at the time), `context_chunks_for(78, ..) = 4` (`omega-runtime.toml`'s `keys_per_chunk=16, cap=4`), and the per-simdgroup stride loop ran `for (key = chunk; key < 78; key += chunks)` — every key in `[0, 39)` is unconditionally `continue`d (the dead cached half, every call), and the correct chunk count for a 39-key live range is `ceil(39/16) = 3`, not 4: **the wrong partitioning was compiled in from a fabricated capacity, not merely wasted iterations.** The kernel identity carried this exactly: `omega_cached_attention_..._c39_n39_..._lp9223372036854775807_..._x4`.

**What this bug did NOT cost.** The dead-range `continue` checks (`if (cached && relative < cached_lower) { continue; }`) precede every K/V load and multiply-add in the loop body — a fake key never reached a load or an accumulate, so this was never "double the attention arithmetic" or "half the simdgroups idling": chunks stride-interleave keys across simdgroups (`key = chunk; key += context_chunks`), so the fake cached-half keys were spread across every simdgroup's own assigned subset, not confined to some idle set. The avoidable cost was iteration/address/control overhead (loop trip count, the `cached`/`new_index`/`relative` arithmetic, the branch itself) on the dead half, plus a WRONG chunk count on the live half from the same fabricated 78.

**The fix is two distinct decisions, not one loop edit.** (1) **Partitioning** (`bind.rs:2630`, the single-range candidate): declares `cached_key_rows: 0` — an empty range, not a live range neutered by a sentinel — with `new_key_rows` still the bucketed capacity and `cached_lower_inclusive: i64::MIN` (no sentinel needed once the range is empty). This changes what `context_chunks_for(*cached_key_rows + *new_key_rows, ..)` (`msl.rs:3084`) is fed at CHUNK-SIZING time — `0 + 39 = 39` instead of `39 + 39 = 78` — which changes the compiled chunk count itself (a repartitioning: 4 chunks -> 3 at this window), independent of any loop-bound change. (2) **The stride loop's own upper bound** (`msl.rs:3107-3143`, `render_cached_attention`): when the single-range fusion's ninth (dynamic) operand carries the live `cached_len` at run time, each simdgroup's own loop now stops at `last_key = cached_key_rows + min(new_key_rows - 1, query_row + new_upper)` instead of always walking the full compiled `cached_key_rows + new_key_rows - 1`. This is exactly equivalent, never an approximation: both bands are monotone in `key`, so every key past `last_key` would `continue` on every remaining iteration within that simdgroup's own assigned subset regardless. `cpu.rs`'s CPU evaluator gets a matching typed guard (`run_cached_attention`, new): the runtime `cached_len` operand is rejected with `TensorError::NotLowerable` if it is `>= new_key_rows` (the compiled buffer extent), never silently read out of range. Neither value is "the context length": chunk sizing and the loop bound are named as separate decisions in `context_chunks_for`'s own doc (`msl.rs:2958-2977`) precisely so this distinction doesn't collapse again.

**Consumers updated (file:line, at the rebased tip).** `bind.rs:2402-2411` (doc), `bind.rs:2620-2632` (`cached_key_rows: 0`, `cached_lower_inclusive: i64::MIN`). `msl.rs:2958-2977` (two-decisions doc), `msl.rs:3084-3143` (`last_key` computed per branch, both stride loops changed from `<` capacity to `<= last_key`). `cpu.rs:5065-5074` (the new `cached_len >= new_key_rows` guard). `physical.rs:342-358` (`stream_cached_attention_split_gqa`'s buffer-length check no longer requires the cached slot's buffer to match a zero-sized extent when `cached_key_rows == 0` — the caller may legitimately pass the same buffer it passed for the new range). Identity (`identity.rs:319`) needed no code change: `_c{cached_key_rows}` interpolates the field directly, so `cached_key_rows: 0` alone produces `_c0` in the kernel identity, confirmed live below.

**Live confirmation, decode fixture (release+instrument, real openchat-3.5-1210.Q4_K_S.gguf, `PROXIMA_MAX_TOKENS=8`), step 2 (`cached_len_before=32`, same call the trace above analyzed):**

| | `main` (`8573265`, oracle-A) | this branch (oracle-B) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kernel_identity` | `omega_cached_attention_q1_c32_n32..._lp9223372036854775807_udyn_x4...` (prefill) / `..._c39_n39..._lp9223372036854775807_udyn_x4...` (step 2) | `..._c0_n32..._ln9223372036854775808_udyn_x2...` (prefill) / `..._c0_n39..._ln9223372036854775808_udyn_x3...` (step 2) |
| `context_length` / `context_chunks` (step 2) | `78` / `4` | `39` / `3` |
| `encode_dispatch_calls` (every step) | `520` | `520` |
| `generated_text` (8 tokens) | `"Here is a simple Python function that returns"` | identical |

Dispatch count unchanged (520, matching ROW 358's own census) — this row changes partitioning and iteration count within already-dispatched work, not what gets dispatched. `r366-logs/count-A.log`, `r366-logs/count-B.log`.

**A/B oracle guard.** Oracle-A: `main` (`8573265`, pre-ROW-364/365, built in a detached worktree `proxima-wt-a366`). Oracle-B: this row's rebased branch top. Both `cargo test --release -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument --no-run`, same test-binary hash (`proxima_model_interop-7e054ae5518b199e` both sides, coincidental — confirmed distinct by md5: A=`e1483566a9af504681b0b5c4a6161e09`, B=`2a7f5fa6ebf0fd938cb9ed2b326e6449`, identical size `3866784`). Quiet gate passed before each round (names-only pgrep empty, `while true` pgrep empty, load-1 2.7-5.5 throughout). This establishes CPU-side and text-level (greedy-decode) parity; it does NOT establish Metal-kernel bit-identity across the repartitioning (78->39, 4->3 chunks changes which keys accumulate together within a simdgroup and in what order chunks merge) — the Metal-side correctness evidence for that is the `omega`/`proxima-model-interop` `metal,instrument` parity-suite gates (below, all green at the existing tolerance), not a bit-identical claim.

## ROW 367 -- an RMSNorm's post-reduce tail fuses INTO the reduce as a broadcast epilogue, instead of a separate `Reduce` + `Elementwise` pair; the fold this row's own gate caught first, a refcount bug that rejected production SiLU as "read by another consumer"

**Card:** none (originally scoped as "ROW 364"; renumbered on landing after ROWs 365/366 landed ahead of it from `main`). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-rms`, `perf/rmsnorm-epilogue`, rebased onto `main` at `c854e54` then `d44ec07` (clean both times, zero conflicts), landed as `fix(tensor): epilogue fusion counts distinct consumers, not operand reads` + `test(tensor): production silu fuses; a different projection does not` + `test(tensor): row 364 per-layer bound op artifact`.

**The form.** `reduce_epilogue_fusion` (`bind.rs`, `#[cfg(feature = "reduce-epilogue-fusion")]`) already folded a post-reduce `Elementwise` tail into its own `Reduce`'s `epilogue_body` when the tail's only non-broadcast operand is that reduce's fold output and no other resolved op reads the fold. RMSNorm's tail (`x * rsqrt(mean(x^2) + eps) * weight`, `spec.rs`'s RMSNorm builder) is exactly that shape once the mean-square reduce has no other consumer -- before this row it did not fold because the LIVENESS CHECK undercounted correctly-shaped programs as having "another consumer."

**Corrected evidence tier: this is BoundOp-count STRUCTURAL evidence** (a static property of the bound program, not a dispatch trace and not a timing) **-- see the per-kind dispatch count and the oracle below for the other two tiers.**

**The refcount defect this row fixes (`fix(tensor): epilogue fusion counts distinct consumers, not operand reads`, `bind.rs:2935-2997`).** `resolved_reference_counts` counted every OPERAND-SLOT read of a `NodeId`, not every DISTINCT CONSUMING OP. Production SiLU (`spec.rs`'s `silu` builder, used by `mistral_single_range_cached_forward_program`'s gate/up MLP path) reads its `gate` operand TWICE inside one consumer -- once bare, once again inside `exp(-gate)` -- and chain composition preserves both as separate `operands` slots. The old counter saw `gate`'s source "referenced" twice and concluded a second, external consumer existed, failing `reduce_epilogue_fusion`'s own condition (b) ("no OTHER consumer") and declining to fuse -- on a program with exactly ONE real consumer. The fix dedupes each consumer's own read sources to a `BTreeSet` before folding into the per-source total, so N reads by ONE consumer count as the one reference that consumer actually is. `find_epilogue_source` (`bind.rs:2981-3029`) carries the matching correction: two operand slots naming the SAME reduce through the SAME `Layout` (SiLU's bare/`exp` double-read) are one logical read and are accepted; two slots naming the same reduce through DIFFERENT `Layout`s (a parity-selecting split, e.g. `gate = paired[..,0,..]` / `up = paired[..,1,..]` landing in one consumer) is the real conflict and is still declined -- `compose_reduce_epilogue`'s "implicit fold-result slot" model has room for exactly one such read, and guessing which occurrence wins would silently corrupt the other.

**The Tanh-vs-production-SiLU fixture lesson (`test(tensor): production silu fuses; a different projection does not`).** The existing `silu_gate_times_up_fuses_both_reduces_bit_for_bit` fixture built its own `Tanh(gate)` stand-in instead of calling `crate::spec::silu` -- a `Tanh(gate)` reads `gate` ONCE, so the refcount defect above was invisible to it: the fixture passed both before and after the fix, proving nothing about the bug it was meant to guard. This row's test change replaces the stand-in with a call to the PRODUCTION `silu` builder itself, so the fixture now exercises the real double-read shape and would have caught the original defect. A second test (`a_gathered_source_aborts_the_single_range_candidate_entirely`'s sibling in the same block) asserts the DIFFERENT-`Layout` case is still declined, so both branches of `find_epilogue_source`'s corrected match arm are covered.

**Structural evidence (BoundOp count), corrected onto the SAME builder production takes.** The originally-drafted census called `mistral_cached_forward_program` (the dual-range builder), NOT `mistral_single_range_cached_forward_program`, the builder `proxima-model-interop::generate::build_single_range_program` actually calls for every non-MoE checkpoint including openchat (`DuplicateHeadPosition::None`, `generate.rs:756-786`). That dual-range toy fixture's gate reduce happened to already carry a fused SiLU epilogue on BOTH main and this branch (an accident of that builder's own shapes), so it could not show what this row changes and is not used below. Redone on the single-range builder, one layer, same shapes (`vocab=32, embedding=16, feed_forward=24, query_heads=4, kv_heads=2, head_dim=4, block_count=1`), through `bind()` (fusion on):

| | `main` (`d44ec07`, throwaway census in `proxima-wt-a364`) | this branch (committed as `row_364_per_layer_bound_op_list`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bound op count | 34 | 28 |
| RMSNorm sites (3: two per-layer + none extra at 1 layer... actually 2 attn/ffn norms this shape has no final norm node since `logits` root is the raw MLP output at 1 layer) | `Reduce{element_ops=[Multiply]}` + separate `Elementwise{step_ops=[Multiply,Add,SquareRoot,Reciprocal,Multiply,Multiply]}` tail, at indices (7,8), (24,25), (29,30) -- three sites, 2 ops each = 6 ops | ONE `Reduce{epilogue_broadcast_axes=[1], epilogue_ops=[Identity,Multiply,Add,SquareRoot,Reciprocal,Multiply,Multiply]}` per site, at indices 7, 20, 24 -- three sites, 1 op each = 3 ops |
| other reduce+elementwise pairs also folded (softmax normalization, e.g. main's `Reciprocal,Multiply` tail after its softmax-sum reduce) | present as separate ops | folded into the owning reduce's epilogue where condition (b) holds |

Net: -6 BoundOps (34 -> 28) at this one-layer shape; the 3 RMSNorm sites alone account for -3 of those (a `Reduce`+`Elementwise` pair collapsing to one `Reduce`), the remainder from the SAME fusion pass now also firing on the softmax-tail shape it was already eligible for once the refcount fix stopped rejecting programs with a shared-but-deduped source. Full per-index lists: `r364-logs/branch-print-singlerange.log`, `r364-logs/main-print-singlerange.log`.

**Production-dispatch evidence (executable structure, not structural or latency): the real openchat decode fixture** (release+instrument, `PROXIMA_MAX_TOKENS=8 PROXIMA_METAL_OP_PROFILE_STEP=3`, step 3 op-kind buckets, `r364-logs/production-dispatch-branch.log`): this branch reports `constant=2 elementwise=129 iota=2 reduce-cooperative=66 reduce-packed-row-blocked=224`. Against the `elementwise=194 reduce-cooperative=66 total=520` this row's brief carried forward as the `main` baseline for the identical fixture and step: `elementwise` drops by 65 (194 -> 129). openchat's real architecture is 32 transformer blocks; the RMSNorm-epilogue fold removes one `Elementwise` tail per RMSNorm site, and a 32-layer model has 2 RMSNorm sites per layer (attn_norm, ffn_norm) plus one final norm before the LM head: `32*2 + 1 = 65`, an exact match to the observed drop. This is the ~65 case named in this row's own brief, not the ~33 case -- the real production program's RMSNorm tails DO fold at full model scale, confirming the one-layer toy fixture's structural finding generalizes. `reduce-cooperative` unchanged (66 -> 66; the fold changes what a `Reduce`'s OWN epilogue does, not how many `Reduce`s dispatch). `generated_text="Here is a simple Python function that returns"` matches the brief's expected text exactly.

**WGSL/CUDA typed rejections.** Neither WGSL (`omega/src/wgsl.rs:1126-1131`) nor CUDA (`omega/src/cuda.rs:1188-1193`) has a renderer for `epilogue_broadcast_axes` yet; both reject at bind/emit time with a typed `EmitError::EpilogueNotSupported { reason: "the broadcast-reduce epilogue (epilogue_broadcast_axes) has no {WGSL,CUDA} renderer yet" }` rather than emitting a kernel that reads or writes the wrong element count -- the same "no renderer, reject" contract Metal used before its own broadcast-reduce write landed. This row's fusion is Metal-only in practice until those renderers exist; WGSL/CUDA programs continue to bind the pre-fusion (unfused) shape.

**Oracle A/B (latency evidence, ranges only -- no "not worse" verdict).** Oracle-A: `main` (`d44ec07`, detached worktree `proxima-wt-a364`). Oracle-B: this row's rebased branch top (`proxima-wt-rms`). Both `cargo build --release -p proxima-model-interop --tests --features metal,instrument`.
