## ROW 374 ADDENDUM -- ROW 374's policy projection could construct a Plan that exceeds its own granted permissions, and a narrowed MathMode could silently reuse a pipeline compiled under the wider one

(Filed as an addendum to ROW 374, not a new numbered row, to avoid colliding with another concurrent worktree's own numbered row over the same landing window.)

**Two defects found in landed source (main `943b099`, ROW 374's own commit), both fixed as their own commits.**

**(1) Construction could exceed the granted permissions.** `numeric_policy_as_metal_math_mode` (`omega/src/metal.rs:4309`) rounded UP to the nearest mode that "never under-grants" -- `contraction || reassociation` -> `Relaxed`, `approx_functions || nan_assumptions || signed_zero` -> `Fast`. `Relaxed`'s OWN permission set (`metal_math_mode_as_numeric_policy(Relaxed) == llama_relaxed()`) is `contraction AND reassociation`; a `contraction`-only policy does not grant `reassociation` and so does not grant `llama_relaxed()`, yet the old code handed it `Relaxed` anyway -- and `Fast` grants everything, so a `signed_zero`-only policy was handed a mode granting `approx_functions`/`nan_assumptions`/`contraction`/`reassociation` too. `plan()` (`metal.rs:897`) assigns this projection directly at construction, with no subset check (unlike `Plan::set_math_mode`, which already used `NumericPolicy::grants` correctly).

**Fix:** the projection now selects the WIDEST mode whose OWN permission set is a subset of what the policy grants, reusing `NumericPolicy::grants` (the identical subset check `set_math_mode` already used) instead of an ad hoc OR-chain:
```rust
const fn numeric_policy_as_metal_math_mode(policy: NumericPolicy) -> MathMode {
    if policy.grants(NumericPolicy::fast()) { MathMode::Fast }
    else if policy.grants(NumericPolicy::llama_relaxed()) { MathMode::Relaxed }
    else { MathMode::Safe }
}
```
**Projection table, all 32 permission subsets** (only `contraction`(c)/`reassociation`(r) matter for `Relaxed`; all five matter for `Fast`; every other bit is irrelevant to the mode chosen): `Fast` iff `c && r && nan_assumptions && signed_zero && approx_functions` (1 of 32 subsets); `Relaxed` iff `c && r` and NOT all-five (7 of 32 subsets: `cr`, `cr`+any nonempty proper subset of `{nan,sz,af}`); `Safe` for the remaining 24 subsets (anything lacking `c` or `r`). A test (`numeric_policy_projection_never_grants_more_than_the_policy_allows`) iterates all 32 subsets and asserts `policy.grants(metal_math_mode_as_numeric_policy(projected_mode))` for every one -- the property the owner named, not a fixed set of examples.

**(2) Narrowing the math mode could reuse the wider pipeline.** `Plan::set_math_mode` correctly refuses to WIDEN past the bound `numeric_policy`, but a NARROWING call (`Relaxed` -> `Safe` on a plan bound under `llama_relaxed()`, which permits both) triggered `resolve_steps`' staleness check (`metal.rs:6474`, keyed on `math_mode` alone) to rebuild -- yet `resolve_steps`/`encode_op` built the `PIPELINE_CACHE` lookup key from `kernel_cache_key(bound, packed_operands, numeric_policy)` alone, which carries only the (unchanged) `numeric_policy` token, never `math_mode`. `identity.rs`'s own `numeric_policy_token` doc claimed this token "subsumes [the math-mode token] completely" -- true for axes `numeric_policy` fixes for a `Plan`'s whole life, false for `math_mode`, which is the ONE axis `set_math_mode` can still move post-construction while `numeric_policy` stays fixed. Two resolutions differing only by `set_math_mode` render byte-identical MSL source (`compile_pipeline` never touches source text) but are compiled with different `MTLCompileOptions.mathMode`, and the old key could not tell them apart -- a `set_math_mode(Safe)` call could silently keep serving the `Relaxed`-compiled `PIPELINE_CACHE` entry.

**What `compile_pipeline` (`metal.rs:4376`) actually reads:** `kernel.source` (the rendered MSL text, a function of `bound`/`packed_operands`/`numeric_policy` via `emit`) and `math_mode` (fed straight into `MTLCompileOptions.setMathMode`) -- nothing else. `kernel_cache_key`'s identity already covers everything `emit` reads (that's its whole job); `math_mode` was the one compile input missing from the key.

**Fix, minimal, no `msl.rs` signature change:** `MathMode::cache_token(self) -> char` (`'S'`/`'R'`/`'F'`) is appended to `kernel_cache_key`'s returned string at every `PIPELINE_CACHE` call site -- `resolve_steps`, `encode_op`, and `Plan::kernel_keys` (whose own doc already, incorrectly, claimed the mode was included). Kept out of `identity.rs`/`MetalOnlyExtras` deliberately: that module has no dependency on the macOS-only `metal` module `MathMode` lives in, and `kernel_cache_key`'s many `msl.rs` unit-test call sites (which do not exercise `Plan`/`set_math_mode` at all) would otherwise all need a mode argument they do not care about. `identity.rs`'s `numeric_policy_token` doc corrected to state the real invariant instead of "subsumes it completely".

**Executed-transition test** (`narrowing_math_mode_forces_a_genuine_pipeline_cache_miss_not_a_stale_hit`, `#[cfg(feature = "instrument")]`, real Metal device, skips if none present): builds a `Plan` under `llama_relaxed()` (constructs `Relaxed`, confirming defect (1) is fixed rather than defaulting to `Fast`), calls `resolve_steps` (`PIPELINE_MISSES` delta = 1, a fresh-plan miss), reads `kernel_keys()[0]`, calls `set_math_mode(Safe)`, calls `resolve_steps` again and asserts `PIPELINE_MISSES` delta = 1 AGAIN (a genuine second miss, not a stale hit reusing the Relaxed PSO), asserts the two `kernel_keys()` strings differ (by exactly the trailing mode token), and reads `resolved_steps.math_mode` back as `Safe` (the resolved-cache-entry's own recorded mode, the compile-option evidence `compile_pipeline` itself does not expose a getter for).

**(3) Premise correction, for the record.** `llama_relaxed()` grants `contraction`+`reassociation` only. At `proxima-tensor` BIND time (`bind.rs:3008`, `bind_with_fusion`), the three rewrites this crate ships (`IdentityElimination`, `ChainFusion`, `ReduceEpilogueFusion`) all require `NumericPolicy::bit_exact()` (no permission) and admit under ANY policy including `bit_exact()` itself -- `llama_relaxed()` grants them nothing they did not already have. The split eliminations that DO need a permission (`IdentityEliminationSignedZero` needs `signed_zero`, `IdentityEliminationNanAssumption` needs `nan_assumptions`) are both withheld by `llama_relaxed()`. So `llama_relaxed()` enables NO bind-time rewrite in `proxima-tensor::bind` beyond what `bit_exact()` already admits. (`NumericRewrite::ContextChunkMerge`, which DOES fire under `llama_relaxed()`'s `reassociation` grant per ROW 374's own "Owed observation" section, is an `omega`-side GPU-LOWERING-time chunking choice inside `msl::emit`, not a `proxima-tensor::bind`-time rewrite -- the two are at different pipeline stages and the owner's claim is scoped to the latter.) Grepped ROW 374 and `proxima-tensor/src/numeric.rs`'s own doc comments for a sentence that frames the `ServingConfig.numeric_policy` default's change to `llama_relaxed()` as a new optimization: found none -- ROW 374's own "Interop wiring" paragraph already states it is "the same measured, already-shipping behavior... made honest under the corrected representation," which is the correctness/contract framing the owner asked to confirm, not retract. No sentence required correction under this finding; the check is recorded here per the owner's instruction to state it either way.

## ROW 376 -- batching 32 cached_attention dispatches into ONE command buffer confirms the kernel IS bandwidth-bound like llama's, at a ceiling ~20x below llama's at matched KV bytes

**Card:** none (measurement only, docs-only row plus one harness rewrite). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-r376`, `docs/row-376-attention-batched`, off `main` at `943b099` (ROW 375's own commit).

**Question this row answers.** ROW 375's own per-dispatch reading was withdrawn (addendum above): its `attention_positions` came from a bind call SEPARATE from the one `execute_plan_named_op_timed` actually dispatches from, so its summed records were never shown to be `cached_attention` records at all. This row replaces that harness (`omega/tests/row_375_cached_attention_bare.rs` renamed in place to `row_376_cached_attention_batched.rs`) with a measurement that (a) selects every summed record by its OWN `kind` field, from the SAME call that produced it, asserting the count on every repeat, and (b) reads GPU time off ONE shared command buffer for the whole plan, the `rmsnorm_fused_epilogue_cost.rs` (ROW 368/372) batching shape, instead of one command buffer per op.

**Method.** New library function `omega::metal::execute_plan_timed`/`execute_plan_named_timed` (`omega/src/metal.rs`, `instrument`-gated): identical encode loop to `execute_plan` (one `MTLComputeCommandEncoder`, `endEncoding()` once), but reads `command_buffer.GPUStartTime()`/`GPUEndTime()` once after `waitUntilCompleted()` and returns that total alongside `Evaluated`, mirroring `execute_plan_op_timed`'s existing per-op timing readout at the whole-buffer granularity instead. The test harness builds the SAME real openchat decode shape ROW 375 used (32 query heads, 8 kv heads, head_dim 128, GQA group 4, `NumericPolicy::llama_relaxed()`, merged-KV `cached_key_rows=0`, `mistral_single_range_cached_forward_program`, `feed_forward=256`/`vocab=64` shrunk, `block_count=32`) at three context lengths (40, 512, 4096; the 4096 cell's ~1 GiB KV cache roots are synthesized once via the same `Lcg`-seeded `random_vec` every other cell already uses, then reused across all `REPEATS` timed executions). Per cell, two loops share the SAME `plan`: a BATCHED loop (`execute_plan_named_timed`, warm-up + median-of-7) reporting `total_gpu_ns / 32`, and a VALIDATION loop (`execute_plan_named_op_timed`, warm-up + median-of-7) that filters its returned `Vec<OpGpuTiming>` to `kind == "cached_attention"`, asserts the filtered count `== 32` on every one of the 7 repeats (this assertion is what makes the summed records provably attention records, closing ROW 375's gap), and reports the filtered sum `/ 32`.

**Quiet gate.** THREE-check gate (names-only pgrep, `pgrep -fl 'while true' | grep -v pgrep`, load-1 < 10) run before the build and before each of the three timed cells. Build: pgrep empty, load-1 not checked (build only, no GPU contention risk). Context-40: first check hit both a live `cargo-nextest` (another agent) and load-1 44.95 -- WAITED (not the addendum's single retry, since the process-name check also failed and the addendum's retry allowance is load-1-only); rechecked at 30s (names clear, load-1 36.74), 90s (load-1 24.00), 140s (load-1 10.41), 160s (load-1 7.88, PASS, no other-agent processes). Context-512: names clear but load-1 14.02 -- one 30s retry per the addendum, load-1 9.77 at retry, PASS. Context-4096: pgrep empty, load-1 7.56, PASS on first check.

**Data -- batched (one command buffer, whole 32-layer plan, `total_gpu_ns / 32`) vs the kind-validated per-op cross-check (`execute_plan_named_op_timed`, filtered to `kind == "cached_attention"`, exactly 32 records asserted on every one of 7 repeats, every cell):**

| context | dispatches | batched us/dispatch (median, cov%) | per-op kind-validated us/dispatch (median, cov%) | kv bytes/dispatch (f32 K+V) | GB/s (kind-validated) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 40 | 32 | 6076.191 (0.55%) | 47.194 (24.56%) | 327,680 | 6.94 |
| 512 | 32 | 6371.583 (3.44%) | 329.072 (7.55%) | 4,194,304 | 12.75 |
| 4096 | 32 | 8504.887 (1.55%) | 2620.217 (1.94%) | 33,554,432 | 12.81 |

**The batched column is NOT an attention-isolated number and is reported as such.** It is the whole 32-layer plan's total GPU time divided by 32 -- one decode layer's full cost (QKV/O projections, FFN, embedding lookup, vocab head, AND the one `cached_attention` dispatch), not the attention kernel alone; it stays near-flat (~6.1-8.5ms) across a 102x KV-byte change because the projection matmuls (fixed size, independent of context length) dominate it at every context in this range. This is the mechanism reason `execute_plan_named_timed`'s number cannot answer ROW 375's question by itself, and why the kind-validated per-op cross-check (which DOES isolate the `cached_attention` dispatches, at the cost of returning to a per-op command buffer for that one measurement) is the number reported below against llama.

**Reading, ours vs llama (llama's numbers reused from ROW 375, not re-run -- both invocations are one command line, MEASURED there, reuse is the brief's own stated fallback):**

| shape | us/dispatch | KV bytes | GB/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ours, context=40 (f32) | 47.194 | 327,680 | 6.94 |
| ours, context=512 (f32) | 329.072 | 4,194,304 | 12.75 |
| ours, context=4096 (f32) | 2620.217 | 33,554,432 | 12.81 |
| llama, kv=4096 (f16) | 65.78 | 16,777,216 | 255.0 |
| llama, kv=8192 (f16) | 132.11 | 33,554,432 | 254.0 |

**Ours IS bandwidth-bound like llama's, at a ceiling ~20x below llama's -- an f32-vs-f16 byte-count difference cannot explain that ratio.** Both sides scale close to linearly with KV bytes at the two larger points: llama's kv=4096->8192 is a 2.00x byte change for a 2.01x time change (GB/s flat, 255.0->254.0); ours' context=512->4096 is a 8.00x byte change for a 7.96x time change (GB/s flat, 12.75->12.81) -- the same bandwidth-bound signature ROW 375 could not establish for either side. At MATCHED bytes (llama kv=8192, f16, 33,554,432 bytes == ours context=4096, f32, 33,554,432 bytes -- llama reads the same context in half the elements at twice the per-element width, landing on the identical byte count), llama is 2620.217 / 132.11 = **19.83x faster**, and the GB/s ratio (254.0 / 12.81 = 19.83x) is the same number, as it must be at equal bytes. Halving ours' bytes (f32->f16 KV, an actual codec the fixture does not exercise this row) would only close 2x of that 19.83x -- the remaining ~10x is a genuine kernel/access-pattern gap (candidates named, not isolated: the serial per-chunk loop over `keys_per_chunk=16`/`cap=4`, or per-key scalar work vs llama's SIMD-group-cooperative body), not a precision/byte-count difference. At context=40, the per-op-timed reading (47.194us) exceeds what the ctx512/4096 bandwidth line predicts for 327,680 bytes at ~12.8 GB/s (327,680 / 12.8e9 = 25.6us) by about 21.6us -- consistent with a per-dispatch fixed floor (roughly 20-25us) that a bandwidth-only model does not capture at small context, shrinking to a small fraction of the total by context=512 (25.6us of ours' bandwidth-predicted floor against a 329.072us measured total is under 8%).

**Per-token derived cost (x32 layers), beside ROW 358's own ablation delta (labeled as such -- ROW 358's 1.094ms is the FULL-minus-`!cached_attention` in-program delta, a subtraction that changes dependency/synchronization structure, not a direct measurement of the attention kernel's own execution time in isolation):**

- Ours, context=40, kind-validated: 47.194us x 32 = **1.510ms/token** -- DERIVED, at a context (~40 keys) comparable to ROW 358's own real-checkpoint step-3 context (~34-40 keys).
- ROW 358's own ablation delta, same context regime: **1.094ms/token** -- MEASURED (ROW 358), an in-program FULL-vs-ablated subtraction, not "attention's in-program execution cost" in isolation.
- Ratio: 1.510 / 1.094 = **1.38x** -- this row's kind-validated synthetic-fixture number and ROW 358's real-checkpoint ablation delta now sit within the same order of magnitude (both ~1-1.5ms/token at matched context), unlike ROW 375's withdrawn bare numbers (22.469-22.711ms/token, 13-20x higher than ROW 358's line) -- the kind-validation fix changes this comparison from a 13-20x disagreement to a 1.38x one, itself evidence the withdrawn records were not attention records.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) The batched (whole-plan) number's own FFN/embedding/projection share is not decomposed by this row -- ROW 358's own kind-count table (32 cached_attention, 194 elementwise, 66 reduce-cooperative, 224 reduce-packed-row-blocked, 2 constant, 2 iota at a real checkpoint) is the closest existing per-kind breakdown, but it is a different plan (real 4096-wide checkpoint, not this row's synthetic 256-wide FFN/64-wide vocab fixture) and is not re-derived here. (2) The remaining ~1.38x gap between this row's kind-validated 1.510ms/token and ROW 358's 1.094ms ablation delta is not resolved -- candidates named, none confirmed: an ablation delta and a direct per-op sum are not the same quantity even when both are correctly attributed (the ablation delta also nets out any barrier/hazard-overhead change from removing 32 dispatches, which a per-op sum cannot see either way), and this row's synthetic fixture's context (~40 keys exactly) is not proven identical to ROW 358's real-checkpoint step-3 context (named as "~34-40 keys", not exact). (3) The ~10x kernel/access-pattern gap beyond the f32/f16 byte factor is named, not isolated to a specific loop or instruction -- no AIR/instruction-count read of the `cached_attention` kernel body was attempted this row (the ROW 368 method: `xcrun metal -S -emit-llvm` over the emitted MSL, ROW 368/`msl.rs`'s own emitter -- a natural next row). (4) `execute_plan_named_timed` (the new whole-plan-timed function) has no dedicated unit test of its own beyond this integration-shaped GPU cell; it duplicates `execute_plan`'s encode loop by construction (same reasoning `execute_plan_op_timed` already uses for its own per-op duplication) and does not handle the `metal-buffer-pool` feature's reclaim path (unexercised by this test's feature set; a caller building under `metal-buffer-pool` gets ordinary buffer drops, not pool reclaim, from this diagnostic-only function).

## ROW 377 -- the single-range builder now takes the SAME architecture inputs as its two-range sibling and derives its rope pairing from `qk_norm.is_some()`; a qk-norm checkpoint now takes the placed-KV fast path on Metal instead of ROW 373's fallback

**Card:** `feat(tensor): single-range layer takes qk-norm and derives its rope pairing` + `feat(interop): qk-norm checkpoints use the placed-kv path` + `docs(tensor): row 377 single-range builder honors qk-norm`. **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-srq`, `feat/single-range-qk-norm`.

**The class item ROW 373 named, landed.** `append_mistral_single_range_cached_layer` (`proxima-tensor/src/spec.rs:3841`) took `qk_norm: bool` and used it only to reject; it now takes `qk_norm: Option<(NodeId, NodeId, NodeId)>` -- the identical shape (q-norm weight, k-norm weight, `inv_head_dim`) `append_mistral_cached_layer`'s own `qk_norm` parameter has always taken. `Some` runs the same `rmsnorm_per_head` calls on `q_raw`/`k_new_raw` before RoPE the two-range sibling runs, and selects `RopePairing::SplitHalf { pairs }` vs `RopePairing::Interleaved` from `qk_norm.is_some()` through the existing `fused_rope_pair` helper -- both branches copied node-for-node from `append_mistral_cached_layer`'s own `qk_norm` match (`spec.rs:2746-2823`), not reimplemented. `TensorError::UnsupportedInBuilder`'s rejection branch is gone from this builder entirely (the type stays -- other builders and this crate's own test still use it for whatever they genuinely cannot express). `mistral_single_range_cached_forward_program` (the public entry) now builds `inv_head_dim`/`q_norm_weight`/`k_norm_weight` per layer when `qk_norm: bool` is `true`, the same `qk_norm.then(...)` guard `mistral_cached_forward_program_with_experts` already uses so a dense (non-qk-norm) checkpoint's own node count is unaffected.

**Interop side: no call-site change needed.** `build_single_range_program` (`proxima-model-interop/src/generate.rs:752`) already passed `qk_norm: bool` straight through to `mistral_single_range_cached_forward_program` and mapped `Err(TensorError::UnsupportedInBuilder) => Ok(None)`. With the builder no longer erroring on `qk_norm=true`, that `match` arm simply never fires for a qk-norm checkpoint anymore -- `Ok(Some(SingleRangeProgram))` flows through unchanged, and `LoadedModel::run_decode_loop`'s existing `self.single_range.is_some()` branch (`generate.rs:2235`) takes the placed-KV path on the next Metal decode. Both stale comment blocks describing the ROW 372 rejection (`generate.rs`'s call site doc, `build_single_range_program`'s own doc) were rewritten to state the current behavior.

**Census.** `single_range_layer_binds_qk_norm_with_two_extra_per_head_norm_reduces` (`proxima-tensor::spec::tests`) replaces ROW 372's rejection test: builds the single-range layer with `qk_norm=false` and `qk_norm=true` from the same `single_range_layer_with_order` fixture (now building `qk_norm_weights: Option<(NodeId, NodeId, NodeId)>` and threading `head_dim` through) and asserts the qk-norm program carries exactly `+2` `Op::Reduce` and `+14` `Op::Elementwise` over the plain program -- `rmsnorm_per_head`'s own body is 1 reduce + 7 elementwise per call, twice (q, k), and nothing else moves.

**Bit-identity / tolerance.** `a_single_range_decode_step_with_qk_norm_matches_the_two_range_decode_step` mirrors the existing `a_single_range_decode_step_matches_the_two_range_decode_step` harness exactly (prefill via the two-range oracle, fold the decode step's own rotated K/V onto the merged cache by hand, run both programs, compare logits), with `qwen3_cached_forward_program` (two-range, `qk_norm=true` always) as the oracle, `mistral_single_range_cached_forward_program(.., qk_norm: true, ..)` as the candidate, and `attn_q_norm.weight`/`attn_k_norm.weight` (random, non-degenerate) added per layer. Result: `normalized_error < 1e-4` held at all three cases (`cached_len, new_count` = `(0,1)`, `(1,1)`, `(6,2)`) -- the same tolerance bar the plain-layer parity test already established for this codebase's online-softmax-combine-vs-one-shot-reduce distinction (not required to be 0-ULP, only numerically equivalent). Not measured as exactly bit-identical; the normalized-error bound is the honest claim.

**Qwen3 Metal fixture, path confirmed.** Added `LoadedModel::takes_placed_kv_path` (`#[cfg(test)]`-gated `pub(crate)` accessor, `self.single_range.is_some()`) and asserted it `true` at the top of `qwen3_split_half_rope_cpu_and_metal_greedy_decode_match` before ROW 373 this was structurally impossible (the builder rejected `qk_norm=true`, forcing `single_range = None`). ## ROW 378 -- the CPU's own cross-backend parity reference was itself lossy (`q{4,5,6}k-int8-dot`'s Q8_K activation quantization), so every prior Metal-vs-CPU drift number partly measured the CPU's own noise, not Metal's

**Card:** `feat(tensor): cpu evaluation can request exact activations` + `test(interop): parity harnesses compare metal against the exact cpu reference`. **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-exact`, `feat/exact-cpu-reference`.

**The finding.** `q4k-int8-dot`/`q5k-int8-dot`/`q6k-int8-dot` are default-on and forced on by `std` via `cohort-staged-graph` (`proxima-tensor/Cargo.toml:29` -> `:186`); every one of this crate's Q4_K/Q5_K/Q6_K CPU dots quantizes its activation to Q8_K before dotting. Metal's own kernels dot directly against `f32` activations -- exact against an f64 dequant reference to within fp32 rounding. Every cross-backend harness (`quality::metal_vs_cpu_reports_real_drift`, the qwen3 split-half-rope counterpart, `dense_metal_*_matches_cpu`) was therefore comparing Metal against a LOSSY CPU reference, misattributing the CPU's own Q8_K quantization error to Metal.

**The fix, no new type.** `run_reduce_quantized` (`proxima-tensor/src/cpu.rs`) took a new `exact_activations: bool` parameter, threaded through `run_reduce_with_quantized_weights`/`run_node_into`/the `evaluate_quantized_with_scratch` loop (12 pre-existing call sites in `cpu.rs` pass `false`, unchanged behavior). `false` (every existing caller) keeps today's `q{4,5,6}k-int8-dot` wide-fold path; `true` skips that wide fold and the per-position match falls through to the exact `matmul_q4k_f32`/`matmul_q5k_f32`/`matmul_q6k_f32` dequantize-then-fold kernels regardless of which int8-dot features are compiled in. New public entry points mirror the existing four 1:1: `evaluate_quantized_exact`, `evaluate_quantized_exact_with_scratch`, `evaluate_quantized_named_exact_with_scratch` -- no signature on any pre-existing `pub fn` changed. `omega::backend` gained the identical shape, additively: `CpuPlan.exact_activations` (new field, `false` at `plan_named_cpu`'s one construction site), `plan_named_cpu_exact`/`plan_named_exact` as siblings to `plan_named_cpu`/`plan_named` (zero existing call sites touched across omega's own ~80 `plan_named`/`execute_plan_named` test call sites). `proxima-model-interop::ServingConfig` gained `exact_activations: bool` (config-as-mirror tested the same way `numeric_policy`/`kv_bucket_tokens` already are), read once by both `BackendRuntime` impls (`metal` and non-`metal`). `quality::score_prompt` sets it unconditionally `true` on the `reference` side only -- a no-op on `Engine::Gpu` (Metal is already exact), so `default_vs_default_is_the_degenerate_control` (both sides Metal) is unaffected by construction, not by re-verifying it.

**Three-way parity, real Q4_K row (openchat-3.5-1210 `blk.0.ffn_gate.weight`, row 0), f64 dequant-then-fold reference:** `f64_reference=1.2590506492909554`, exact (`matmul_q4k_f32`) `=1.2590508` (`exact_relative_error=1.563e-7`), int8 (`matmul_q4k_q8k_f32`) `=1.2554812` (`int8_relative_error=2.835e-3`) -- **exact_activations is ~18,140x tighter against the f64 reference than the int8 fast path it replaces**, on this one real row.

**Cross-backend harness, real device.** `quality::real_openchat_file::metal_vs_cpu_reports_real_drift` (real openchat-3.5-1210 checkpoint, real Metal device) passed with the CPU reference now built via `exact_activations: true`. Run without `--nocapture` under a loaded box (another agent's `cargo`/`rustc` observed mid-run); the `quality_summary` line (`kl_max`/`kl_mean`/`exact_match_rate`/`top1_agreement_rate` old-lossy-reference-vs-new-exact-reference) was NOT captured this pass -- residual below, not fabricated.

**Residuals, named not hidden.** (1) The `quality_summary` printed line for `metal_vs_cpu_reports_real_drift`/`qwen3_split_half_rope_metal_vs_cpu_reports_real_drift` under the new exact reference was not captured (test passed; stdout was captured by the test harness, no `--nocapture` run completed before this row closed) -- a follow-up run with `--nocapture` should report the old-vs-new `kl_max` numbers directly, the expectation (not yet measured) being an order-of-magnitude-or-more drop matching the CPU-only three-way finding above. (2) `dense_metal_*_matches_cpu` (`tests/capability_matrix.rs`) assert exact greedy-id/text equality on a tiny synthetic checkpoint, not a numeric drift metric -- left unchanged; `exact_activations` has no assertion surface there to wire into without also changing what those tests assert. (3) `q3_k_m_variant_against_q4_k_s_reference_reports_real_drift` (cross-checkpoint, not cross-backend) was not run or wired -- out of this row's stated scope (Metal-vs-CPU, not checkpoint-vs-checkpoint).

## ROW 379 -- ROW 376's batched-dispatch bandwidth floor holds after porting cached-attention onto a runtime chunk count and a block-staged Q·K/softmax/V loop; the chunk cap has no headroom left before Metal's 32 KiB threadgroup-memory ceiling

**Card:** `perf(omega): cached-attention row counts read from a runtime uniform` (`6c48b22f`) + `perf(omega): attention chunk count is runtime; one pipeline serves every kv bucket` (`67dbf0bd`) + `perf(omega): attention stages a key block's scores and reduces once per block` (`4086ceda`). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-attnv`, `perf/attention-vec-lowering`.

**The three port slices.** (1) `6c48b22f` moves `render_cached_attention`'s row counts (`cached_key_rows`/`new_key_rows`) off compile-time constants baked per shape onto a runtime uniform buffer (`metal.rs` uploads it, `msl.rs` reads it) -- one compiled pipeline now serves every KV bucket instead of one per shape. (2) `67dbf0bd` does the same for `context_chunks_for`'s chunk count: `ATTENTION_CONTEXT_CHUNK_CAP` (`sized.rs`, build-time constant per principle 12) bounds the runtime uniform, so the same compiled kernel serves `chunks=1..cap` without recompiling. (3) `4086ceda` adds the block-staged Q·K/softmax/V body (`block_width_for`, gated on `NumericRewrite::TreeReduce`): `block_width` sequential keys are staged into `threadgroup float ss[]` and the online-softmax combine (`simd_max`/`simd_sum`) fires once per block instead of once per key, mirroring llama.cpp's `kernel_flash_attn_ext_vec` `C`-keys-per-block staging (`ggml-metal.metal:4016-4017`). `block_width=1` renders byte-identical to the pre-port sequential body (`block_staged_attention_holds_parity_at_context_{40,512,4096}`, new tests in the same commit, all pass).

**Cap sweep, `OMEGA_ATTENTION_CONTEXT_CHUNKS_CAP`, `attention_context_chunks_batched` (`row_376_cached_attention_batched.rs`), context_length ∈ {40, 512, 4096}, `per_op_timed_kind_validated_us_per_dispatch: mean`:**

| cap | 40 (µs / GB/s) | 512 (µs / GB/s) | 4096 (µs / GB/s) | static threadgroup bytes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4 (ROW 376 baseline) | 43.2 / 7.58 | 269 / 15.59 | 2295 / 14.62 | 10368 (10.1 KiB) |
| 12 (largest that fits) | 43.5 / 7.53 | 274.9 / 15.26 | 2275.2 / 14.75 | 31104 (30.375 KiB) |
| 32 (requested) | REJECTED -- `CompileFailed { log: "Compiler encountered an internal error" }` at pipeline warm-up | -- | -- | 82944 (81 KiB) |
| llama.cpp (`kernel_flash_attn_ext_vec`) | -- | -- | 65.8 / 255 | -- |

Static threadgroup memory is `qg * cap * bw * 4` (`ss[]`) `+ 2 * qg * cap * 4` (`shared_m`/`shared_l`) `+ qg * cap * hd * 4` (`shared_o`) bytes, `qg=query_groups=4`, `bw=block_width=32` (`omega-runtime.toml`'s `[attention_block]`, `TreeReduce` granted), `hd=head_dim=128` -- `= 2592 * cap` bytes. `cap=12` is the largest integer under Metal's 32 KiB (32768-byte) static per-threadgroup limit (`2592*12=31104`); `cap=13` already exceeds it (`33696`). `cap=32` (`82944` bytes, 2.53x the limit) fails at Metal pipeline-state creation, matching the byte math directly -- no ambiguity about which side of the limit it's on.

**Occupancy reading.** `cap=12`'s GB/s (7.53 / 15.26 / 14.75) is flat against `cap=4`'s (7.58 / 15.59 / 14.62) -- every delta is inside the ~2-11% CoV band `row_376`'s own harness reports for these cells (not a regression, not a win). Tripling the simdgroup-merge width bought nothing: the bottleneck this kernel pays for is not cross-simdgroup online-softmax merge occupancy, it's the per-dispatch structure underneath both cap values -- the same residual `ROW 376` named (a ceiling ~20x below llama's at matched KV bytes, `14.6-15.3 GB/s` vs llama's `255 GB/s`). **Kept `cap=4`** (`omega-runtime.toml`'s `[attention_context_chunks]` `cap = 4` unchanged, no commit for this slice) -- there is no evidence a higher cap earns its extra threadgroup memory. Next instrument: profile the per-dispatch structure directly (Metal GPU frame capture on one `cached_attention` dispatch) to find where the ~17x gap to llama's GB/s concentrates, rather than sweeping `cap` further; V's float4 accumulation (the register-resident weighted-value fold, currently scalar-per-`dimension`) is the next slice to land, not another cap value.

**Crossing counters, step 2 and step 34 (`token_breakdown_metal`'s per-decode-step `pipeline_hits`/`pipeline_misses`/`pipeline_compile_ms`), all six oracle rounds below:** every round, both A (main) and B (branch), reports `pipeline_hits=454 pipeline_misses=1` at BOTH step 2 and step 34 -- the one miss per step is each step's own steady-state per-op cache-population cost (`op_setup_calls=455`, one op not yet resident), identical in shape and count on both sides. `pipeline_compile_ms` at step 34: A1 `0.355125`, A2 `0.360208`, A3 `0.380`; B1 `0.395875`, B2 `0.412291`, B3 `0.382708` -- same order of magnitude, no branch-introduced recompile.

## ROW 380 -- the split kernel decoded `tgid` against the LIVE `u.splits` instead of the compiled grid multiplier, so a below-max split count corrupted device memory past the token-embedding gather

**Card:** `fix(omega): attention split decode uses the grid's multiplier, idle threadgroups write nothing`. **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-split`, `perf/attention-key-splits`.

**The crash.** `row_376_cached_attention_batched::cached_attention_batched_context_512` (`splits_for(512) = 4`, `ATTENTION_SPLIT_MAX = 32`) panicked intermittently: `Tensor(GatherIndexOutOfRange { node: NodeId(2), index: 3242016549, extent: 64 })` (`bare-cell-512.log`) -- a garbage index into the token-embedding gather, i.e. a PRIOR dispatch corrupted device memory. Context 40 (`splits_for = 1`, no merge) and 4096 (`splits_for` clamps to `ATTENTION_SPLIT_MAX = 32`, so live equals compiled) ran clean 7/7 -- the failure was isolated to exactly the case where the live split count is BELOW the compiled maximum.

**Root cause, `omega/src/msl.rs:3415` (pre-fix) x `omega/src/metal.rs:4339-4367`.** `grid_threads`' `CachedAttention` arm (`msl.rs:2405-2413`) widens the dispatch grid by the compiled constant `ATTENTION_SPLIT_MAX` (32) whenever `cached_attention_merge_needed` holds, and `pack_cached_attention_uniforms` (`metal.rs:4339`) uploads `u.splits` as the LIVE `splits_for` result (4 at context 512) -- both correct and intentional (`metal.rs:4384-85`'s own doc: `u.splits` must be the live count for the slice math). The bug: the split kernel's `tgid` decode also divided by this SAME live `splits` (`long split = query_row_and_split % splits; long query_row = query_row_and_split / splits;`, old `msl.rs:3401`), not the compiled multiplier the grid was actually built with. The dispatched grid always contains `rows * kv_heads * 32` threadgroups; decoding with modulus 4 instead of 32 means every `tgid` past the first `rows * kv_heads * 4` wraps `query_row` into `0..rows*8` instead of `0..rows`, so threadgroups past the real row range read Q/K/V out of bounds and their `final_store` scratch write (`(query_index * max_splits + split) * (2 + head_dim)`, `query_index` built from the wrapped `query_row`) lands outside the scratch allocation, into whatever buffer Metal placed next -- corrupting the token-embedding ids buffer the next op's gather read.

**Proof, not inference.** (1) Read both sides of the boundary: `grid_threads` multiplies by `crate::sized::ATTENTION_SPLIT_MAX` (`msl.rs:2409`), `pack_cached_attention_uniforms` uploads the live `splits_for` (`metal.rs:4339,4387`) -- two DIFFERENT values feeding the SAME kernel's decode and dispatch. (2) `split_kernel_emits_the_slice_formula_and_scratch_index` (`msl.rs`, new assertions) renders the fixture at `cached_attention_op_dynamic(200, 56)` (256-key context, `splits_for(256, keys_per_split=128) = 2`, still below `ATTENTION_SPLIT_MAX = 32`) and pins the pre-fix decode text (`long split = query_row_and_split % splits;` -- the live field, confirmed present before the fix by re-running the test against the unmodified source). (3) The 512-context cell reproduced the panic on the FIRST run (`bare-cell-512.log`, 6.48s, panicked on the 6th of 7 repeats) and again on retry with a DIFFERENT garbage index (`index=1097602797` vs `index=3242016549`, `bare-cell-512-retry.log`) -- consistent with reading whatever value the prior corrupting write happened to leave, not a fixed off-by-one.

**Fix.** `msl.rs:3401-3419`: compute `merge_needed` once (shared with `final_store`'s own branch, single source of truth), decode `tgid` against `constexpr long grid_splits = {ATTENTION_SPLIT_MAX or 1}` -- the SAME constant `grid_threads` multiplied the grid by -- instead of the live `u.splits`, and add `if (split >= splits) { return; }` so an idle threadgroup (`split` past the live count but still inside the widened compiled grid) returns before touching Q/K/V or scratch. No identity partial is written for an idle split: the merge kernel already reads only `i < u.splits` (`msl.rs`'s merge body, `own_max = (iwg < splits) ? in0[...] : -INFINITY`), so an unwritten idle slot is never read. Chose grid-side decode (not widening the grid to the live `splits` at encode time) because `ATTENTION_SPLIT_MAX` is already the one compile-time constant three call sites agree on -- the grid width (`grid_threads`), the scratch stride (`final_store`'s `max_splits`), and now the decode -- widening the grid to a runtime value would need a fourth site to derive independently and lose that single source of truth. `metal.rs:4382-4387`'s doc comment corrected to stop implying the live value governs "split extraction" (`tgid` decode) -- it never should have.

**20-repeat reproduction, post-fix, `cached_attention_batched_context_512` (7 repeats/invocation x 3 invocations = 21 total):** all 3 rounds `ok`, 0 panics (`fix-512-round{1,2,3}.log`).

**Bare cells, post-fix, `per_op_timed_kind_validated_us_per_dispatch: median` (`--nocapture`, dedicated single-test runs):**

| context | median µs | cov | kv_bytes/dispatch | effective GB/s (median-based) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 40 | 43.637 | 8.28% | 327680 | 7.51 |
| 512 | 89.524 | 14.88% | 4194304 | 46.85 |
| 4096 | 519.436 | 8.94% | 33554432 | 64.61 |

512 and 4096 now run at all (pre-fix, 512 panicked before producing a number); both are well above ROW 379's pre-split baseline (15.59 / 14.62 GB/s at cap=4, no split) because this branch's whole point -- splitting the live key range across threadgroups -- is now safe to exercise at every split count, not only at the two split counts (1 and 32) that happened not to trigger the bug.

Mean `gpu_exec_ms` at `3..7`: A `20.545`, B `20.576` (+0.15%, inside both arms' own ~1.35% CoV, and the per-round sign flips: B1 < A1, B2 > A2 by 0.03, B3 > A3 by 0.16) -- not a systematic regression. **Caveat, named not hidden:** this fixture's context length tops out at 95 over 64 decode steps (`context_length=95` max observed), below `keys_per_split=128`, so `splits_for` never exceeds 1 here -- this oracle exercises the common (`grid_splits=1`) path's lack of regression, not the split path the bug lived in. The split path's own correctness and no-crash proof is the 21-repeat reproduction above plus `block_staged_attention_holds_parity_at_context_512`, which DOES cross the threshold (`splits_for(512)=4`) and holds `relative < 1e-4` parity against the bit-exact sequential kernel post-fix (gate run below).

## ROW 381 -- `keys_per_split` 128 -> 16 wins the decode scoreboard window (36.1us vs 43.6us bare, beyond 2x CoV) at the cost of a 68% regression at 512 keys; the fixture's own greedy text and gpu_exec hold across the trade

**Card:** `perf(omega): attention splits fire at the decode window`. **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-r381`, `perf/row-381-split-sizing`, off `main` at `433ae2fb` (ROW 380's own commit).

**Question.** ROW 380 fixed the split kernel's correctness; this row asks whether a smaller `[attention_splits] keys_per_split` moves ROW 376's own scoreboard window (39-78 live keys), where the shipped default (128) clamps `splits_for` to 1 -- one dispatch, no scratch, no merge -- for the whole window.

**Ladder, bare `per_op_timed_kind_validated_us_per_dispatch: median`, kind-validated, median-of-7, `--test-threads=1`** (`row_376_cached_attention_batched`, `omega/tests/row_376_cached_attention_batched.rs`), rebuilt per cell via `OMEGA_ATTENTION_SPLITS_KEYS_PER_SPLIT=<n>` (the brief's own `OMEGA_ATTENTION_SPLIT_KEYS_PER_SPLIT` has no trailing `S` on `SPLITS` and does not match `proxima-build/src/sizing.rs`'s `<PREFIX>_<SECTION>_<KEY>` naming for `[attention_splits]` -- using it silently falls through to the TOML default and would have produced three cells all still running at 128; caught by reading `omega_sized.rs`'s generated constant after each build, not assumed):

| keys_per_split | context | splits | median us | cov | vs 128 baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 128 (ROW 380 baseline) | 40 | 1 | 43.637 | 8.28% | -- |
| 128 (ROW 380 baseline) | 512 | 4 | 89.524 | 14.88% | -- |
| 16 | 40 | 3 | 36.132 | 5.20% | -17.1%, delta 7.47us > 2x CoV (3.76us) -- **clears** |
| 16 | 512 | 32 | 150.867 | 10.07% | +68.5%, regression |
| 8 | 40 | 5 | 41.812 | 12.63% | -4.1%, delta 1.79us < 2x CoV (10.55us) -- does not clear |

`keys_per_split=16` is the only candidate that beats 128 at the scoreboard window beyond 2x CoV; `8` is statistically indistinguishable from 128 at this window (more splits, more per-threadgroup fixed overhead, no net win). `16` at 512 keys forces `splits=32` (vs 128's `4`) -- 8x the split count and 8x the merge-dispatch/scratch-write traffic, which loses badly at that shape. Per the brief's own rule (beat 128 at 40 keys beyond 2x CoV -> land it), `keys_per_split=16` is kept; the 512-key regression is accepted because the decode window (repeat single-token generation) is the hot path this crosses far more often than a 512-key prompt-processing shape.

**Change.** `omega/omega-runtime.toml`'s `[attention_splits] keys_per_split` 128 -> 16, doc comment updated with the measured trade. Two unit tests in `omega/src/msl.rs` asserted the OLD invariant ("a 40-key context never splits under llama_relaxed") as a byte-identical-output guarantee -- both rewritten to assert the policy-split correctly: `bit_exact()` still never splits at any `keys_per_split` (it withholds `ContextSplitMerge` outright); `llama_relaxed()` now splits a 40-key context into 3 (`forty_keys_stays_one_split_under_bit_exact_but_splits_under_llama_relaxed`, `forty_key_plan_stays_one_kernel_under_bit_exact_but_splits_under_llama_relaxed`).

**Oracle, A (main `433ae2fb`) / B (this branch), `PROXIMA_MAX_TOKENS=64`, `bind::real_openchat_file::runs_the_cached_decode_loop_on_the_metal_backend_and_reports_the_plan_cache`, one round (budget-limited, see Residual):**

| | step 3..7 gpu_exec_ms range | step 2 barriers | step 34 barriers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A (main) | 20.880-21.406 | 290 | 290 |
| B (branch) | 20.175-20.219 | 322 | 322 |

`generated_text` md5 identical both arms: `84c7519e6bffea98476fefd9d545a0fc` (matches ROW 380's own baseline hash). B's `barriers` count is +32 at every step sampled -- the merge dispatch's hazard-tracking edges, consistent with `cached_attention_merge_needed` now holding at this fixture's live capacity (`cached_len_before=33` at step 3, `context_length=34`, `splits_for(34, 16)=3 > 1`) where it did not at `keys_per_split=128` (`splits_for(34,128)=1`). Despite the added merge dispatch, B's `gpu_exec_ms` range at 3..7 sits entirely BELOW A's, not above -- decision rule (md5 identical AND B not above A's range) is met.

**Flip decision: FLIPPED.** `keys_per_split=16` lands.

## ROW 382 -- V accumulates as float4 per `ty` group with a `simd_shuffle_xor` cross-group reduce; wins big at 4096 keys, flat at 40, a real regression at 512 under ROW 381's own `keys_per_split=16`

**Card:** `perf(omega): attention accumulates v as float4 per ty group with a final cross-group reduce`. **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-vacc`, `perf/attention-v-float4`, rebased onto `main` at `136002bd` (ROW 381's own commit; the branch's original base, `433ae2fb`, moved out from under it mid-session).

**The V layout finding.** The block-staged Q·K stage already loads Q/K as `float4` via `kbase` (the pair-packed rotate-half layout, `kbase = (cached ? key : new_index) * (kv_heads * (head_dim / 2)) + kv_head * (head_dim / 2)`); V's layout is different -- unrotated, `head_dim` contiguous floats per key at `kbase * 2` -- so the SAME `kbase` computed for Q·K reinterprets cleanly as a `float4` V pointer only by doubling it (`kbase * 2`), never re-deriving a second base. This is llama's own `kernel_flash_attn_ext_vec` register form (`ggml-metal.metal:4125-4143`): each of the 4 `ty` groups (8 `tx` lanes each, splitting the 32-lane simdgroup 4-ways) loads its OWN `float4` chunk of V for its OWN assigned key, accumulates in registers across the 8-key block, then the 4 `ty` groups' partials are folded together by a butterfly `simd_shuffle_xor` reduce (strides 8, then 16) before landing in `shared_o` -- the same scratch array the merge step already reads, reused rather than doubled (`omega/src/msl.rs`'s own doc comment on the now-hoisted `threadgroup float shared_o[...]` declaration, this landing's own move: declared once above the `block_width` branch instead of once per policy arm, since both arms read it identically).

**The emitted V loop and reduce (`head_dim % 32 == 0`).**
```
constexpr long v_registers = head_dim / 8 / 4;
float4 v_acc[v_registers] = {float4(0.0f), ...};
for (long cc4 = 0L; cc4 < 8L; cc4++) {
    long local_index = block_start + sub + 4L * cc4 + (long)ty;
    bool valid = local_index < min(block_start + sub + 32L, num_local_keys);
    ... kbase computed exactly as the scalar form did ...
    float key_weight = valid ? ss[...] : 0.0f;
    device const float4* v4 = (device const float4*)((cached ? in6 : in7) + kbase * 2);
    for (register_index in 0..v_registers) { v_acc[register_index] += valid ? float4(v4[tx + 8 * register_index]) * key_weight : float4(0.0f); }
}
for (register_index in 0..v_registers) {
    v_acc[register_index] += simd_shuffle_xor(v_acc[register_index], 8);
    v_acc[register_index] += simd_shuffle_xor(v_acc[register_index], 16);
}
if (ty == 0) { shared_o4[tx + 8 * register_index] = v_acc[register_index]; }  // per register_index
simdgroup_barrier(mem_flags::mem_threadgroup);
weighted[local_dimension] += shared_o[local_group_index * head_dim + dimension];  // lane-strided read-back
simdgroup_barrier(mem_flags::mem_threadgroup);
```

**The alignment fallback.** `head_dim % 32 != 0` (this crate's `head_dim = 8` fixtures: a multiple of 8 so Q/K's own `float4` loads stay valid, but not of 32) keeps today's scalar per-key V loop byte for byte -- `weighted[local_dimension] += key_weight * (cached ? in6[kbase * 2 + dimension] : in7[kbase * 2 + dimension]);`, unconditionally on any `dimension` stride, no `v_registers` sizing hazard. Two new tests pin both sides: `block_staged_v_accumulate_uses_float4_and_a_cross_ty_reduce_when_aligned` (`head_dim=32`, asserts the `float4` pointer, the accumulate line, both `simd_shuffle_xor` strides present, and the scalar loop line ABSENT) and `block_staged_v_accumulate_falls_back_to_scalar_when_head_dim_not_32_aligned` (`head_dim=8`, asserts the inverse).

**Rebase, conflicts hit.** `main` advanced from `433ae2fb` to `136002bd` (ROW 381: `keys_per_split` 128 -> 16) between this branch's own commit and this landing attempt. `omega/src/msl.rs` conflicted in exactly the test module's doc-comment region: ROW 381 rewrote the doc above `forty_keys_stays_one_split_under_bit_exact_but_splits_under_llama_relaxed` (old: "40 keys never split", new: "40 keys now split into 3 under `llama_relaxed`, `keys_per_split=16`"), while this branch inserted its own two new tests directly above that same test. Resolved by keeping ROW 381's updated doc-comment and test body verbatim (main wins on the now-current `keys_per_split=16` fact) and re-inserting this branch's two new tests immediately before it, preserving both branches' additions with no row/test dropped.

**Bare cells, `per_op_timed_kind_validated_us_per_dispatch: median` (kind-validated, GPU time, median-of-7, `--test-threads=1`), CURRENT main sizing (`keys_per_split=16`, `max=32`, read from `omega-runtime.toml` after the rebase):**

| context | splits | median us (this branch) | cov | prior median us (same splits, no V-float4) | delta | effective GB/s (this branch, median-based) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 40 | 3 | 36.833 | 10.39% | 36.132 (ROW 381) | +1.9%, inside combined CoV (11.6%) -- flat | 8.90 |
| 512 | 32 | 170.307 | 3.68% | 150.867 (ROW 381) | **+12.9%, beyond combined CoV (10.7%) -- a real regression** | 24.63 |
| 4096 | 32 | 309.440 | 6.71% | 519.436 (ROW 380, same splits=32 since both 128 and 16 clamp to `max` at this length) | -40.4%, beyond combined CoV (10.9%) -- a real win | 108.44 |

**Mechanism (report the number that hurts first).** At 512 keys the live sizing already forces `splits=32` (ROW 381's own tradeoff), so each threadgroup's block-staged loop covers very few keys per split; the V-accumulate rewrite adds fixed per-block cost (two `simdgroup_barrier`s, a `shared_o4` write, the register-zero/fold loop) that a short per-split key range cannot amortize, so the fixed cost dominates and the cell regresses. At 4096 keys the SAME split count (32) covers ~8x more keys per split, so the same fixed per-block cost amortizes over far more accumulate iterations and the memory-throughput win (float4 V loads instead of four scalar loads per key) dominates -- the win and the loss are the same mechanism (fixed per-block overhead vs. amortized throughput) on opposite sides of "how much work does one split do." 40 keys sits at splits=3, an intermediate few-keys-per-split regime, and lands within noise of the pre-change baseline for the same reason 512 loses, just not far enough beyond CoV to call it a regression on its own.

## ROW 383 -- the split divisor has a knee: ROW 381's small divisor (16) helps only at the decode window; sweeping `max` down to 8/16 at 512/4096 keys never recovers the pre-ROW-381 speed, so the fix reinstates the ORIGINAL divisor (128) once context crosses it, rather than clamping harder on the small one

**Card:** `perf(omega): attention split count has a knee: short slices only at short context`. **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-r383`, `perf/row-383-split-rule`, off `main` at `3c66bc88` (ROW 382's own commit).

**Question.** ROW 381 lowered `keys_per_split` 128 -> 16 to fix the decode window (40 keys, splits 1 -> 3) but regressed 512 keys (splits 4 -> 32, 89.5us -> 150.9us). ROW 382's V-float4 rewrite made that regression worse (170.3us). This row asks: does capping `max` down from 32 recover the pre-ROW-381 speed at 512/4096 keys without losing the decode-window win?

**Bare cells, `per_op_timed_kind_validated_us_per_dispatch: median` (kind-validated, GPU time, median-of-7, `--test-threads=1`, `row_376_cached_attention_batched`), rebuilt per cell via `OMEGA_ATTENTION_SPLITS_MAX=<n>`, verified against the generated `omega_sized.rs` constant after each build:**

| context | max override | splits (keys_per_split=16 pre-fix) | median us | cov | vs current (max=32) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 40 | -- (ROW 381 baseline) | 3 | 36.132 | 5.20% | -- |
| 512 | -- (ROW 381 baseline, `keys_per_split`=128) | 4 | 89.524 | 14.88% | -- |
| 512 | 32 (ROW 382 baseline) | 32 | 170.307 | 3.68% | -- |
| 512 | 8 | 8 | 176.895 | 12.31% | +3.9%, inside combined CoV -- flat |
| 512 | 16 | 16 | 172.480 | 17.65% | +1.3%, inside combined CoV -- flat |
| 4096 | 32 (ROW 382 baseline) | 32 | 309.440 | 6.71% | -- |
| 4096 | 16 | 16 | 306.818 | 4.64% | -0.8%, inside combined CoV -- flat |
| 4096 | 8 | 8 | 308.187 | 4.92% | -0.4%, inside combined CoV -- flat |

**Finding: capping `max` down does not help.** At 512 keys, 8/16/32 splits all land 170-177us (all within each other's CoV) -- nowhere near the 89.5us the ORIGINAL `keys_per_split=128` divisor got at the SAME length (splits=4). At 4096 keys, 8/16/32 splits are likewise statistically indistinguishable (306-309us). This rules out "just clamp `max` lower" as the fix: the regression is not caused by *how many* splits result once splitting kicks in at 512 keys, it is caused by the *small divisor itself* engaging at a length where it never used to. The mechanism is genuinely non-monotonic in context length: more splits helps at the tiny decode window (normally one occupancy-starved threadgroup; splitting buys free parallelism) AND at huge contexts (enough keys per split to amortize the merge dispatch's fixed cost), but hurts in between (occupancy is already adequate at ~4 splits; a finer divisor only adds fixed per-split overhead with nothing to amortize it against).

**Rule.** Two divisors, not one, selected by a single length threshold that is itself the larger divisor's own value (no third threshold constant):

```
divisor(len) = keys_per_split           if len <  keys_per_split_at_scale
             = keys_per_split_at_scale  if len >= keys_per_split_at_scale
splits = clamp(ceil(len / divisor(len)), 1, max)
```

`keys_per_split = 16` (ROW 381's small divisor, unchanged), `keys_per_split_at_scale = 128` (the ORIGINAL pre-ROW-381 divisor, reinstated as the large-context rule), `max = 32` (unchanged). A third build-time key was necessary, not a fourth: the mechanism is genuinely two-regime (verified by the bare-cell sweep above finding no single divisor or `max` clamp recovers both ends), and `keys_per_split_at_scale` doubles as both the large-context divisor and the switch threshold, so no separate constant is needed for "when to switch."

**Five-length tabulation (`splits_for`, `NumericPolicy::llama_relaxed()`):**

| len | divisor used | splits | matches |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 40 | 16 (small, 40 < 128) | 3 | ROW 381's decode-window win, unchanged |
| 256 | 128 (scaled, 256 >= 128) | 2 | pre-ROW-381 behavior |
| 512 | 128 (scaled) | 4 | ROW 381's own measured-fastest cell, 89.5us |
| 1024 | 128 (scaled) | 8 | pre-ROW-381 behavior |
| 4096 | 128 (scaled) | 32 | same split count the small divisor already reached once clamped to `max`; ROW 382's -40.4% win is untouched |

**Change.** `omega/omega-runtime.toml`'s `[attention_splits]` gains `keys_per_split_at_scale = 128`; `omega/build.rs` emits `ATTENTION_SPLIT_KEYS_PER_SPLIT_AT_SCALE`; `omega/src/msl.rs`'s `splits_for` picks the divisor by `context_length < ATTENTION_SPLIT_KEYS_PER_SPLIT_AT_SCALE`. Five unit tests added/updated in `msl.rs`: `splits_for_has_a_knee_at_the_scaled_divisor_threshold` pins all five tabulated lengths; `long_contexts_split_across_more_than_one_threadgroup_under_llama_relaxed`'s doc comment corrected to name `keys_per_split_at_scale` instead of the old single `keys_per_split`; `cached_attention_two_dispatch_form_is_inert_under_bit_exact`'s doc comment likewise. `forty_keys_stays_one_split_under_bit_exact_but_splits_under_llama_relaxed` and `split_count_never_exceeds_the_compiled_maximum` needed no code change (still hold under the new rule: 40 < 128 uses the small divisor unchanged; 1,000,000 clamps to `max` either way).

(2) **The `generated_text` md5 mismatch is the extraction command, not the text.** Reproduced ROW 383's own saved oracle logs (`r383-logs/oracle_A.log`, `oracle_B.log`) with the SAME extraction method ROWs 353-382 used, `grep -o 'generated_text="[^"]*"' | md5` (a `[^"]*` match, which stops at the first embedded literal `"` -- the string contains an escaped quote, `\"Invalid input\"`, so this method truncates the field at `...if n <= 0:\n        return \"`, 171 of the field's 233 characters): both logs hash to **`84c7519e6bffea98476fefd9d545a0fc`**, matching ROWs 353-382's own quoted hash exactly, not ROW 383's reported `a62fd09e17e19a2c84261fa47d6e88e5`. Ran a fresh 64-token decode on freshly-built `bc7f6114` (`decode_main.log`) and got the identical truncated-method hash, `84c7519e6bffea98476fefd9d545a0fc`, again. The full (untruncated, greedy `.*"`) field text on both the saved ROW 383 logs and this fresh run is byte-identical: `"Here is a simple Python function that returns the nth Fibonacci number using recursion:\n\n\`\`\`python\ndef fibonacci(n):\n    if n <= 0:\n        return \"Invalid input\"\n    elif n == 1:\n        return 0\n    elif"` -- its prefix matches ROW 353's own quoted prefix, "Here is a simple Python function that returns the nth Fibon", verbatim. **Conclusion: the text did not change between `3c66bc88` and `bc7f6114`** (the only commits in that range are this row's own split-rule change and its docs commit, `git log --oneline 3c66bc88..bc7f6114`); ROW 383's `a62fd09e...` hash was produced by a different, uncross-checked extraction command applied to the same text, not a real divergence. No commit changed the generated text; nothing to attribute to any commit in the range.

(3) **Quiet A/B, replacing ROW 383's load-contaminated round.** ROW 383's own A/B attributed B (branch) reading above A (main) to host load (`load-1=3.17` at A, rising to `8+` at B). Re-ran A (detached worktree at `3c66bc88`, release, `metal,instrument`) and B (main `bc7f6114`) back-to-back on a verified-quiet box (load-1 4.4-6.4 across both runs, no builder/measurement processes, no stray loops), one round each, `gpu_exec_ms` at steps 3..7:

| arm | range |

| B (`bc7f6114`, main) | 20.235958-20.485166 |

`generated_text` md5 identical both arms (`84c7519e6bffea98476fefd9d545a0fc`, truncated-method, both logs). B's range sits at or below A's across its full span (B's own max, 20.485, is below A's own max, 20.744) -- the "B not above A" decision rule ROWs 380-382 used is met on this quiet round, reversing ROW 383's own load-contaminated reading without needing the identical-divisor argument as a substitute.

## ROW 384 -- the four small per-layer matvecs (attn_q/k/v/output) carry the SAME ~3.2x gap to llama as the large FFN shapes for Q4_K; only the Q5_K shape (attn_v) is worse, and nsg width is not its lever

**Card:** `docs(tensor): row 384 small-shape matvecs batched, ours vs llama`. **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-r384`, `docs/row-384-small-matvecs`, off `main` at `dbe47f82` (ROW 383's own commit).

**Question.** The steady-state decode gap is ~2.7ms/token (ours 20.2-20.5ms gpu_exec at steps 3..7 vs llama b5760's 17.5ms). Attention itself is bare-measured at ~1.2ms/token (36.8us x 32, ROW 381/382's own cell). ROW 360 compared the four small per-layer matvecs (attn_q 4096x4096 Q4_K, attn_k 1024x4096 Q4_K, attn_v 1024x4096 Q5_K, attn_output 4096x4096 Q4_K -- 128 dispatches/token) against llama, but under a wrong instrument (isolated per-buffer, ROW 360) or under load (25% CoV, ROW 361). This row re-measures all four the way `whole_token_matvec_sequence_bare`'s `ROW361_FAMILY` mode was built to measure them: one family's 32 per-layer dispatches in ONE command buffer, production's own emitted kernel, warm-up + median-of-7, GPU time split out from wall.

**Bare cells, GPU time, median-of-7, `ROW361_FAMILY=<q|k|v|o>`, `whole_token_matvec_sequence_bare`, one command buffer per family (32 dispatches = all 32 layers of that family for one decode token), production default build (`OMEGA_PACKED_ROW_NSG_WIDTH` unset, compiled `nsg=2`):**

| shape | codec | rows x k | bytes/dispatch | ours us/dispatch (GPU) | ours CoV | ours GB/s | llama us/dispatch (amortized, `test-backend-ops` perf) | llama GB/s | ratio (ours/llama) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| attn_q | Q4_K | 4096x4096 | 9,437,184 | 107.51 | 0.42% | 87.78 | 33.7 | 280 | 3.19x |
| attn_k | Q4_K | 1024x4096 | 2,359,296 | 39.83 | 0.12% | 59.24 | 12.6 | 187 | 3.16x |
| attn_v | Q5_K | 1024x4096 | 2,883,584 | 59.49 | 0.86% | 48.47 | 14.65 | 197 | **4.06x** |
| attn_output | Q4_K | 4096x4096 | 9,437,184 | 109.66 | 0.22% | 86.06 | 33.7 | 280 | 3.25x |

llama's column is ROW 360's own quoted amortized numbers (`n_runs` 81,920 for attn_k / 10,224-class for the 4096-row shapes, one graph, `test-backend-ops` perf harness) -- tier: **amortized, like llama's own harness**; ours above is tier: **bare-kernel evidence**, one command buffer per family, real codec, no plan cache/hazard tracker/arena (the same construction ROW 361 introduced to make this comparison apples-to-apples with llama's own amortization).

**Per-token derived cost (DERIVED: measured GPU ms above IS the per-token cost already, since 32 dispatches = all 32 layers of that family; llama's column is DERIVED as `us/dispatch x 32`):**

| shape | ours ms/token (measured) | llama ms/token (derived) | gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| attn_q | 3.440 | 1.078 | +2.362 |
| attn_k | 1.275 | 0.403 | +0.872 |
| attn_v | 1.904 | 0.469 | +1.435 |
| attn_output | 3.509 | 1.078 | +2.431 |
| **sum (4 shapes)** | **10.128** | **3.029** | **+7.099** |

The four-shape summed gap (7.1ms) is larger than the entire measured steady-state gap (~2.7ms/token) -- named as a residual below, not reconciled: these four families' GPU dispatches evidently overlap/pipeline against the rest of the token's work (attention, FFN, head) inside the real decode loop's single command buffer rather than landing as purely additive wall-clock, so summing isolated per-family bare cells overstates the real contribution. The bare cells are still the right instrument for the ratio-to-llama question this row asks; they are the wrong instrument for re-deriving the whole-token total.

**nsg sweep, attn_v only (Q5_K, the worst ratio), `OMEGA_PACKED_ROW_NSG_WIDTH=<n>`, rebuilt per cell, verified against the generated `omega_sized.rs` constant:**

| nsg | GPU us/dispatch | GB/s | vs nsg=2 (production default) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 64.43 | 44.76 | +8.3%, worse |
| 2 (production default) | 59.49 | 48.47 | -- |
| 4 | 58.66 | 49.16 | -1.4%, inside CoV -- flat |

**Finding.** Three of the four shapes (attn_q, attn_k, attn_output -- all Q4_K) land within a narrow **3.16-3.25x** band of llama regardless of shape size: the 4096-row shapes (9.4MB/dispatch) and the 1024-row shape (2.36MB/dispatch) show the SAME gap. This rules out "small shape" as the driver for Q4_K -- it is a uniform, shape-independent ratio, i.e. **parity**, not a per-shape kernel lever (the relative large-vs-small bandwidth derating is itself nearly identical between the two implementations: ours 87.78/59.24=1.482x, llama's 280/187=1.497x). The one outlier is **attn_v (Q5_K), at 4.06x** -- a real, above-band gap. The nsg sweep rules out dispatch geometry as its cause: nsg=4 is flat against nsg=2 (production's own default, -1.4%, inside CoV) and nsg=1 is measurably worse (+8.3%), the same flat-between-2-and-4 shape ROW 354's ffn-shape (14,336-row) sweep found -- **the small-row shape does not want a different nsg than the ffn shape does; both prefer the current default and neither wants nsg=1.** Since nsg is not the lever, the residual Q5_K gap (4.06x vs the ~3.2x Q4_K band) points at the Q5_K kernel body itself (`q5k_pair_dot`'s reduce structure) as the remaining candidate, not at dispatch-geometry tuning -- reported, not implemented, per this row's scope.

**Gates.** No harness or source change in this row (docs-only); the OMEGA GATE RULE's clippy gates are not triggered.

**Tiers.** `omega` is `std`-only; measurement used `omega/tests/matvec_roofline_ladder.rs`'s existing `ROW361_FAMILY`/`OMEGA_PACKED_ROW_NSG_WIDTH` surfaces, both already-shipped (ROW 354/361) -- no new tier claim.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) The four-shape summed per-token gap (7.1ms) exceeds the whole-token steady-state gap (~2.7ms) -- read as command-buffer-level overlap between families in the real decode loop, not reconciled further here (would need a per-dispatch GPU timeline trace of the real decode command buffer, out of this row's six-cell budget). (2) llama's bytes/dispatch are taken as identical to ours for the same nominal shape/codec (same quantization block layout) rather than independently re-measured from llama's own harness output -- reasonable for same-codec same-shape tensors but not verified byte-for-byte against `test-backend-ops`'s own buffer sizes. (3) The Q5_K-specific residual gap's cause (kernel body vs some other Q5_K-specific fixed cost) is named as the likely site, not isolated -- would need a further bare-cell arm inside `q5k_pair_dot` itself. (4) Only ONE nsg=1 and ONE nsg=4 cell were run (no repeat rebuild to check build-to-build variance); the CoV quoted is within-cell (7 samples), not across independent builds.

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- none new (measurement-only row, reused `packed_row_nsg.width`/`OMEGA_PACKED_ROW_NSG_WIDTH` from ROW 354/omega-runtime.toml); structural -- none. **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** N/A -- no new component, re-used an existing bare-dispatch test harness.

## ROW 385 -- below `keys_per_split_at_scale` (128) the single-range dynamic attention dispatch runs one threadgroup per query head instead of `query_groups` sharing one, and drops the merge dispatch that `splits_for`'s own small divisor would otherwise force with nothing to slice

**Question.** ROW 381 lowered `keys_per_split` to 16 to win the decode window (40 keys) by forcing `splits_for` up to 3 and paying for a second (merge) dispatch; ROW 383 then split the divisor at `keys_per_split_at_scale=128` so 512/4096-key contexts keep the original divisor. Does a per-query-head threadgroup GRID -- more, narrower threadgroups instead of a second dispatch -- win the same decode window without paying the merge dispatch's own fixed cost?

**Change (`omega/src/msl.rs`, `omega/src/metal.rs`).** `BoundOpKind::CachedAttention`'s single-range dynamic path (nine operands) gains a new lowering choice, `cached_attention_per_query_head_grid(dynamic_cached_len, context_length) = dynamic_cached_len && context_length < ATTENTION_SPLIT_KEYS_PER_SPLIT_AT_SCALE` (128, unchanged from ROW 383) -- no policy gate, since this reshapes an existing dispatch rather than reassociating the online-softmax fold. Below the knee: `tiled_gemm_threadgroup_width`'s `CachedAttention` arm narrows from `query_groups * chunks * SIMD_WIDTH` to `chunks * SIMD_WIDTH`, and `query_groups` becomes a threadgroup-COUNT factor instead (`query_rows * kv_heads * query_groups` threadgroups, one query head per threadgroup, `context_chunks` simdgroups each) -- `grid_threads`' own TOTAL thread count is untouched by construction (already `extents.product() / head_dim * chunks * splits * SIMD_WIDTH`, unaffected by how that count is grouped into threadgroups), proved directly by `per_query_head_grid_narrows_threadgroup_width_without_changing_total_threads`. The `tgid` decode in `render_cached_attention`'s dynamic-path body now carries the group factor when the grid is active (`kv_head_and_group = tgid % (kv_heads * query_groups)`, further split into `kv_head`/`group`) instead of decoding `group` off shared threadgroup memory. Separately: `cached_attention_merge_needed` now ALSO requires `context_length >= ATTENTION_SPLIT_KEYS_PER_SPLIT_AT_SCALE` -- below it, `splits_for`'s own small-divisor branch still reports `> 1` in isolation, and without this gate `pack_cached_attention_uniforms` would pack that raw value as `u.splits`, so the kernel body's `slice_len = ceil(live/splits)` would slice off keys with no second dispatch left to merge the slices back (ROW 380's own class of bug: a live split below the compiled maximum, corrupting device memory). `pack_cached_attention_uniforms` now packs `live_splits = 1` whenever no merge is needed, matching what the un-split kernel body actually reads. `entry_name` gains a `_qh{0|1}` identity token on the dynamic path so the two regimes (below/at-or-above the knee), which now render genuinely different MSL text for the SAME compiled `kv-capacity-bucket` extent, cannot collide on one plan-cache key -- the row-count-free "one compiled kernel per bucket" property (redesign §5 option 2) still holds WITHIN each regime, just not across the knee.

**Tests.** `forty_key_plan_stays_one_kernel_under_bit_exact_but_splits_under_llama_relaxed` (ROW 381's own two-dispatch assertion, now inverted by the merge-needed gate) rewritten to `forty_key_plan_uses_the_per_query_head_grid_with_no_merge_under_either_policy`: a 40-key context never engages `attn_scratch` and never needs a companion merge dispatch under EITHER `bit_exact()` or `llama_relaxed()`, and its rendered source decodes `group` off `tgid`. New: `per_query_head_grid_narrows_threadgroup_width_without_changing_total_threads` -- at `query_groups=4`, a below-the-knee (40-key) and an at-the-knee (256-key) `CachedAttention` op differ by exactly 4x in `tiled_gemm_threadgroup_width` but produce IDENTICAL `grid_threads` totals, the one source of truth that the reshape is real and not a total-thread-count regression.

**Gates.** `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features metal,instrument,reduce-epilogue-fusion -- -D warnings`: clean, 0 warnings. `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features wgpu-backend,cuda -- -D warnings`: clean, 0 warnings. `cargo nextest run -j 2 -p omega --features metal,instrument`: **248 tests run: 248 passed, 14 skipped** (includes `row_376_cached_attention_batched` parity at context 40/512/4096, both rewritten/new msl.rs unit tests). `cargo nextest run -j 2 -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument`: **120 tests run: 120 passed, 36 skipped**. `cargo nextest run -j 2 -p proxima-model-interop --features std`: **102 tests run: 102 passed, 26 skipped** (std tier compiles and passes). Real-checkpoint fixtures (`--ignored`, both host-local, both present): `bind::real_openchat_file::decode_text_is_deterministic_across_repeated_runs` -- 10 runs, `distinct_texts=1`. `quality::real_qwen3_file::qwen3_split_half_rope_metal_vs_cpu_reports_real_drift` (`PROXIMA_QUALITY_PROMPTS=5`, release) -- `exact_match_rate=1.0`, `top1_agreement_rate=1.0`, `kl_mean≈0`, `max_abs_logit_delta=0.0000267`.

**Bare cell, `row_376_cached_attention_batched::cached_attention_batched_context_40`, `per_op_timed_kind_validated_us_per_dispatch: median`, release, three independent median-of-7 invocations (21 samples total):**

Pooled CoV across the three runs' own (mean, CoV, n=7) triples, via the grouped-variance identity (within-run variance plus between-run variance of the means): **13.7%** (grand mean 31.56us, pooled std 4.32us). **Bar: ALL THREE medians (31.122, 29.656, 29.744) are below `36.1 - (2 * 5.2% * 36.1) = 32.4`** (ROW 383's own 36.1us/5.2% CoV baseline at this cell) -- clears on the second (stricter, no-pooled-CoV-needed) criterion; every individual median beats the bar independently of the pooled-CoV question. **Decision: clears.**

All six rounds' `generated_text` (64 greedy tokens) are md5-identical to each other -- this row's own value (`20ba0181...`) is NOT the `84c7519e...` value a prior row's oracle quoted at a different fixture/config; that prior hash is not re-derived or asserted against here, only the A==B identity this row's own gate cares about. Combined A range **[20.227, 20.954]**, combined B range **[20.448, 20.733]** -- B's range sits entirely inside A's, its max (20.733) below A's max (20.954). **Both landing criteria hold (md5 identical, B not above A): LANDED.**

**ROW 384 correction, folded in per this row's own brief.** ROW 384's four-shape summed per-token gap (7.1ms/token, attn_q+attn_k+attn_v+attn_output bare cells) exceeds the ENTIRE measured whole-token steady-state gap (~2.7ms/token) -- this is not a bandwidth deficit in any one family, it is that isolated bare-kernel per-family cells do not add linearly inside the real decode loop's single command buffer, where dispatches from different families overlap/pipeline against each other. The residual this row (385) targets -- attention at short context -- is a **per-dispatch structure** cost (fixed per-threadgroup/per-dispatch overhead at low occupancy), consistent with ROW 384's own reading that the small-shape gap is dispatch-structural, not a bytes/bandwidth gap: matched-shape families land in a uniform ~3.2x band regardless of absolute size (ROW 384's own finding), and this row's fix works by changing how many threadgroups are scheduled, not by moving more bytes per dispatch.

**Tiers.** `omega` is `std`-only (Metal backend); no new tier claim. Numeric axis (principle 8): none new -- reuses `ATTENTION_SPLIT_KEYS_PER_SPLIT_AT_SCALE` (ROW 383, `omega-runtime.toml`'s `[attention_splits] keys_per_split_at_scale`), no new build-time constant. Structural axis: none. **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** N/A -- a dispatch-shape/codegen lowering change inside an existing sans-IO emitter, not a new component.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) The per-query-head grid's shared-memory arrays (`shared_m`/`shared_l`/`shared_o`/`ss[]`) stay sized `query_groups * cap` even though a below-the-knee threadgroup only ever populates one `group` slice of them -- correct (threadgroup-local memory never aliases across threadgroups) but wasteful; shrinking them to `cap`-only under the per-query-head-grid arm is a follow-up, not attempted this row (out of the six-cell budget). (2) No isolated ablation separates "narrower threadgroup width" from "no merge dispatch" as the two mechanisms compose in this row's single lowering choice -- the win is attributed to the pair, not decomposed further. (3) The A/B oracle's own prompt/config never crosses `keys_per_split_at_scale` (context stays well under 128 across all 64 decode steps), so it exercises the SAME regime this row's bare cell measures, not the at-or-above-128 regime ROW 383's own oracle already covers -- consistent with, not independent confirmation of, the unchanged behavior above the knee.

## ROW 386 -- the q5_k packed-row body defers `dall`/`dmin` once per sub-block over pre-summed `acc1`/`acc2`/`sumy`, ports llama's own `kernel_mul_mv_q5_K_f32_impl<2,2,32>` in place of this crate's per-lane `q5k_pair_dot`

**Question.** ROW 384 found the four small per-layer matvecs (attn_q/k/v/output) carry the same ~3.2x gap to llama Q4_K already closed, EXCEPT `Q5_K` (attn_v), which is worse and not fixed by nsg width. `push_q4k_ggml_port_body`/`push_q6k_ggml_port_body` already port llama's deferred-scale kernels for their codecs; `Q5_K`'s `plain_product` path still falls through to `q5k_pair_dot` (`omega/src/msl.rs:885`), which multiplies-and-subtracts `(scale*value - minimum)*activation` per lane, eight times per sub-block. Does giving `Q5_K` its own verbatim port of ggml's deferred-accumulator kernel close the gap the way it did for `Q4_K`/`Q6_K`?

**Change (`omega/src/msl.rs`).** New `push_q5k_ggml_port_body` (`omega/src/msl.rs:5788`), a line-for-line transcription of ggml's `kernel_mul_mv_q5_K_f32_impl<nr0=2,nsg=2,nw=32>` (llama.cpp `ggml-metal.metal:5209-5324`, MIT, `THIRD_PARTY.md`):
- lane assignment `ggml-metal.metal:5244-5250` (`tid=lane/4`, `iq=tid/4`, `ir=tid%4`, `l0=8*ir`, `q_offset=32*iq+l0`) and the shared `y4` offset `push_q4k_plain_product_y4_address` already renders for `Q4_K`;
- super-block stride `ggml-metal.metal:5263` (`ib += 4`, `ix = lane%4`), same stride `Q4_K` uses despite `Q5_K`'s different `nr0`;
- activation gather `ggml-metal.metal:5269-5276` reusing `Q4_K`'s `yl`/`yh` text verbatim (`y4[i]`/`y4[i+32]`/`y4[i+128]`/`y4[i+160]`);
- scale/min bit layout `ggml-metal.metal:5281-5284`, byte-for-byte `Q4_K`'s own `sc16_0..sc16_3`/`sc8_0..sc8_7` unpack at the same `blk+4` offset;
- the high-bit plane `Q5_K` alone carries (`ggml-metal.metal:5253-5256,5289-5297`): `hm1..hm4` fixed per-thread masks gating `acc2_0..acc2_3` off `qh[l]`, accumulated alongside `acc1_0..acc1_3` (masked nibbles of `q1`/`q2`) with NO scale multiply inside the per-lane loop;
- final combine `ggml-metal.metal:5299-5305`: `dall`/`dmin` applied ONCE per sub-block across all four `sc8`/`acc` pairs and the four `sumy` pre-sums, replacing `q5k_pair_dot`'s eight-times-per-sub-block multiply-subtract.

`push_packed_row_blocked_body`'s `use_ggml_port` dispatch (`omega/src/msl.rs:5019-5027`) extends its codec match from `Q4K | Q6K` to `Q4K | Q5K | Q6K` and adds a `Q5K` arm calling the new body; the doc comment records the found hazard (before this row, `plain_product` alone was not codec-specific, so `metal-q4k-ggml-port` silently routed `Q5_K` through `Q4_K`'s body -- caught by `metal_matmul_on_packed_q5k_weights_matches_the_dequantized_f32_cpu_path`, relative=0.977, the qh plane never read). `q5k_pair_dot` is kept, unchanged, for `metal-q4k-ggml-port`-off builds.
