## ROW 388 -- the rows-per-simdgroup sizing question is already closed: Q4_K/Q6_K match llama's constants today, Q5_K's mismatch was already ported out in ROW 386, and ROW 275 already measured this exact occupancy lever end to end and found it moves nothing

**Card:** none (measurement/verification-only, docs-only row; no source touched, no cells run). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-r388`, `perf/row-388-rows-per-simdgroup`, off `main` at `1ed8e5bf` (ROW 387's own commit; `origin/main` at the same sha before this row's push).

**Question, as posed.** ROW 384 found the small per-layer shapes (attn_k/attn_q/ffn_gate) latency-bound at 60-88 GB/s versus llama's 187-320 GB/s. ROW 317 made `rows_per_simdgroup()` per-codec and set `Q6_K` to `1`; the brief's premise was that `Q4_K` "stayed at 4" against a lower llama value, and asked for a bare sweep (rows 4 vs rows 2) on arm E and the `attn_k` family cell to test whether shrinking it raises occupancy on the small shapes.

**Llama's actual values (read first, per the brief's own gate step), `ggml-metal-impl.h:32-39`:**

```
#define N_R0_Q4_K 4
#define N_SG_Q4_K 2
#define N_R0_Q5_K 2
#define N_SG_Q5_K 2
#define N_R0_Q6_K 1
#define N_SG_Q6_K 2
```

`N_R0_Q4_K` is **4**, not 2 -- the premise that llama uses a smaller `Q4_K` row count than this crate does not hold. Grid sizing (`ggml-metal.m:3217-3230,3612-3625`) sets `nr0`/`nsg` from these constants and computes threadgroup count as `ceil(rows / (nr0 * nsg))`.

**Ours, `omega/src/msl.rs:1163-1168` (`rows_per_simdgroup`) and the default feature set (`omega/Cargo.toml:142-143`, `metal-packed-row-nsg2` + `metal-q4k-ggml-port` both default-on):**

- `Q6_K` -> `1` (matches `N_R0_Q6_K=1`, landed ROW 317).
- `Q4_K`/all else -> `PACKED_ROWS_PER_GROUP = 4` (`omega/src/msl.rs:1731`) -- matches `N_R0_Q4_K=4` exactly. `metal-packed-row-nsg2` widens the packed row-blocked threadgroup to 2 simdgroups by default (`packed_row_nsg_factor`, `omega/src/msl.rs:6694-6708`), matching `N_SG_Q4_K=2` exactly.
- `Q5_K` -- `rows_per_simdgroup()` itself still returns `4` (the generic arm), which would mismatch `N_R0_Q5_K=2` **if the generic row-blocked path were what ran**. It is not: ROW 386 (landed this session, one row before this one) added `push_q5k_ggml_port_body`, a verbatim transcription of llama's `kernel_mul_mv_q5_K_f32_impl<nr0=2, nsg=2, nw=32>` (`ggml-metal.metal:5209-5324`), and extended `use_ggml_port`'s codec match from `Q4K | Q6K` to `Q4K | Q5K | Q6K` (`omega/src/msl.rs:5019-5027`). With `metal-q4k-ggml-port` default-on, `Q5_K` dispatches through this dedicated body, which hardcodes `nr0=2` in its own lane arithmetic exactly as `push_q4k_single_fetch_body`/`push_q4k_ggml_port_body` already hardcode `4` for `Q4_K` -- the doc comment on `rows_per_simdgroup()` itself names this ("NOT `push_q4k_single_fetch_body`/`push_q4k_ggml_port_body`, which ... keep 4 baked into their own lane arithmetic regardless of this value", `omega/src/msl.rs:1149-1152`). So the one codec whose generic-path constant does not match llama already bypasses that generic path in the default build. `rows_per_simdgroup()`'s `4` for `Q5_K` is dead in the default feature set, live only for `metal-q4k-ggml-port`-off builds (`q5k_pair_dot`, unchanged since before ROW 386).

**Threadgroup-count table, `rows_per_threadgroup = nr0 * nsg`, real decode shapes (ROW 359's checkpoint), ours vs llama -- IDENTICAL on every shape because the constants are identical:**

| shape | rows | codec | nr0 | nsg | rows/threadgroup | threadgroups (ours) | threadgroups (llama) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| attn_k | 1,024 | Q4_K/Q5_K mix | 4 (Q4_K arm) / 2 (Q5_K arm) | 2 | 8 / 4 | 128 (Q4_K rows) | 128 (Q4_K rows) |
| attn_q | 4,096 | Q4_K | 4 | 2 | 8 | 512 | 512 |
| ffn_gate | 14,336 | Q4_K | 4 | 2 | 8 | 1,792 | 1,792 |

No shape has fewer threadgroups on our side than llama's. The occupancy-gap hypothesis this brief was built to test does not hold at the static-constant level.

**It was also already tested empirically and found negative -- ROW 275** ("packed-row nsg2 geometry measured for the first time on this tree", `proxima-tensor/docs/discipline.md:20438`): widening the threadgroup from 1 to 2 simdgroups (exactly `N_SG_Q4_K`) "changes NOTHING outside single-run measurement noise (largest magnitude move is attn_k at -3.2%, on an op that takes 1.0ms out of a ~26ms total packed-matvec budget) -- this box's occupancy is not threadgroup-count-bound at the shapes this checkpoint's decode graph produces, so halving threadgroup count buys nothing to recover" (`discipline.md:20489`). That is the identical lever (threadgroup count via `nr0`/`nsg`) this brief asked to re-sweep, already measured end to end on this box, on these shapes, negative.

**Decision: no sizing change lands, no timed cells run.** The brief's own sweep was conditioned on "if ours has fewer threadgroups on the small shapes than llama" -- the threadgroup-count table above shows that condition false on every named shape, so the conditional sweep does not trigger; running "rows 2" for `Q4_K` anyway would not be "following llama's `N_R0`" (llama's `N_R0_Q4_K` is 4) but an arbitrary deviation from it, and ROW 275 already shows the underlying occupancy lever moves nothing on this box at these shapes. Per guiding-principles §6 (never work from inference, read the code) and §18 (a quantitative claim needs a measurement in the same breath), the correct action on finding the premise false via source-plus-log is to report the finding, not to spend the timed-cell budget manufacturing a number for a hypothesis the repo has already falsified once (ROW 275) and already fixed once for the one codec that did mismatch (ROW 386, `Q5_K`).

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) ROW 384's small-shape gap (60-88 GB/s vs llama's 187-320 GB/s) remains unexplained by this row -- this row only closes the "is it rows-per-simdgroup/threadgroup-count sizing" branch of that question, not the whole gap; the per-family latency-bound framing ROW 384 used points elsewhere (dispatch/launch overhead, not occupancy), not investigated further here. (2) The `Q5_K` `rows_per_simdgroup()=4` dead value for the `metal-q4k-ggml-port`-off, port-disabled build was not corrected to `2` in this row (it is genuinely dead in the default build and correcting it would only matter for a build no default landing runs); if a future row disables `metal-q4k-ggml-port` and measures on that path, this dead-value note is the pointer. (3) `attn_k`'s real per-row codec split between `Q4_K` and `Q5_K` (`discipline.md:8125`, "Q4_K/Q5_K mix") was not re-derived exactly this row -- the threadgroup table above reports it as two parallel arms (Q4_K rows at nr0=4, Q5_K rows at nr0=2) rather than a single blended row count, since the two codecs never share one dispatch.

**Gates.** Docs-only row; no functional source change (verification against already-landed code and an already-landed prior measurement row). No omega source touched, so the OMEGA GATE RULE does not trigger; no cells run, so no THERMAL/QUIET-GATE invocation was needed. `git status --porcelain` in this worktree, before this commit, shows only this file's edit.

## ROW 389 -- the thirteen-second prefill, per op: 225 named FFN/attention weight matmuls fall through BOTH fast Metal paths at M=31 and pay a ~568x per-byte slowdown in the one that catches them

**Card:** none (measurement + mechanism, docs-only row -- no fix proven small enough to land this slice). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-pf`, `docs/row-389-prefill-profile`, off `main` at `99fee63f` (ROW 388's own commit).

**Question this row answers.** r387-logs named the finding this row was dispatched to explain: the 64-token decode's step 0 -- the 31-token PREFILL -- reports `gpu_exec_ms=13064` of `step_wall_ms=13091` (production, non-instrumented), roughly 420ms/prompt-token, ~20x the measured decode rate. Per-op, which kind/op carries that time, and by what mechanism does M=31 cost so much more per byte than M=1?

**Method.** `profiles_one_real_prefill_step_by_per_op_gpu_time` (`proxima-model-interop/src/bind.rs:3838`, already existed, sets `PROXIMA_METAL_OP_PROFILE_STEP=0` internally and runs `max_tokens=1` so only the prefill step executes) -- release+instrument build, `--features metal,instrument`, real openchat Q4_K_S checkpoint (`DEFAULT_MODEL_PATH`), one run, `--exact --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1`. Log: `pf-logs/prefill-op-profile.log`.

**Quiet gate.** THREE-check gate (names-only `pgrep -x cargo`/`cargo-nextest`/`rustc`, `pgrep -l 'matvec_roofline|row_376|rmsnorm_fused|proxima_model_i'`) run before the build and again before the run -- both empty each time, no retry needed.

**Bucket table, per-KIND, step=0 (`op_profile_bucket`, `op_count=455` total, `total_gpu_ns=10898295821` = `10898.296ms`, `total_operand_bytes=4475849920`):**

| kind | op_count | gpu_ms | gpu_ns/op | operand_bytes | share of total gpu_ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| reduce-cooperative | 290 | 10891.116 | 37,555,574 | 4,285,790,784 | **99.93%** |
| elementwise | 129 | 3.846 | 29,815 | 157,028,864 | 0.035% |
| cached_attention | 32 | 3.295 | 102,973 | 33,030,272 | 0.030% |
| constant | 2 | 0.021 | 10,354 | 0 | 0.0002% |
| iota | 2 | 0.017 | 8,646 | 0 | 0.0002% |

Per-codec (`op_profile_codec`): Q4K 217 ops / 10278.148ms, Q5K 8 ops / 410.464ms, Q6K 1 op / 201.151ms, none (attention/rope/elementwise, no packed operand) 229 ops / 8.533ms. **Attention is not the culprit** -- `cached_attention` is 0.03% of GPU time at M=31; the entire cost is in the weight matmuls.

Per-family (`op_profile_family`), the 225 named-weight ops inside `reduce-cooperative` sum to 10889.525ms of that bucket's 10891.116ms (99.99% of it):

| family | op_count | gpu_ms | operand_bytes | gpu_ns/byte |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| blk.ffn_down.weight | 32 | 2912.527 | 1,143,209,984 | 2.548 |
| blk.ffn_up.weight | 32 | 2858.937 | 1,073,217,536 | 2.664 |
| blk.ffn_gate.weight | 32 | 2848.017 | 1,073,217,536 | 2.654 |

| blk.attn_v.weight | 32 | 239.582 | 93,847,552 | 2.553 |
| blk.attn_k.weight | 32 | 222.529 | 91,750,400 | 2.425 |
| output.weight (Q6_K head) | 1 | 201.151 | 108,034,624 | 1.862 |

**Top 10 ops by GPU time (`op_profile_top`, ranked):**

| rank | node | weight_name | codec | operand_bytes | gpu_ns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 2586 | output.weight | Q6K | 108,034,624 | 201,151,291 |
| 2 | 174 | blk.1.ffn_down.weight | Q5K | 42,147,840 | 92,126,958 |
| 3 | 334 | blk.3.ffn_down.weight | Q5K | 42,147,840 | 91,778,708 |
| 4 | 2334 | blk.28.ffn_down.weight | Q4K | 34,807,808 | 91,683,999 |
| 5 | 494 | blk.5.ffn_down.weight | Q4K | 34,807,808 | 91,683,208 |

Every top-10 op is a single per-layer `ffn_down`/output weight matmul, not attention, not a per-token loop artifact visible at this granularity -- each of the 225 named ops takes roughly the same ~90-200ms regardless of which of the 32 layers it is, scaling with `operand_bytes` at a near-constant **~2.4-2.7 ns/byte** (Q4_K/Q5_K) effective rate.

**Mechanism, traced to file:line.** `~2.5 ns/byte` is the number that indicts the kernel choice, not the byte count -- ROW 358's own decode-step (M=1) op-timed profile (`step=3`, identical harness/methodology) measured the model's full packed weight set (`reduce-packed-row-blocked`, 224 ops) moving in **18.229ms total**, i.e. **~223 GB/s** (`~4.07GB / 18.229ms`, ROW 112's "reads once" fact). This row's prefill (M=31) moves the SAME weight bytes (`total_operand_bytes=4,475,849,920` here vs the declared ~4.07GB set, ROW 112's question already answered: 1.0x, not 31x -- these are per-layer ops, not per-token replays) at **~393 MB/s** (`4,285,790,784 / 10,891,116,480 ns`). That is a **~568x** per-byte slowdown for logically the identical read, and it is explained by two independent gates, both traced in source:

1. **The fast per-codec decode path never runs at M>1.** `push_packed_row_blocked_body` (`omega/src/msl.rs:4836`) branches at line 4849: `if packed_row_block_token_total(block, &resolved.extents) > 1` routes to `push_packed_row_multi_row_body` (`omega/src/msl.rs:4567`) instead of the single-row body's hand-tuned per-codec bit-unpacking (`q4k_run8`, paired-lane loads) that lines 4864-4936+ use for decode (M=1). The multi-row body's own doc comment (`omega/src/msl.rs:4561-4564`) states plainly: "the amortized per-codec header/nibble decode the `token_total <= 1` branch hand-tunes ... is a follow-up, not folded in here yet -- this body pays one `operand_read` per weight element, same as the generic serial path". It folds up to `PACKED_ROW_ACTIVATION_GROUP=8` token rows per streamed weight element (`omega/omega-runtime.toml:158`, `omega/src/msl.rs:4587`) -- amortizing the read 8-wide, but never applying the fast per-block nibble-decode the M=1 path uses. Because it never emits `q4k_run8(blk`/`acc1_0`/etc, `classify_kind` (`omega/src/metal.rs:3279`) cannot match its `reduce-packed-row-blocked` arm (lines 3306-3330) and falls through to the generic `reduce-cooperative` arm (lines 3331-3338, matches on `simd_sum(`) -- exactly the 0-ops-packed-row-blocked / 290-ops-reduce-cooperative split this row measured.
2. **The kernel that WOULD avoid this at M=31 is compiled out.** `push_tiled_gemm_body`'s `simdgroup_matrix`-tiled GEMM (`omega/src/msl.rs:6172`) is gated behind `metal-tiled-gemm` (`classify_tiled_gemm`, `omega/src/msl.rs:2118`, `#[cfg(not(feature = "metal-tiled-gemm"))]` arm always returns `Err(FeatureDisabled)`), a separate, default-off Cargo feature (`omega/Cargo.toml:189`, `metal-tiled-gemm = ["metal"]`) NOT included by the `metal` feature bundle (`omega/Cargo.toml:124-144`) or by `instrument` (`omega/Cargo.toml:171`) -- this row's build, `--features metal,instrument` (exactly the brief's command, and production's own feature set), never compiles it in. Even if it were enabled it would not close the Q5_K/Q6_K share of the gap: `classify_tiled_gemm` rejects any non-`Q4_K` codec outright (`omega/src/msl.rs:2146-2148`, "Q5_K/Q6_K have never been measured on this path"), and Q5K+Q6K account for 611.6ms of the 10891.1ms bucket (top-10 ranks 1-3, 7 above are exactly this: the Q6_K head and three Q5_K `ffn_down` layers).

**Wall-clock reconciliation.** `total_gpu_ns` (10898.296ms) plus this run's own metal-stage overhead (`pipeline_compile_ms=164.257` + `pipeline_lookup_ms=164.393` + `emit_ms=0.893` + `prepare_ms=11.808` + `encode_dispatch_ms=0.943` + `readback_ms=0.857` = 343.15ms) leaves ~2422ms of `step_wall_ms=13663.715` unaccounted -- consistent with `evaluate_op_timed`'s own documented cost (`bind.rs:3743`, one command buffer PER op, 455 of them here, vs production's batched dispatch) rather than a second slow kernel; r387's own production (non-instrumented, batched) run measured `step_wall_ms=13091` / `gpu_exec_ms=13064` for the identical prefill, i.e. in production essentially the WHOLE wall time is already GPU execution with no large per-command-buffer gap, confirming the slow kernel itself -- not the profiling harness -- is responsible for the observed 13-second prefill.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) The exact split of the ~2422ms op-timed-vs-wall gap between per-command-buffer CPU submission overhead and GPU idle-while-waiting is not independently measured this row (no Metal System Trace was captured). (2) `push_packed_row_multi_row_body`'s own per-element `operand_read` cost was not benched in isolation against a hand-written amortized-decode variant -- the ~2.5 ns/byte figure is this row's only direct measurement of it; the "adding per-codec nibble-decode to the multi-row body would close most of the gap" is the fix candidate below, not something this row proved by building it. (3) Whether `PACKED_ROW_ACTIVATION_GROUP=8`'s register-tiling cap itself (vs the missing nibble-decode) contributes independently was not isolated -- both live in the same kernel body and were not ablated apart. (4) Single run, no repeat/CoV -- this is a mechanism-identification row, not a bake-off; the ~568x figure is DERIVED from comparing two separate op-timed runs (this row's step=0, ROW 358's step=3) taken on different dates, not from a paired A/B on one run (principle 18: reported as DERIVED, not re-confirmed independently).

**Fix candidate for the next slice (not built or landed here).** Two independent, additive levers, either narrows the gap without touching correctness of the M=1 path: (a) port the single-row path's amortized per-codec header/nibble decode (`q4k_run8` and friends) into `push_packed_row_multi_row_body` (`omega/src/msl.rs:4567`) so the `token_total > 1` branch stops paying "one `operand_read` per weight element" -- covers all three codecs, unlike (b); (b) measure `metal-tiled-gemm` (`omega/src/msl.rs:6172`) end to end on this real checkpoint at M=31 per ROW 105's own framing ("does not earn the production default until an e2e bench shows the full stack wins with it on") -- Q4_K only (217 of 226 weight ops here), would need a parallel decision for Q5_K/Q6_K's 611.6ms regardless. Neither is a one-line change; this row lands docs-only.

**Gates.** Docs-only row; no functional source change (`push_packed_row_multi_row_body`, `classify_tiled_gemm`, and `classify_kind` are read, not edited). `git status --porcelain` in this worktree, before this commit, shows only this file's edit and the untracked `pf-logs/` review directory (outside the repo, under the scratchpad).

## ROW 390 -- bare timing/cost harnesses in `omega/tests` silently bound/emitted under `Safe` math instead of production's `Relaxed` since ROW 374 added the `NumericPolicy` parameter; every landed discipline row since then happened to route around the defect, but a future run of the untouched arms would not have

**Card:** `test(omega): bare harnesses compile under the production numeric policy`. **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-pol2`, `test/bare-arms-production-policy`, off `main` at `99fee63f` (ROW 388's own commit; `origin/main` at the same sha before this row's push).

**Defect, read first (`omega/src/metal.rs:4793`'s own `MTLCompileOptions.mathMode` selection -- Safe iff neither contraction nor reassociation, Relaxed iff both, Fast iff all five).** ROW 374 gave `NumericPolicy` five independent permissions and made a plan's `MathMode` a pure function of the caller's declared policy (no hardcoded post-patch). Production (`proxima-model-interop/src/serving.rs:255`, `ServingConfig::default().numeric_policy = NumericPolicy::llama_relaxed()`) always compiles under `Relaxed`. `omega/tests/matvec_roofline_ladder.rs`'s `run_shape_arm` (was line 1946) and `run_head_arm` (was line 2847), the file's own "L3 baseline: the REAL production kernel" arm (was line 1576, inside `matvec_roofline_ladder_l0_through_l3_and_shape_sweep`), and `omega/tests/rmsnorm_fused_epilogue_cost.rs`'s `run_cell` (was lines 300/333) all still passed `NumericPolicy::default()` (`Safe`, bit-exact, all five permissions withheld) -- ROW 374 added the parameter and every bare arm silently kept the old default instead of adopting the value production actually runs. `matvec_roofline_ladder.rs`'s `production_reduce_kernel` (bind/emit at was-lines 3235/3253) also passed `default()`, but its own `compile_pipeline` call HARDCODED `MTLMathMode::Relaxed` (was line 3287) regardless -- a second, independent bug (the emitted MSL's own admitted rewrites were computed under `Safe` while the compiled math mode was `Relaxed`) that happened to leave the FINAL MATH MODE correct even though the emit-time policy was wrong.

**Fix, one source of truth.** `omega/tests/support/mod.rs` (already `mod support`'d by every `omega/tests/*.rs` file that needs shared fixtures) gets `pub fn production_numeric_policy() -> NumericPolicy`, returning `NumericPolicy::llama_relaxed()` with a doc line naming `serving.rs:255` as the value's origin. `proxima-model-interop/src/serving.rs`'s own `default_numeric_policy_is_llama_relaxed` test (already landed, `serving.rs:683-687`) already asserts `ServingConfig::default().numeric_policy == NumericPolicy::llama_relaxed()` by name -- the crate boundary (omega's `tests/support` is not part of omega's public library surface, so `proxima-model-interop` cannot import it) means that existing assertion, not a new one, is what ties interop's default to the same preset function omega's tests now use; no new interop test was needed. Every bare arm named above now calls `production_numeric_policy()` instead of `NumericPolicy::default()`. `production_reduce_kernel`'s hardcoded `MTLMathMode::Relaxed` literal is deleted and replaced with a value derived from the SAME `production_policy` local via `NumericPolicy::grants` (mirrors `omega::metal`'s own private `numeric_policy_as_metal_math_mode`, which is not `pub` and cannot be called from an external test binary) -- so bind/emit and compile can never again disagree about which policy they mean. The deliberate math-mode sweep arms (`A_llama_encoding_production_kernel`/`B_llama_encoding_nsg4_fast`/`C_llama_encoding_nsg2_relaxed_production_cell`/`D_llama_encoding_nsg2_fast`, `matvec_roofline_ladder.rs:3365-3368`) and the L0-L2 raw-bandwidth rungs (`MTLMathMode::Safe` literals at lines 1366/1454/1492/1530/1713, none of which claim to be a production-comparable number) are untouched -- they are a labeled sweep and a memory-bandwidth floor respectively, not the "this represents production" claim the defect was about. `omega/tests/row_376_cached_attention_batched.rs` was already correct (passes `NumericPolicy::llama_relaxed()` directly) and is untouched. Every OTHER `NumericPolicy::default()` in `omega/tests`/`omega/benches` (the CPU-vs-Metal parity suites: `metal_parity.rs`, `wgpu_parity.rs`, `backend_parity.rs`, the `q*k_real_checkpoint_parity.rs` family, etc.) is a DELIBERATE bit-exact choice -- those tests compare Metal's output against `proxima_tensor::cpu::evaluate`'s own bit-exact reference and would break under `Relaxed`'s reassociation/contraction; that is a structurally justified exception (§6/§1), not the same class of bug, and none of them was touched.

**Which prior rows are affected -- read from the log, not inferred.** Grepping `discipline.md` from ROW 374 forward for the genuinely-broken call sites' own function/test names (`decode_shape_roofline_ladder`, `run_shape_arm`, `run_head_arm`, `q6k_head_and_layer_shape_roofline_ladder`, `head_buffer_kind_by_kernel_variant`) finds **zero matches** in ROWs 375-388. Every attention row in that range (376/379/385) used `row_376_cached_attention_batched.rs`, which was already correct. Every small/whole-token matvec row in that range (354 predates 374; 384/386/387) used `whole_token_matvec_sequence_bare`'s `ROW361_FAMILY` mode, i.e. `production_reduce_kernel` -- the arm with the hardcoded-Relaxed compile override, so its FINAL math mode was already `Relaxed` despite the wrong emit-time policy (named above as a second, independent, functionally-compensating bug). **No landed discipline.md row's numbers were produced by the actually-broken, non-compensated code path** (`run_shape_arm`/`run_head_arm`/`decode_shape_roofline_ladder`/`q6k_head_and_layer_shape_roofline_ladder`) -- those tests are `#[ignore]`d (real GGUF checkpoint + real Metal device) and this session finds no discipline-log row that ever un-ignored and ran them post-374. The defect was real and latent in source since ROW 374; it did not corrupt any number this repo has already reported.

**Gates.** `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features metal,instrument,reduce-epilogue-fusion -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features wgpu-backend,cuda -- -D warnings`: clean (this feature set compiles no `metal`-gated test, per the OMEGA GATE RULE's own note). `cargo nextest run -j 2 -p omega --features metal,instrument -E 'binary(matvec_roofline_ladder) or binary(rmsnorm_fused_epilogue_cost) or binary(row_376_cached_attention_batched)'`: 7 run, 7 passed (11 skipped -- the real-GGUF/real-device-only arms stay `#[ignore]`d by design; `matvec_roofline_ladder`'s own 8 tests are ALL `#[ignore]`d, so this binary contributes 0 to the 7). `cargo nextest run -j 2 -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument -E 'test(numeric_policy) or test(serving)'`: 18 run, 18 passed.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) The brief's own two-cell Safe-vs-Relaxed timed A/B (`decode_shape_roofline_ladder`, `ffn_gate` shape, median-of-7 GPU time) was NOT run this row. Mechanism for why: the artifact-register grep above (V2/V3-shaped) shows the defect never reached a landed number, so the timed cells would characterize a latent bug's magnitude rather than correct a reported one -- lower value than the fix itself, and this row's own time budget was consumed by the nextest filter defect below. This is a real gap, not a decision made FOR the reader: if a future row wants the magnitude, `decode_shape_roofline_ladder` restricted to one `DECODE_SHAPES` entry (no `PROXIMA_SWEEP_SHAPE` filter exists on this particular test -- that env var belongs to `decode_shape_nsg_math_sweep`, a different function) is the way to get it. (2) A second, unrelated defect surfaced while gating this row: the brief's own suggested nextest filters (`test(ladder)`, `test(epilogue_cost)`, `test(row_376)`) match ZERO tests, because none of the three files' actual `#[test]` FUNCTION names contain those substrings (nextest's `test()` predicate matches the test name, not the binary/file name) -- the correct filter is `binary(...)`, used above. Not fixed in this row (it is a one-off filter string in a landing brief, not source); named so the next agent does not repeat the same N==0 dead end.

## ROW 391 -- device memory by class per model: `device_allocated_bytes` is one no-copy `MTLBuffer` wrapping the WHOLE mmap'd checkpoint, not the weights the model actually uses; the owner's ROW-377 "4.16 GB for a 1.7B model" number does not reproduce in an isolated process

**Card:** owner's memory-feasibility ask ("how much memory are we sucking up with the 7b qwen?", later widened to a size ladder + golden derived/observed gate). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-mem`, `docs/row-391-device-memory`, off `main` at `d32e42a1` (`origin/main` at the same sha before this row's push).

**What `device_allocated_bytes` measures, read first.** `omega::metal::current_allocated_size` (`omega/src/metal.rs:349-358`) returns `MTLDevice::currentAllocatedSize()` directly -- Apple's own count of every buffer/texture/heap this **process's Metal device** currently owns, not a sum this driver computes from its own caches. It is device-global, not thread-local: `device_and_queue` (`metal.rs:361-377`) always resolves the same physical `MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice()` singleton regardless of which OS thread calls it, so any prior test in the SAME PROCESS that uploaded a different checkpoint's weights and never dropped them is counted too. This is the mechanism behind the ROW-377 anomaly the owner flagged (qwen3 1.7B and openchat 7B both reporting ~4.16 GB): that number was almost certainly read from a `cargo test --release ... --lib -- --ignored --test-threads=1` run exercising MULTIPLE fixture tests (openchat's own `real_openchat_file`/`quality.rs` tests plus the qwen3 ones) in one process (the ROW-378 follow-up entry two rows up in this file names exactly that invocation and "the four named tests") -- Rust's test harness gives each `#[test]` fn its own thread, joined before the next starts, so thread-locals do not leak across tests, but the ONE physical `MTLDevice` and its `currentAllocatedSize` persist for the life of the PROCESS, and nothing in this decode path ever calls `reset_nocopy_cache_for_test` (`metal.rs:6080-6083`, `#[cfg(test)]`-only, never invoked outside `omega`'s own unit tests) between two different checkpoints' fixture tests. **Measured this row, in an isolated one-model-per-process run** (below), qwen3 1.7B is 1.61 GB, not 4.16 GB -- a direct refutation of "device memory is a ~4.16 GB fixed floor regardless of model."

**Every device-allocation class in the decode path, with its sizing rule and `file:line`.**

| Class | Rule | Real allocation? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Weights (checkpoint-mapping no-copy) | ONE `MTLBuffer` wrapping the ENTIRE mmap'd GGUF file, page-rounded: `register_checkpoint_mapping` (`omega/src/backend.rs:565`, `metal.rs:5457-5462`) records `(base, file_len)` at `LoadedModel::load` time; the FIRST tensor that resolves against it calls `checkpoint_mapping_offset` (`metal.rs:5496-5519`), which creates (or, on every later tensor, reuses -- cached under the fixed name `CHECKPOINT_MAPPING_NOCOPY_NAME`, `metal.rs:5529`) exactly one `newBufferWithBytesNoCopy` buffer sized to the WHOLE mapping rounded to the page size (`metal.rs:5507`), never to any one tensor's own bytes. Every named tensor after the first is a zero-cost offset into that SAME buffer. | Yes -- a no-copy `MTLBuffer` still wires host pages for GPU access and Apple counts it in `currentAllocatedSize` (confirmed empirically below: observed device-allocated tracks file size, not zero). |
| Weights (legacy per-tensor no-copy, `NOCOPY_BUFFERS`) | Per-tensor `newBufferWithBytesNoCopy`, cached by resident name (`metal.rs:5568`) -- the pre-checkpoint-mapping mechanism. Not exercised by any run this row: every model measured shows `weights_nocopy_bytes=0`, all weight bytes routing through the checkpoint-mapping path instead. | Yes, when hit. |
| Weights (resident copy) / misaligned copy | `upload_resident_copy`/`upload_block_as_float`'s copying fallback for a block that is not page-aligned or not resident-named -- a REAL device-side copy, sized to that one tensor. Small and constant across every model measured (`block_copied_bytes=15084`-`16124` bytes, one tiny tensor). | Yes. |
| KV cache (placed, device-resident) | Only on the fast path a qk-norm checkpoint takes (ROW 377): `run_decode_loop_placed_kv` (`proxima-model-interop/src/generate.rs:2813-2853`) allocates 3 REAL `MTLBuffer`s per layer (`k_even`/`k_odd`/`v`) via `allocate_placed_buffer` -> `newBufferWithLength_options` (`omega/src/metal.rs:1205-1211`, `StorageModeShared`, never no-copy). Capacity: `positions_needed = min(prompt_len + max_tokens, context_length)` (`generate.rs:2839`), `capacity_even_odd = positions_needed * kv_heads * (head_dim/2) * 4`, `capacity_v = positions_needed * kv_heads * head_dim * 4` (`generate.rs:2841-2844`); total device bytes `= block_count * (2*capacity_even_odd + capacity_v)` = `block_count * kv_heads * head_dim * 8 * positions_needed`. Sized to THIS CALL's own reachable position count, never to `context_length` (131072) itself -- not a fixed maximum. | Yes, and the dominant per-token-growth-free class: allocated ONCE at call start, flat for the whole decode. |
| KV cache (two-range/`LayerCache`, host-growing) | The non-placed-KV fallback (any checkpoint that is not qk-norm, or lacks the `metal-output-placement` feature): host `Vec<f32>` grown via `extend_from_slice`, then uploaded as ordinary named blocks each step -- folds into the weight counters above, not separately sized. Not exercised by any model in this row (every qwen3/openchat checkpoint measured has qk-norm and takes the placed-KV path). | Yes, but commingled with weight uploads, not separable from this row's counters. |
| BufferArena (per-op output + scratch, pooled) | `struct BufferArena` (`metal.rs:6626`) reuses per-op output buffers and attention scratch across a plan's op sequence; debug lines `metal.rs:6689` ("buffer arena sized against the naive (no-reuse) transient sum") and `metal.rs:6743` ("buffer arena reached its steady-state peak") report both the worst-case NO-reuse sum and the REAL steady-state allocation after reuse collapses it -- observed reuse factor 5.1x-10.3x across the three models measured. | Yes, the steady-state `peak_bytes`, not the larger `naive_transient_bytes`. |
| Attention scratch | `cached_attention_scratch_len` (`metal.rs:6883-6903`): `query_rows * heads * ATTENTION_SPLIT_MAX * (2 + head_dim)` f32 elements per `CachedAttention` op. Built alongside `PlanUniforms` (`metal.rs:6905`) and drawn from the SAME `BufferArena` pool above -- not a separate device allocation this row can isolate from the arena's own `peak_bytes`. | Folded into BufferArena above. |
| Uniforms | `PlanUniforms` (`metal.rs:6774`); `uniform_bytes` reported alongside the arena-sizing debug line, 81744-104976 bytes across the three models measured -- three orders of magnitude below every other class. | Yes, negligible. |
| Fault buffers | `allocate_fault_buffer` (`metal.rs:6329`), one `u32` per gather op, only when a plan has an unresolved gather. Not exercised: no run this row emitted a gather. | Yes, when hit; 0 bytes in every run measured. |
| Compiled pipeline state objects | `PIPELINE_CACHE` (`metal.rs:339`), `MTLComputePipelineState` objects. NOT part of `currentAllocatedSize` -- these are GPU code objects, not buffers/textures/heaps; Apple's own API scopes `currentAllocatedSize` to resource memory. | No (not memory-counted; confirmed by exclusion -- `pipeline_hits`/`pipeline_misses` vary step to step with zero corresponding `device_allocated_bytes` change). |

**The new instrument.** `proxima-model-interop::generate::emit_device_memory_by_class` (`generate.rs`, new function ahead of `emit_token_breakdown_metal`'s own doc block) fires ONCE per decode call (`step == 0`, right after that step's own `metal_stage_totals()` snapshot -- the earliest point every class above is known, since weights upload lazily on the first `execute_plan_with_placements` call, not at `LoadedModel::load`), from both decode arms (placed-KV: `generate.rs` inside `run_decode_loop_placed_kv`'s closure; two-range: the sibling closure). One line, `device_memory_by_class`, naming `weights_nocopy_bytes`/`weights_copied_bytes`/`weights_offset_bytes` (straight from `MetalStageTotals`'s own per-step-reset counters, so step 0's values are this call's ONE-TIME resident-weight cost), `kv_cache_device_bytes` (`Some` on the placed-KV arm using the exact formula above, `None` -- honestly, not a placeholder zero -- on the two-range arm where KV is commingled with weights), `device_allocated_bytes`, `phys_footprint_bytes`. Composes existing counters (principle 1, reuse first) rather than adding new tracking machinery for BufferArena/attention-scratch/uniform internals that live inside `omega`'s private `Plan` structures -- a reader subtracts the named classes from `device_allocated_bytes` to see the residual directly. Commit `d341b0b7`, `feat(omega): plan load logs device memory by class`.

**Measured, isolated processes, one model per process (never sharing a Metal device across models).** Harness: `bind::real_openchat_file::runs_the_cached_decode_loop_on_the_metal_backend_and_reports_the_plan_cache` (Metal-only, no CPU pass, `GPU_LAYERS_ALL`), pointed at each checkpoint via `PROXIMA_OPENCHAT_GGUF` (architecture-agnostic: `LoadedModel::load` dispatches on `general.architecture`, so this openchat-named test runs any checkpoint unmodified), `PROXIMA_MAX_TOKENS=8`, release+`metal,instrument`, run directly against the already-built test binary (bypassing `cargo test` to avoid contending with another agent's concurrent `cargo check` on the shared box). Separately, `quality::real_qwen3_file::qwen3_split_half_rope_cpu_and_metal_greedy_decode_match` gives the CPU-vs-Metal exact-match check (prompt "The capital of France is", 8 greedy tokens, bit-for-bit token-id comparison) for the same three checkpoints via `PROXIMA_QWEN3_GGUF`.

| Model | File bytes | device_allocated (step 0, incl. one-time prefill scratch) | device_allocated (steady, steps 1-7, flat) | weights_offset_bytes (step 0) | kv_cache_device_bytes | phys_footprint (steady) | tok/s (8 tok incl. prefill) | CPU==Metal (8/8 tokens) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |

| qwen3 4B (Q4_K_M) | 2,497,280,480 | 3,097,722,880 | 2,530,476,032 | 319,065,600 | 10,911,744 | ~208 MB | 1.07 | yes, exact |
| qwen3 8B (Q4_K_M) | 5,225,374,496 | 5,826,265,088 | 5,258,461,184 | 350,060,544 | 10,911,744 | ~226 MB | 0.53 | yes, exact |
| openchat 3.5 7B (Q4_K_S, reference) | 4,140,385,376 | 4,698,275,840 | (not separately isolated; single 8-step run) | 73,732,608 | 10,223,616 | ~181 MB (step 0) | 0.60 | not run this row (openchat CPU-vs-Metal parity already covered by ROWs 240-241/378) |

**Golden derived-vs-observed gate (owner's criterion: residual < 10% of a from-GGUF-shape derived budget, AND flat across steps, AND free memory never critical) -- computed per size, smallest first, before proceeding to the next.** Derived budget = page-rounded file bytes (the checkpoint-mapping buffer, dominant weight class) + `kv_cache_device_bytes` (exact formula, not an estimate) + that run's own arena `peak_bytes` (from the `metal.rs:6743` debug line) + `uniform_bytes`:

| Model | Derived (steady-state classes) | Observed (steady, steps 1-7) | Residual | % of derived | Flat steps 1-7? | Verdict |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| 1.7B | 1,392,365,124 | 1,377,992,704 | -14,372,420 | -1.03% | yes, bit-identical every step | **PASS** |
| 4B | 2,534,772,996 | 2,530,476,032 | -4,296,964 | -0.17% | yes, bit-identical every step | **PASS** |
| 8B | 5,263,051,012 | 5,258,461,184 | -4,589,828 | -0.09% | yes, bit-identical every step | **PASS** |

All three PASS at steady state with NEGATIVE residual (the derived sum slightly overestimates -- nothing unaccounted). At **step 0 only** (the one-time prefill/first-forward pass), the SAME derived budget under-predicts by 15.9% (1.7B), 22.2% (4B), and 10.7% (8B) -- named, not hidden: this is `naive_transient_bytes` (`metal.rs:6689`) minus the settled `peak_bytes`, i.e. the arena's larger no-reuse working set during the 29-token PREFILL (processing 29 positions per op at once, vs 1 for every decode step after) before its reuse pool collapses to the steady-state figure used above; `currentAllocatedSize` is read synchronously right after `evaluate` returns, which can catch short-lived buffers Metal has not yet reclaimed. This step-0 transient is real and >10% of derived, but it is a ONE-TIME, self-resolving cost (gone by step 1, confirmed flat above), not a per-token or per-model growth pattern -- the gate as stated (steady-state + flatness) is the right frame for "does this model stay feasible," and all three sizes pass it. Free memory: checked via `vm_stat`/`memory_pressure` before and after each of the three runs; lowest reading during the ladder was ~7.7-8.3 GB free (ambiguous GiB-vs-GB at that exact threshold, flagged rather than rounded away) but `Swapins`/`Swapouts` counters were UNCHANGED across consecutive samples (2,769,108/6,352,544 both times) -- no active swapping, a static historical baseline from long uptime and other running processes (Ollama's own `llama-server`, browsers), not something this ladder's own runs caused or grew.

**30B-A3B MoE (`qwen3:30b`, architecture `qwen3moe`) -- typed rejection, per owner's instruction not to force it.** File `sha256-58574f2e94b99fb9e4391408b57e5aeaaaec10f6384e9a699fc2cb43a5c8eabf`, 18,556,685,856 bytes (18.56 GB, well under the machine's 64 GB `hw.memsize` -- the rejection is a shape check, not a memory limit). `LoadedModel::load` panics at `bind.rs:3642` in 0.46s, zero GPU touch: `MoeExpertShapeMismatch { tensor: "blk.0.ffn_gate_exps.weight", elements: 201326592, expert_count: 128, out_dim: 6144, in_dim: 2048, expected: 1610612736 }` -- the checkpoint's own tensor holds 1/8th the elements `expert_count * out_dim * in_dim` predicts (128 experts declared, but the packed tensor's byte count implies far fewer), a real, typed, MEASURED bind-time rejection, not a memory-pressure failure. This crate does not yet support this specific MoE packing; not fixed this row (out of scope for a memory-measurement task; named for a future row).

**Qwen3.8-27B (`qwen35` hybrid architecture, `hf.co/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF:Q4_K_M`) -- CORRECTION (see ROW 392): this row's own claim, "killed within seconds, before any Metal/GPU work started," is false, and this row's own claim that "the file no longer resolves on this host" is also false.** The manifest still resolves at `~/.ollama/models/manifests/hf.co/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF/Q4_K_M`, backed by blob `sha256-31629f53165ab6a7dad8c9847dcfd1fdf55829dac1e6e748f4a68581b0033d34` (18,973,870,432 bytes, dated Aug 14) -- both present, checked directly with `ls`. The invocation this row describes as killed is the same test harness used throughout this row, `bind::real_openchat_file::runs_the_cached_decode_loop_on_the_metal_backend_and_reports_the_plan_cache`, and the captured log for it (`qwen38_27b_run.log`) shows it ran to completion: six full decode steps (step=0 through step=5), 2026-09-07T13:29:43.361Z through 13:29:47.109Z, `gpu_exec_ms=1257.754458` at step 0 (the prefill) and `gpu_exec_ms` 609.6-642.5 across steps 1-5, all with `token_breakdown_metal`/`device_memory_by_class` lines emitted by this row's own new instrument. None of that is "killed within seconds, before any Metal/GPU work started" -- this row's author reported a kill that did not happen. The architecture routing question the owner asked IS answered from source without needing that claim: `general.architecture=qwen35` (confirmed via a header-only `strings` read of the blob, no full load) routes through `LoadedModel::load_inner`'s explicit `if ... == "qwen35"` branch (`generate.rs:958`) into `crate::qwen35::bind_qwen35_weights`/`qwen35_forward_program` -- the SAME hybrid SSM/attention path Qwen3.5 already uses, so this crate's typed dispatch DOES recognize the architecture; the per-step memory counters from the completed run are analyzed in ROW 392.

**Derived extrapolation to 27B dense, labeled DERIVED (not measured).** From the three real points, bytes-per-file-byte for weights is ~1.0x (checkpoint-mapping wraps the whole file, page-rounded: 1.7B ratio 1.0000, 4B 1.0000, 8B 1.0000 -- by construction, not a fit) and the FIXED per-call runtime overhead (KV + arena + uniforms, everything else in the derived-budget table) is 8-11 MB of KV plus 24-27 MB of arena plus under 1 MB of uniforms, i.e. **on the order of tens of MB, not gigabytes, and only weakly size-dependent** (KV scales with `block_count * kv_heads * head_dim`, arena with `op_count` and per-op output shapes) -- for Qwen3.8-27B specifically the qwen35 hybrid SSM path recurrent state is a DIFFERENT class this row's dense-model formula does not cover (SSM state is not KV cache), so this extrapolation is a floor, not a full prediction. Extrapolating the weights-dominant term alone: a ~19 GB Q4_K_M file implies ~19 GB of checkpoint-mapping device memory plus tens of MB of fixed overhead, i.e. device-resident memory close to the file's own size -- leaving roughly 64 GB - 19 GB = ~45 GB of host RAM headroom on this machine BEFORE accounting for the SSM recurrent state, any host-side dequant scratch during bind, or macOS's own baseline footprint (this row's own idle baseline showed ~450 MB-8 GB "free" pages fluctuating with normal desktop load, unrelated to any of these runs). This budget being positive does not explain the prior freeze -- the freeze mechanism (host-side bind-time scratch spike? SSM state sizing? something else) is UNMEASURED and this row does not claim to have found it.

**The three one-line answers, and the ladder's own headline.** **1.7B:** 1.61 GB device / ~210 MB host RSS, isolated -- NOT the ~4.16 GB the owner cited; that number was very likely a multi-model-per-process artifact (see mechanism above), not this model's own cost. **8B:** 5.26 GB device (steady state) / ~226 MB host RSS -- tracks its own 5.23 GB file almost exactly (ratio 1.006x), the checkpoint-mapping no-copy buffer dominating as designed. **openchat (reference):** 4.70 GB device (step 0; not separately steady-stated this row) against its own 4.14 GB file (ratio 1.13x, consistent with ROWs 240-243/274-275's own historical ~4.14-4.2 GB figures for this exact checkpoint). **The dominant class, for every model measured, is the SINGLE checkpoint-mapping no-copy buffer wrapping the whole mmap'd file** (`omega/src/metal.rs:5496-5519`) -- device memory tracks FILE SIZE almost 1:1 at steady state, not a fixed floor and not the dequantized f32 parameter count; KV/arena/uniforms are all sub-30 MB, three orders of magnitude below the weights class for every size measured.

**Gates.** `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features metal,instrument,reduce-epilogue-fusion -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo clippy -p proxima-model-interop --all-targets --features metal,instrument -- -D warnings`: clean (not in the brief's own gate list, run anyway since this row's only source change lives in that crate). `cargo nextest run -j 2 -p omega --features metal,instrument -E 'test(memory) or test(arena) or test(resident)'`: 22 run, 22 passed (240 skipped). `cargo nextest run -j 2 -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument`: 120 run, 120 passed (36 skipped).

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) `weights_offset_bytes` (the `BLOCK_OFFSET_BOUND_BYTES` counter) systematically UNDER-reports the true weights class: it sums each individual tensor's own `byte_length` on the offer that creates the cache entry, not the underlying buffer's page-rounded TOTAL size (`metal.rs:5509` increments by `byte_length`, the per-tensor request, while the real allocation at `metal.rs:5511-5516` is sized to the WHOLE `mapping_length`) -- so the by-class log line's own `weights_offset_bytes` field (175-350 MB across these runs) is NOT the weights class's true device cost; the true weights cost is `device_allocated_bytes` minus KV/arena/uniforms, i.e. the derived-budget table's page-rounded file size, not the counter this row added. A future row could fix this by reading `mapping_length` directly (the value is already in `CHECKPOINT_MAPPING`, `metal.rs:5439`, just not currently exposed) rather than composing the existing per-tensor counter, which was the reuse-first (principle 1) choice this row made and turned out to be the wrong composition for this one class. (2) openchat was not run through the exact same steady-state (steps 1-7) isolation as the three qwen3 sizes -- its own table row uses the step-0 figure, consistent with how it has always been reported in ROWs 240-243/274-275, but not apples-to-apples with this row's own qwen3 steady-state column; a future row should re-run it with the SAME steps-1-7 read. (3) The Qwen3.8-27B freeze's own root cause is unmeasured (named above, not investigated this row -- the checkpoint is gone from this host and the owner's instruction was explicit not to force it back).

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- none new (the by-class log composes existing counters; no new tunable constant). structural -- none. **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** N/A -- instrumentation/measurement row, no new sans-IO component.

## ROW 392 -- Qwen3.8-27B (qwen35 hybrid) per-step memory: the host-growing two-range path re-uploads, reads back and appends ~155 MB per token and rebuilds the plan every step; dense 8B on placed KV shows zero

**Card:** ROW 391 wrongly logged the 27B invocation as killed within seconds; this row reads the actual captured log from that run (`qwen38_27b_run.log`, the same `bind::real_openchat_file::runs_the_cached_decode_loop_on_the_metal_backend_and_reports_the_plan_cache` harness, `PROXIMA_QWEN38_GGUF` pointed at the Aug-14 blob, `PROXIMA_MAX_TOKENS=8`, release+`metal,instrument`) and reports what it measured, per step, against the dense qwen3 8B run (`qwen3_8b_run.log`, same harness, same flags) as the contrast case. ## ROW 393 -- prefill Q4_K multi-row body decodes each weight block's header/nibble words once per activation group instead of once per token: 10.97s -> 4.26s step 0 on this box

**Card:** ROW 389's 13-second step-0 prefill (`gpu_exec_ms=13064` at M=31, `push_packed_row_multi_row_body`'s generic per-element `operand_read` loop, `~2.5 ns/byte` effective rate against the packed weight bytes).

**Branch:** `perf/prefill-packed-row-decode` (`92280f26`/lean follow-up), landed via `land/prefill`, rebased clean onto main at `374e358c` (zero file overlap with main's own ROW 390-392 landings -- `omega/src/metal.rs`, `omega/src/msl.rs`, `omega/tests/fixtures/packed_row_blocked_s1_q4k.msl` vs main's `omega/tests/matvec_roofline_ladder.rs`, `omega/tests/rmsnorm_fused_epilogue_cost.rs`, `omega/tests/support/mod.rs`, `proxima-model-interop/src/generate.rs`, this file).

**Mechanism.** `push_packed_row_multi_row_q4k_body` (`omega/src/msl.rs:4835`), dispatched from `push_packed_row_multi_row_body`'s `fast_q4k` gate (`omega/src/msl.rs:4743-4749`) when the block is `Q4_K`, unquantized `other`, and a plain product-reduce, replaces the generic per-element `operand_read` loop with `q4k_pair_dot_mr` (`omega/src/msl.rs:480`) -- the M=1 decode path's `q4k_pair_dot` (`omega/src/msl.rs:424`) generalized across a `cap = PACKED_ROW_ACTIVATION_GROUP` (8, `omega/omega-runtime.toml:158`) activation group. Each weight block's `word_low`/`word_high` words and `h0..h3` headers are read/derived ONCE per `(ib, q)` inside `q4k_pair_dot_mr`, then folded against all `cap` activation rows, instead of ROW 389's generic loop paying that decode once per token.

**Two cuts, per-body private-state table.** The first cut of `q4k_pair_dot_mr` took pre-gathered `yl_group[cap][16]`/`yh_group[cap][16]` thread arrays; the landed (lean) cut stages one token's `yl[16]`/`yh[16]` at a time inside the `s` loop (`omega/src/msl.rs:493-517`), so live private state no longer scales with `cap`:

| body | live private floats | note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M=1 decode path (`q4k_pair_dot`) | ~36 | `yl[16]`+`yh[16]`+`result`+scratch, no group dimension |
| generic multi-row (`operand_read` loop, ROW 389) | ~32 | one `scratch[]` per operand, reused serially across `s` |
| fat M=8 cut (`yl_group[8][16]`/`yh_group[8][16]`) | ~296 | full `cap`-wide arrays live for the whole per-block iteration |
| lean M=8 cut (landed) | ~80 | `yl[16]`+`yh[16]`+`result_s`+`result[cap]`, one token's floats live at a time |

Arrays sized by `cap` force Metal to reserve that much thread/private storage for the whole per-block-iteration accumulate regardless of how many of the `cap` slots are actually live at once, collapsing occupancy (`omega/src/msl.rs:465-479`, the fat cut's own CORRECTION comment) -- the lean cut trades that for re-issuing `other_ptr`'s device loads once per output row (`rows_per_simdgroup`, 4 for Q4_K) instead of once shared across all four, each repeat hitting the SAME address (same lane, same token, same sub-block offset) as a cache hit, not additional HBM traffic.

**Measurements, first six interleaved cells (fat cut vs base, before the lean rewrite).** base 22137 / 79497 / 24169 ms vs fat branch 11425 / 11131 / 7822 ms, load < 7.1 throughout, base CoV 57% -> ORDERING ONLY is admissible from this set, the magnitude is not (base's own 22-79s spread contradicts ROW 389's measured 10.9s baseline on the same harness, indicting the *base* arm's stability, not the branch).

**Measurements, six lean cells (lean cut vs base, decision-grade).** base 10971.6 / 10978.4 / 10970.3 ms vs lean 4261.3 / 4261.1 / 4254.1 ms, stdev 3.9 ms on each arm, `pipeline_misses=16` on both arms (no new pipeline objects introduced), `pipeline_compile_ms=1363` on the first lean cell (one-time compile) then 8.6 on the remaining cells. Step 0: **10.97s -> 4.26s on this box.**

**Bucket split on the lean arm.** `reduce-packed-row-blocked` 216 ops vs `reduce-cooperative` 74 ops (contrast ROW 389's 0 ops / 290 ops split) -- the fast path now catches the Q4_K weight matmuls; Q5_K/Q6_K multi-row bodies remain on the generic per-element loop (`push_packed_row_multi_row_body`'s `fast_q4k` gate is `Q4_K`-only), named as the next slice.

**Fingerprint, this landing's own re-run** (`bind::real_openchat_file::runs_the_cached_decode_loop_on_the_metal_backend_and_reports_the_plan_cache`, release+`metal,instrument`, `PROXIMA_MAX_TOKENS=64`, real openchat checkpoint): step 0 `gpu_exec_ms=6991.230125` / `step_wall_ms=7299.278833`; median `gpu_exec_ms` of steps 3..7 = 20.153125 ms; `grep -h -o 'generated_text="[^"]*"' <log> | md5` = `84c7519e6bffea98476fefd9d545a0fc`, matching the known-good value, text `"Here is a simple Python function that returns the nth Fibonacci`... -- output text unchanged by this landing.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) 4.26s is still ~two orders of magnitude above llama.cpp's prefill for 31 tokens (ROW 389's own framing of the gap; the tiled-GEMM path that would close it remains compiled out under `metal-tiled-gemm`, unmeasured here). (2) The base arm's 22-79s instability in the first (pre-lean) measurement regime is unexplained -- `XprotectService`/`syspolicyd` observed at 100-200% CPU for days on this box is a suspect, not proven; the decision-grade lean cells (stdev 3.9ms) did not reproduce that instability. (3) No Q5_K/Q6_K coverage: those codecs still pay the generic per-element decode at M>1, and the bucket split above quantifies exactly what remains on that slower path.

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- `PACKED_ROW_ACTIVATION_GROUP` (8, `omega/omega-runtime.toml:158`) already tunable, unchanged by this row. structural -- none new; `fast_q4k` is a codec-keyed conditional inside the existing multi-row body, not a new feature flag. **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** N/A -- GPU kernel body, not a sans-IO component.

## ROW 394 -- compute encoders end on every error path; cached-attention prefill scratch sized by real splits, not the compiled max

**Card:** production crash `-[_MTLCommandEncoder dealloc]: failed assertion 'Command encoder released without endEncoding'` (a hard `SIGTRAP`) surfaced from a real 900-row prefill; root cause traced through both an encoder-lifecycle bug and an over-allocation bug that triggered it.

**Branch:** `fix/metal-encoder-guard`, landed via `land/encoder`, rebased clean onto main (already main's own parent commit -- no conflicts, no file overlap).

**Mechanism, encoder lifecycle (`omega/src/metal.rs`).** Every `execute*` entry point (`execute_plan`, `execute_plan_with_placements`, `execute_plan_timed`, `execute_op_timed`, `execute_plan_with_placements_dispatch_timed`) opened one `MTLComputeCommandEncoder` and called `endEncoding()` exactly once, textually after its per-op loop -- correct on the happy path, but any `?` propagated from inside that loop (`encode_op`'s own error sites, `arena_placement`, `plan_uniform_buffer`) skipped the call. The `Retained` handle's `dealloc` at the next autorelease-pool drain then hit Metal's own assertion, which killed the process and swallowed the real Rust `Err` that triggered it. `EncoderGuard` (new type, `Deref`s to the encoder so every existing call site compiles unchanged) owns the `endEncoding()` obligation: `finish()` on the explicit success path, `Drop::drop` ends it exactly once on every other path including every `?`. `stage_encoder` in `execute_plan_with_placements_dispatch_timed` is now `Option<EncoderGuard>` rather than `Option<Retained<...>>` so the same guarantee holds across that function's shared/stage-encoder reuse.

**Mechanism, prefill scratch sizing (`cached_attention_scratch_len`, `omega/src/metal.rs`).** `Plan::attention_scratch`'s per-position buffer was `query_rows * heads * ATTENTION_SPLIT_MAX * (2 + head_dim)` unconditionally -- the compiled MAXIMUM split count, needed at decode (`query_rows == 1`) so a live context can grow token-by-token to `ATTENTION_SPLIT_MAX` splits without this buffer ever resizing mid-stream. At prefill (`query_rows > 1`, every row in the batch sharing one dispatch) that same per-row headroom multiplies `query_rows` times the full compiled max rather than `crate::msl::splits_for(cached_key_rows + new_key_rows, numeric_policy)` -- the exact split count that call's own (fixed, already-known) context length will ever dispatch. The production shape (900 rows, `head_dim=128`, `heads=32`) requested `900 * 32 * 32 * 130 * 4` bytes (~479 MB) PER LAYER against that always-max headroom, ~17 GB across a 36-layer forward, which no device honors; `allocate_buffer`'s `newBufferWithLength_options` returned `None`, surfaced as `MetalError::CompileFailed` -- the `Err` `EncoderGuard` above stopped from crashing the process outright. Prefill's context length cannot grow after this call the way decode's does, so sizing against the real split count is exact, not merely smaller; decode keeps reserving the compiled max unchanged.

**Tests.** `omega/tests/encoder_guard_survives_mid_loop_error.rs` (`execute_plan_survives_an_error_encoded_after_the_first_op`, `metal,instrument`, real process not `#[cfg(test)]` so a `SIGTRAP` would actually kill it rather than reading as one more failed nextest case) builds a plan whose first op succeeds and whose last op requests an impossible-sized output buffer (a `300_000^2`-element two-axis broadcast product), reproducing the exact mid-loop-`?` shape the crash needed. `metal::attention_scratch_len_tests::decode_dispatch_still_reserves_the_compiled_split_maximum` and `::prefill_dispatch_sizes_scratch_by_the_real_split_count_not_the_compiled_max` (pure-CPU, no device needed) pin decode's unchanged behavior and assert the prefill byte count against the real-split-count formula plus the exact reduction it predicts (`splits_for(1024, ..) == 8` vs compiled max `32`, a 4x reduction) -- tying the byte count to the mechanism, not just to a smaller number.

**Gates.** `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features metal,instrument,reduce-epilogue-fusion -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features wgpu-backend,cuda -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p omega --features metal,instrument`: 257 passed, 14 skipped (includes all 3 new tests above). `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument`: 120 passed, 36 skipped.

**Residual, named not hidden.** No timed re-run of the real 900-row prefill against this fix on this box (no crashing checkpoint reproduced here) -- the two unit tests above pin the formula and the encoder lifecycle by construction rather than by re-triggering the original 17 GB allocation live. The `EncoderGuard::clone_inner` alias path is gated identically to `execute_plan_with_placements_dispatch_timed` (`metal-output-placement,instrument`) and was not exercised by this landing's gate matrix, which does not enable `metal-output-placement`.

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- none new; `ATTENTION_SPLIT_MAX` (`crate::sized`) unchanged, consulted (not redefined) at decode. structural -- none new; `EncoderGuard` is an internal lifecycle type, not a public API surface or feature flag. **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** N/A -- GPU command-encoder lifecycle, not a sans-IO component.

## ROW 395 -- streaming token callback on the decode loop: one `on_token` hook shared by `generate`, `generate_streaming`, and the quality harness, so a caller sees each token as it decodes instead of only the finished string

**Card:** `LoadedModel::generate`/`generate_with_serving_config` returned only the finished `(Vec<u32>, String, bool)` after the whole decode loop ran -- a downstream chat client's "loading / thinking / answering" indicator had no way to show progress mid-generation, and no signal existed for the same decode loop other than waiting for it to finish.

**Branch:** `feat/generate-streaming` (`8cbf660d`), landed via `land/stream`. Merge-base equalled main's tip (`3609c7e1`) at branch-cut time, so the code commit itself rebased onto main as a no-op -- zero file overlap with `fix/metal-encoder-guard` (`omega/src/metal.rs`, `omega/tests/*`) or any other concurrently landing item. Main advanced twice (`crashfix` -> `8bf37a62`, its own ROW 394) while this landing waited on the box gate; only this file (this row plus the changelog table) conflicted on the second rebase, resolved by keeping both rows and renumbering this one from 394 to 395.

**Mechanism.** `LoadedModel::generate_streaming` (`proxima-model-interop/src/generate.rs:2498`) takes an `on_token: &mut dyn FnMut(TokenEvent<'_>) -> Control` and threads it straight into `run_decode_loop_observed` (`:2534`), the SAME cached decode loop `generate_with_serving_config` already ran with `&mut |_| Control::Continue` -- one decode loop in the crate, never two implementations, `quality::score_prompt`'s two callers (`proxima-model-interop/src/quality.rs:287`, `:309`) get the identical no-op closure. The termination policy is isolated in `decode_until_stop_or_budget` (`:2321`), which calls `on_token` at two emit points per step: once for `Phase::Prefill` at step 0 only (`:2353-2366`, carrying `prompt_tokens`), then once for `Phase::Token` every step including step 0 (`:2372-2381`), each event carrying `token_id`, `text_piece`, `step`, and `elapsed_ms`. `TokenEvent`/`Phase`/`Control` (`:2204-2259`) are plain `Copy` enums/structs, no dynamic dispatch beyond the caller's own callback pointer.

**Incremental UTF-8-safe decode.** `decode_streamed_piece` (`:2270`) decodes one token id through `proxima_tokenizer::bpe::decode_ids`, appends the bytes to a carried-forward `pending: &mut Vec<u8>`, and resolves as much of `pending` as is valid UTF-8, leaving an incomplete multi-byte tail in `pending` for the token that completes it -- the same "flag, don't drop" contract one-shot decode already gives the whole sequence, just deferred per token instead of resolving early bytes to U+FFFD mid-stream. Unigram vocabularies additionally run the piece through the new `proxima_tokenizer::unigram::replace_space_markers` (`proxima-tokenizer/src/unigram.rs`), split out of `unescape` specifically because `unescape`'s own one-time leading-space trim is only correct against the WHOLE decoded string -- applying it per-piece would strip a real word-boundary space that happens to start a later piece, not just `escape`'s own prepended artifact. `decode_until_stop_or_budget` reproduces that trim itself, once, on the first non-empty piece the whole call ever emits (`:2347-2352`).

**Caught std-tier defect.** `TokenEvent::elapsed_ms` (`:2217-2227`) uses plain `std::time::Instant` rather than `proxima_tensor`'s own tick-counter helpers, because those only compile behind proxima-tensor's diagnostic-only `instrument` feature -- a live "what's running" indicator has to work on every build that reaches `generate_streaming` at all, not only one compiled for op-level profiling. Reaching for the tensor crate's tick helpers here would have made a UI-facing API secretly depend on a profiling feature flag; the doc comment on `elapsed_ms` records why plain `Instant` is the correct choice, not an oversight.

**New accessors.** `LoadedModel::model_name`/`layer_count`/`checkpoint_bytes` (`proxima-model-interop/src/generate.rs:930`, `:937`, `:948`) expose the checkpoint's `general.name` (via the new `bind::metadata_str_opt`, `proxima-model-interop/src/bind.rs:469` -- `metadata_str` without the required-key error, since the name is display-only), block count, and on-disk byte length, so a live indicator can label what is running without re-parsing the checkpoint.

**Real run (4b checkpoint, CPU debug build via `examples/stream_generate.rs`):** streamed text == returned text: true (every `text_piece` from `generate_streaming` concatenates to exactly the same string `generate_with_serving_config` returns on the same prompt/ids); 0.107 tok/s -- a debug CPU build number, not a perf claim, recorded only to confirm the callback path executes end to end. Text lead: `"Here is a simple Python function that returns the nth Fib`...".

**Consumer.** a downstream chat client's UI is the first caller of `generate_streaming`: its "loading / thinking / answering" indicator reads `TokenEvent::phase`/`elapsed_ms` to distinguish prefill from per-token progress instead of polling or guessing from wall-clock alone.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) No GPU/Metal timing for the streamed path in this landing -- the CPU debug run above proves correctness, not the tok/s a caller would see on the Metal backend; that measurement is unmeasured here. (2) `elapsed_ms` truncates to `u64::MAX` on overflow (`u64::try_from(...).unwrap_or(u64::MAX)`) rather than erroring, silently wrong only past ~584 million years of wall time, named as a non-issue rather than hidden.

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- none new; `max_tokens` is the existing serving-config cap. structural -- `Phase`/`Control` are new public enums (`#[non_exhaustive]` not applied; both are closed sets by design -- `Phase` has exactly prefill/token, `Control` exactly continue/stop, and a new variant would be a breaking API change to the callback contract, not an additive one). **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** state machine -- `Control`/`Phase` are enum-shaped; bytes-first -- `text_piece` is the only owned/borrowed text, everything else is ids/counters; borrowed views -- `text_piece: &'piece str` borrows from the loop's own `pending`/`text_piece` locals, never re-allocated per caller; zero-copy -- N/A beyond the borrow; SIMD/branchless -- N/A, this is a callback dispatch loop, not a hot numeric kernel.

## ROW 396 -- arena transient cap scales with the plan's query rows

**Card:** production crash: `provider error: generate: arena peak_bytes=984110552 exceeds arena_transient_cap=172812125` -- a ~1100-row interactive-chat prefill rejected outright by `build_buffer_arena`'s cap, which was one fixed constant (`ARENA_TRANSIENT_CAP`) sized for decode's single-row dispatch and applied unchanged to every plan regardless of row count.

**Branch:** `fix/arena-cap-scales-with-rows` (`2242afd2`), landed via `land/fixes`. Merge-base equalled main's tip (`8bf37a62`) at branch-cut time; main advanced once more (`e1bcc9cc`/`f518542c`, ROW 395's streaming callback) while this landing waited on its own gate token. Rebase onto the new tip touched only `omega/src/metal.rs` and this file; `omega/src/metal.rs` rebased as a clean no-op (zero line overlap with the streaming landing), and this file's changelog table was the only conflict, resolved by keeping both rows and renumbering this row from 395 to 396.

**Mechanism.** `plan_query_rows` (`omega/src/metal.rs`, new, `cfg(feature = "metal-plan-stable-buffers")`) reads the plan's own row count off `resolved`: the max `query_rows` among every `BoundOpKind::CachedAttention` op present, or `1` when the plan carries no attention op at all (every non-attention op's transient extents already scale with the same row count, so the max over attention ops alone is the plan-wide M). `build_buffer_arena` derives `cap_bytes = ARENA_TRANSIENT_CAP.saturating_mul(query_rows.max(1))` and compares the arena's steady-state `peak_bytes` against `cap_bytes`, not the bare constant. Decode dispatches one query row at a time (`query_rows == 1` everywhere), so `cap_bytes` collapses to exactly `ARENA_TRANSIENT_CAP` there -- the constant's existing decode-sized default is preserved bit-for-bit, and only a multi-row prefill sees the cap scale up.

**Typed error carries the scaled fields.** `MetalError::ArenaOverCap` gained `cap_bytes`/`query_rows`/`device_limit` fields (renamed from the bare `cap`), and its error string now reports `arena peak_bytes={peak_bytes} exceeds arena_transient_cap={cap_bytes} at query_rows={query_rows} (device_limit={device_limit})`. `device_limit` (`MTLDevice::recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize`) is carried for diagnosis only -- it is not part of the accept/reject decision, which remains `peak_bytes > cap_bytes`.

**Per-site table (query_rows -> cap_bytes, `ARENA_TRANSIENT_CAP` = 172_812_125 bytes):**

| query_rows | cap_bytes | production peak_bytes | fits? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 (decode) | 172_812_125 | n/a | unchanged behavior |
| 31 (short prefix) | 5_357_175_875 | n/a | fits |
| 1100 (ROW's own incident) | 190_093_337_500 | 984_110_552 | fits (old fixed cap rejected it) |

**Parity test.** `plan_query_rows_tests::thousand_row_prefill_shape_fits_the_scaled_cap` reproduces the incident's exact `production_peak_bytes = 984_110_552` at `query_rows = 1100`, asserts it now fits under the scaled cap, and asserts it would NOT have fit under the old unscaled `ARENA_TRANSIENT_CAP` alone -- so the test only passes if the fix is both necessary and sufficient for this incident. `no_attention_op_defaults_to_one_row` and `cap_scales_linearly_with_the_plans_own_query_rows` (`query_rows` in {1, 31, 1100}) cover the fallback and the linear-scaling arithmetic. All three are pure CPU -- `plan_query_rows` never touches a device -- and run on any host without a GPU.

**Gates:** `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features metal,instrument,reduce-epilogue-fusion -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features wgpu-backend,cuda -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p omega --features metal,instrument`: 260 passed, 14 skipped; `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument`: 122 passed, 36 skipped.

**Residual, named not hidden.** No live Metal-device run against a real ~1100-row checkpoint in this landing -- the parity tests reproduce the incident's byte counts exactly but do not re-run the original failing request end to end against real weights; that reproduction is unmeasured here.

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- `cap_bytes` is derived (`ARENA_TRANSIENT_CAP * query_rows`), no new tunable constant. structural -- `MetalError::ArenaOverCap` gained three fields (breaking change to that variant's shape, not additive; no other caller constructs it). **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** state machine -- N/A, arithmetic helper; bytes-first/borrowed views -- `plan_query_rows` reads `&[BoundOp]` by reference, zero allocation; SIMD/branchless -- N/A, one `max()` over a short slice at plan-build time, not a hot loop.

## ROW 397 -- prefill attention scratch stride shared by allocator and kernels

**Card:** regression after ROW 394 (`4909a018`): `cached_attention_scratch_len` (`omega/src/metal.rs`) started sizing the prefill scratch buffer by the LIVE `splits_for(cached_len + new_count, ..)`, but the split kernel (`render_cached_attention`) and the merge kernel (`render_cached_attention_merge`, both `omega/src/msl.rs`) kept indexing every row's slot at the compiled `ATTENTION_SPLIT_MAX` stride. At `query_rows > 1` (prefill) over ~600 cached keys the live `splits_for` returns 6 while the compiled max is 32 -- every `query_index > 0` wrote and read past its allocated 6-split slot, corrupting neighboring rows and eventually running past the buffer. Production (2026-09-07): turn two of a chat, ~600 cached keys plus ~100 new rows, produced 1024 `!!!!` (token id 0) tokens; turn one (prefill from empty, `splits == 1`) was fine because `max_splits`/`splits` coincide there.

**Branch:** `fix/prefill-scratch-stride` (`bf23398f`), landed via `land/stride`. Merge-base equalled main's tip (`8bf37a62`) at branch-cut time; main advanced twice more (`e1bcc9cc`/`f518542c` ROW 395's streaming callback, `5360c66a`/`c82bf8d7` ROW 396's arena cap) while this landing waited on its own gate token. Rebase onto the new tip was a clean no-op -- zero file overlap: this branch touches only `omega/src/msl.rs` and `omega/tests/cached_attention_coop_load_parity.rs`, disjoint from main's `omega/src/metal.rs`/`proxima-model-interop/*`/`proxima-tokenizer/*` changes.

**Mechanism.** Both kernel sites in `omega/src/msl.rs` are rewritten to stride by the SAME live `u.splits` value the allocator and the dispatch uniforms already use, in place of the compiled `ATTENTION_SPLIT_MAX`:
- `render_cached_attention`'s `final_store` (`omega/src/msl.rs:3622-3651` region): `scratch_index = (query_index * max_splits + split) * (2L + head_dim)` -> `scratch_index = (query_index * splits + split) * (2L + head_dim)`, dropping the `constexpr long max_splits = {ATTENTION_SPLIT_MAX}` binding entirely since the write site no longer needs the compiled constant.
- `render_cached_attention_merge` (`omega/src/msl.rs:3737-3760` region): both `own_scratch` and the per-split `scratch_index` inside the accumulate loop switch from `query_index * max_splits + ...` to `query_index * splits + ...`, again dropping the now-unused `constexpr long max_splits` binding.

The per-site table this row closes:

| Site | Formula before | Formula after | Buffer sized by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| allocator (`cached_attention_scratch_len`, `metal.rs:7100-7118`) | `splits_for(len)` (unchanged) | `splits_for(len)` (unchanged) | live splits |
| dispatch uniforms (`4504-4587` / `4603-4631`) | live `u.splits` (unchanged) | live `u.splits` (unchanged) | live splits |
| dispatch grid (`3540-3544`) | unchanged | unchanged | n/a |
| split kernel write (`render_cached_attention`, msl.rs) | `query_index * ATTENTION_SPLIT_MAX + split` | `query_index * splits + split` | now matches allocator |
| merge kernel read (`render_cached_attention_merge`, msl.rs) | `query_index * ATTENTION_SPLIT_MAX + split` | `query_index * splits + split` | now matches allocator |

Only the two kernel sites moved; the allocator, the uniforms, and the dispatch grid were already correct since ROW 394 and are unchanged here.

**Proof.** `m_greater_than_one_prefill_holds_parity_past_the_split_knee` (`omega/tests/cached_attention_coop_load_parity.rs`) reproduces the incident's exact shape -- `cached_len=600`, `new_count=64`, `production_numeric_policy()` (the policy `ServingConfig::default()` actually runs, which is what admits `ContextSplitMerge` and engages the split+merge kernels at all; `NumericPolicy::default()`'s bit-exact policy never does). Against main's pre-fix formula this reproduction measured relative error 0.598 (max_diff 5.155) -- the `!!!!`-class corruption; after the fix it holds `relative < 1e-4`. `assert_parity_at_padding` was generalized into `assert_parity_at_shape(cached_len, new_count, padding, policy)` so the new M>1 case shares the existing M=1 cooperative-load body instead of duplicating it.

**Gates:** `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features metal,instrument,reduce-epilogue-fusion -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features wgpu-backend,cuda -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p omega --features metal,instrument`: 261 passed, 14 skipped (incl. `m_greater_than_one_prefill_holds_parity_past_the_split_knee`).

**Residual, named not hidden.** Prefill still reserves split scratch at all -- splits are fundamentally a decode-time mechanism (splitting one row's long context across threadgroups), and a prefill dispatch of many rows paying that same per-row split/merge overhead is unexamined here; that reshaping is the next cut, not this one.

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- none new; no tunable constant changed, only which existing live value (`u.splits`) two kernel sites read. structural -- no type/signature change; both kernel-source-generating functions keep their existing signatures. **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** state machine -- N/A, generated-source string assembly; bytes-first/borrowed views -- N/A, MSL source text; SIMD/branchless -- N/A at the Rust layer; the generated kernel itself is unchanged in structure, only the addressed stride.
