## ROW 398 -- a partial utf-8 tail flushes as replacement char

**Card:** a downstream chat client reported `decoded bytes are not valid utf-8` at a 32-token cutoff on a ~1100-token prompt. Cause: `decode_streamed_piece` (`proxima-model-interop/src/generate.rs:2270`) returned `Err` when a buffered incomplete lead byte was followed by a non-continuation token -- `core::str::Utf8Error::error_len()` returning `Some(_)` -- a normal autoregressive outcome, not corruption. A production report of a chat turn ending mid multibyte glyph, or a budget-exhausted decode stopping mid CJK/emoji character, hit the same path.

**Branch:** `fix/decode-partial-utf8-tail` (`ecdfcf55`), landed via `land/utf8`. Merge-base equalled main's tip (`818f5e46`, ROW 397) at branch-cut time -- rebase was a clean no-op, zero commits to replay.

**Mechanism.** `decode_streamed_piece` used to treat any `Utf8Error` with `error_len().is_some()` (a genuinely invalid byte run, not just an incomplete tail) as a hard `Err`. That conflated two different situations: pending bytes that are STILL incomplete and might resolve once more bytes arrive (`error_len() == None`, the existing streaming-defer path, unchanged) and pending bytes that are PROVEN unresolvable because the byte that arrived cannot continue them (`error_len() == Some(_)`) -- the latter can never become valid no matter what token comes next, so erroring the whole decode call over it serves no caller. The fix loops: each `Some(_)` arm flushes the proven-valid prefix (via the new `push_valid_prefix` helper, which both call sites already know is valid by `Utf8Error::valid_up_to`'s own contract), appends one U+FFFD for the unresolvable run, drains `valid_up_to + bad_len` bytes from `pending`, and continues the loop over whatever bytes remain -- so one bad run never fails the whole call, and decoding resumes normally on the bytes after it. The `error_len() == None` (still-incomplete) path is untouched: those bytes still wait in `pending` for the token that completes them, exactly as before this fix.

**Proof.** Two new tests in `proxima-model-interop/src/generate.rs`: `budget_ending_mid_multibyte_character_flags_instead_of_erroring` reproduces a real Qwen3 byte-fallback token (`vocab_with_eos`'s own `<0xE4>`, the first of three bytes a real 3-byte codepoint like `中` starts with) with the budget running out before the other two bytes arrive, and asserts the caller-visible outcome matches `proxima_tokenizer::decode`'s own one-shot "flag, don't drop" contract for the same truncated ids (`"Hi\u{FFFD}"`). `incomplete_lead_byte_followed_by_a_non_continuation_byte_flags_and_resumes` covers the other resolution path -- the lead byte followed by plain ASCII (never a valid continuation byte) -- and asserts the streamed event text is `"\u{FFFD}Hi"`: the unresolvable lead byte flags as one U+FFFD, then decoding resumes normally on the bytes that follow it. Real check (2026-09-07, release build, GPU/Metal backend, Qwen3 4B Q4_K checkpoint via ollama's local blob store, a 1045-word/~1100-token repeated-sentence prompt, `max_tokens=32`): `gguf_generate` exited cleanly with no `InvalidUtf8` error, `tokens_generated = 32`, `generated_text = " The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog while the orange cat watches quietly from the sunny windowsill.\n\nOkay, let me try to figure out what's going"` -- the exact class of long-prompt/short-budget cutoff the original report hit, run clean under the fix.

**Gates:** `cargo clippy -p proxima-model-interop --all-targets --features metal,instrument -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument`: 124 passed, 37 skipped (incl. both new tests); `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features std`: 106 passed, 26 skipped (the std tier still compiles and passes with this change).

**Residual, named not hidden.** An incomplete trailing tail at the very end of a decode session (bytes that are still ambiguous, `error_len() == None`) is still deferred rather than flushed -- that is the pre-existing, correct streaming-defer behavior this fix does not touch. Only the PROVEN-unresolvable case (`error_len() == Some(_)`) changed.

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- none; no tunable constant. structural -- no public signature change; `decode_streamed_piece` keeps its existing signature, `push_valid_prefix` is a new private helper. **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** state machine -- the byte-accumulation loop over `pending` is already enum-free scalar state (a `Vec<u8>` buffer plus a loop), unchanged in shape; bytes-first -- yes, `pending: &mut Vec<u8>` throughout; borrowed views -- the `core::str::from_utf8` validation borrows `pending`'s bytes directly, no copy until a valid prefix is pushed into the output `String`; SIMD/branchless -- N/A, this is UTF-8 boundary bookkeeping on a handful of bytes per token, not a hot numeric loop.

## ROW 399 -- one lossy utf-8 decode for streamed and batch paths

**Card:** a downstream chat client reported `decoded bytes are not valid utf-8` again, this time on a >budget prompt where the id buffer's OWN token, not a boundary artifact of streaming, decoded to a genuinely invalid byte run. Root cause: `pipe::decode` (`proxima-tokenizer/src/pipe.rs:149`, pre-fix) still hard-errored on a proven-invalid run -- `Utf8Error::error_len()` returning `Some(_)` -- exactly the case ROW 398 already fixed for `decode_streamed_piece`, because the one-shot `decode` runs on the whole id buffer at the end of every generation (`proxima-model-interop/src/generate.rs:3137` and `:3635`) and never went through the streaming fix. The two decode paths had drifted: one lossy, one still typed-error, over the identical byte-run shape.

**Branch:** `fix/decode-invalid-run-replacement` (`325b3895`), landed via `land/decode`. Merge-base equalled main's tip (`5665bd0c`, ROW 398) at branch-cut time -- rebase was a clean no-op, zero commits to replay.

**Mechanism.** `push_valid_prefix` and `decode_streamed_piece`'s loop from ROW 398 are lifted out of `proxima-model-interop` into a new shared free function, `drain_lossy_utf8` (`proxima-tokenizer/src/pipe.rs:133`): drains as much valid UTF-8 as it can from a `&mut Vec<u8>` into a `&mut String` in place, flushing exactly one U+FFFD per proven-invalid run (`error_len() == Some(_)`) and resuming on whatever bytes remain, while leaving a still-incomplete trailing sequence (`error_len() == None`) untouched in the buffer for the caller to decide. `pipe::decode` now calls `drain_lossy_utf8` on the full id-buffer bytes and, if anything remains pending afterward (an incomplete trailing sequence at the very end of the whole sequence, since there is no next call coming), flushes it as one trailing U+FFFD itself -- so the one-shot batch path and the per-token streaming path in `generate.rs` now run the identical routine over the identical byte-run shapes, instead of two hand-written copies that could (and did) diverge. `push_valid_prefix` is deleted; `decode_streamed_piece` calls `drain_lossy_utf8` directly and keeps its own incomplete-tail deferral semantics (it does NOT force-flush the tail, unlike the one-shot `decode`, since a future token may still complete it). `TokenizerError::InvalidUtf8` is no longer producible from `decode` at all -- `decode`'s only remaining error path is `TokenizerError::TokenIdOutOfRange`.

**Proof.** `decoding_an_invalid_byte_run_mid_buffer_flushes_one_replacement_char_and_resumes` (`proxima-tokenizer/src/tests.rs`) replaces the old typed-error test: ids `[b'H', 0xE4, b'i', b'!']` (`0xE4` alone is never a legal continuation byte at that position, a genuinely invalid run sitting between two ASCII bytes) now decode to `"H\u{FFFD}i!"` instead of erroring.

**Gates:** `cargo clippy -p proxima-tokenizer -p proxima-model-interop --all-targets --features metal,instrument -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-tokenizer`: 86 passed, 0 skipped; `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument`: 124 passed, 37 skipped; `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features std`: 106 passed, 26 skipped. Invariant grep: `push_valid_prefix` has zero remaining references anywhere in-tree; `drain_lossy_utf8` is the sole implementation both `pipe::decode` and `decode_streamed_piece` call.

**Residual, named not hidden.** `TokenizerError::InvalidUtf8` remains a declared enum variant (kept for API/wire compatibility with any external caller still matching on it) but is now dead on every path this crate itself exercises -- `decode` cannot produce it and nothing else constructs it. A future cleanup could deprecate or remove the variant entirely; left in place here since removing a public enum variant is a breaking API change out of scope for a decode-correctness fix.

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- none; no tunable constant. structural -- new public function `drain_lossy_utf8(&mut Vec<u8>, &mut String)` re-exported from `proxima-tokenizer`; `decode`'s public signature is unchanged, only its error surface narrowed. **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** state machine -- the drain loop is the same enum-free scalar `Vec<u8>` + loop shape as ROW 398, now shared instead of duplicated; bytes-first -- yes, `pending: &mut Vec<u8>` throughout; borrowed views -- `core::str::from_utf8` validates `pending`'s bytes in place, no copy until a valid prefix is pushed into `output`; SIMD/branchless -- N/A, UTF-8 boundary bookkeeping on a handful of bytes per call, not a hot numeric loop.

## ROW 400 -- load-time device-memory budget gates serving before the first weight upload

**Card:** the owner's rule -- "memory is a feasibility constraint" -- had no load-time enforcement: `ServingConfig::gpu_memory_fit` (`-fit`) existed only as a rejected `UnsupportedServingConfig` stub, so a checkpoint whose weights plus KV cache plus arena overhead exceed the host's own device memory only failed later, mid-forward, at whatever buffer allocation happened to be the one that finally overflowed -- if it failed at all rather than silently degrading.

**Branch:** `feat/load-time-fit-gate` (`10c935c6`, `fad7cacd`, `b2b1b544`), landed via `land/wip-1`. Merge-base `f518542c` (ROW 395) at branch-cut; rebased onto main's tip through ROW 399 (four intervening fix/docs pairs: ROW 396 arena transient cap, ROW 397 prefill scratch stride, ROW 398/399 lossy utf-8 decode) -- clean rebase, zero conflicts, all four commits touched `omega/src/metal.rs`'s `ArenaOverCap`/`build_buffer_arena` region and `generate.rs`'s `decode_streamed_piece`, disjoint from this branch's own additions.

**Mechanism.** Three layers, each a plain-data/pure-function surface (principle 1 -- no new pipe, no new runtime type):

1. `omega::metal::system_memory_facts()` (`omega/src/metal.rs`) probes the Metal device once per load and emits one `system_facts` telemetry event: `recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize`, `maxBufferLength`, `hasUnifiedMemory`, `currentAllocatedSize` (all straight `MTLDevice` accessor pass-throughs) plus `physical_memory_bytes` (`sysctlbyname("hw.memsize")`, read the same way `page_size` already reads a host fact through `libc`).
2. `proxima_model_interop::memory_fit` (new module, alloc/core only, zero `omega` dependency so its arithmetic is testable with a hand-built `HostMemoryLimit` fake) derives a `MemoryBudget` by class -- `WeightClassBytes` (dense/expert/table, from `bind::tensor_bytes_by_class`'s GGUF tensor-name split, plus qwen35's own SSM conv/state bytes), page-rounded dense bytes (the checkpoint's mmap is one no-copy `MTLBuffer`), placed-KV bytes at the requested `context_length` (`kv_row_bytes = kv_heads * head_dim * 8`, mirroring `run_decode_loop_placed_kv`'s own formula exactly), and a fixed arena allowance. `fit_context_length` compares the total against `HostMemoryLimit::available_bytes` (`min(recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize, hw.memsize) - os_headroom_bytes`) and returns `FitOutcome::Fits`, `ReducedContext { from, to }` (shrinks `context_length` to the largest value that fits, with a `context_length_reduced` warn event), or `InteropError::MemoryBudgetExceeded` naming every class and number when even `context_length = 1` cannot fit.
3. `LoadedModel::apply_memory_fit_gate`, called from `generate_with_serving_config` before `BackendRuntime::new` ever asks a device for a buffer, wires the two together: a no-op when `gpu_memory_fit` is `false` or this host has no Metal device (probe failure fails OPEN, not closed -- a probe this crate cannot evaluate is not evidence the load is unsafe). `ServingConfig::gpu_memory_fit` now defaults `true` (the branch's one deliberate deviation from the owner's exact `-fit off` invocation, documented at the field and at `Default`) -- a load that silently exceeds host memory is the defect this field closes, so the safe behavior is what a caller gets without asking.

`LOAD_TIME_FIT_OS_HEADROOM_BYTES` (8 GiB default) and `LOAD_TIME_FIT_ARENA_ALLOWANCE_BYTES` (28_311_552 bytes, the largest measured `BufferArena` peak across ROW 391's own per-step table) are build-time constants from `omega-runtime.toml`'s new `[load_time_fit]` section (principle 12), both env-overridable (`OMEGA_LOAD_TIME_FIT_OS_HEADROOM_BYTES`/`OMEGA_LOAD_TIME_FIT_ARENA_ALLOWANCE_BYTES`).

**Rebase reconciliation.** No textual conflicts, but the rebase surfaced two real correctness gaps in the branch's own commits that a clean textual merge could not have caught: (a) `checkpoint_weight_bytes`/`memory_fit` are the ONLY consumers of `bind::tensor_bytes_by_class`, `memory_fit::{kv_row_bytes, WeightClassBytes::total_bytes, MemoryBudget, HostMemoryLimit, FitOutcome, fit_context_length}`, and `qwen35_ssm_state_bytes` -- every one metal-gated (`apply_memory_fit_gate`'s own `#[cfg(all(feature = "metal", target_os = "macos"))]`) -- so `cargo nextest run --features std` (no metal) hit ten `warnings = "deny"` dead-code errors the branch's own commits never gated against; fixed by cfg-gating the module (`any(test, all(feature = "metal", target_os = "macos"))`), the field, its three construction sites, and `tensor_bytes_by_class` to match. (b) two of the crate's own config-as-mirror tests (`kv_bucket_tokens_agrees_across_literal_and_default_override`, `numeric_policy_agrees_across_literal_and_default_override`) build a full `ServingConfig` literal by hand to assert it equals a `..Default::default()` override, and both still hard-coded `gpu_memory_fit: false` from before this branch flipped the default -- caught immediately by the metal,instrument gate, fixed by updating both literals to `true`.

**Real facts, this box** (`omega::metal::system_memory_facts()`, `generate::memory_fit_gate_tests::gate_on_leaves_a_generously_fitting_context_length_unchanged`'s own probe): `recommended_max_working_set_size = 51_539_607_552` (48 GiB), `max_buffer_length = 38_654_705_664`, `has_unified_memory = true`, `physical_memory_bytes = 68_719_476_736` (64 GiB) -- `limit_bytes = min(...) = 51_539_607_552`, `available_bytes = 51_539_607_552 - 8_589_934_592 = 42_949_672_960` (~40 GiB). A 4B Q4_K checkpoint (~2.5 GB weights) and a 27B checkpoint (~19 GB weights) both sit well under that ceiling even before subtracting KV/arena, so neither real-model test in the capability matrix crossed the gate.

**Proof.** `memory_fit::tests` (7 tests, `--features std`, no metal): `kv_row_bytes_matches_the_placed_kv_capacity_formula`, `budget_matches_hand_computed_formula_for_the_fixture_shape`, `fits_within_a_generous_limit_without_reducing_context`, `reduces_context_length_to_the_largest_value_that_fits`, `errors_with_every_class_when_weights_alone_exceed_the_limit` -- pure arithmetic against hand-computed fixtures, no device. `generate::memory_fit_gate_tests` (2 tests, `metal,instrument`, real Metal device required): `gate_off_leaves_an_otherwise_infeasible_context_length_untouched` (an explicit opt-out leaves `context_length = u32::MAX` untouched), `gate_on_leaves_a_generously_fitting_context_length_unchanged` (this box's real device limit comfortably fits a 1 MB fixture checkpoint's budget, `context_length` unchanged) -- the one real-device probe this landing runs, no model.

**Gates:** `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features metal,instrument,reduce-epilogue-fusion -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features wgpu-backend,cuda -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo clippy -p proxima-model-interop --all-targets --features metal,instrument -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p omega --features metal,instrument`: 261 passed, 14 skipped; `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument`: 131 passed, 37 skipped (incl. both new gate tests, every real-checkpoint capability-matrix/metal-backend test still green); `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features std`: 111 passed, 26 skipped. Invariant grep: `gpu_memory_fit: false` remains in exactly one place in `serving.rs` (`fully_supported_config_applies_without_error`'s own independent literal, not a `Default`-mirror test) -- both mirror tests now read `true`.

**Residual, named not hidden.** `LOAD_TIME_FIT_ARENA_ALLOWANCE_BYTES` is a fixed constant (this budget runs before any forward exists to measure a real peak); ROW 396's `plan_query_rows`-scaled `ARENA_TRANSIENT_CAP` is the RUNTIME counterpart that catches what this load-time estimate cannot -- a prefill whose row count blows past the fixed allowance still fails at `build_buffer_arena`'s own gate, one layer deeper than this one. `HostMemoryLimit::available_bytes` never accounts for `currentAllocatedSize` (bytes another already-loaded model has claimed) -- this gate prices a cold load, not a multi-model host; a follow-up serving multiple checkpoints on one device would need to subtract that field, which `SystemMemoryFacts` already carries but `apply_memory_fit_gate` does not yet read.

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- `LOAD_TIME_FIT_OS_HEADROOM_BYTES` (8 GiB) and `LOAD_TIME_FIT_ARENA_ALLOWANCE_BYTES` (28_311_552 bytes), both build-time consts from `omega-runtime.toml`'s new `[load_time_fit]` section, both env-overridable. structural -- new public `ServingConfig::gpu_memory_fit` default (`false` to `true`); new public `InteropError::MemoryBudgetExceeded` variant; no existing signature changed. **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** state machine -- `FitOutcome` is a two-variant enum, no boolean flag; bytes-first -- every quantity is a plain `u64` byte count, no text; borrowed views -- `HostMemoryLimit`/`WeightClassBytes`/`MemoryBudget` are `Copy` payload structs, no allocation on the gate's own hot path (called once per load, not per token); SIMD/branchless -- N/A, load-time arithmetic on a handful of scalars, not a hot numeric loop.

## ROW 401 -- CPU decoders for `IQ4_NL`/`Q5_1`/`IQ2_XS`/`IQ3_XXS`, the four codecs Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's UD-Q2_K_XL GGUF needs that proxima lacked

**Card, Flash-Next census (`project_omega_autotune_and_distribute_direction`, headers only via `proxima-gguf` `pipe::parse_complete`, `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF` UD-Q4_K_XL, 4 shards, 111.32 GB).** `qwen4exp`: 48 layers, 512 experts (10 used, ff 640) + shared expert, 12 NSA-style sparse-attention layers (indexer top_k 2048) interleaved with 36 DeltaNet-style layers (fused `attn_qkv` + `ssm_{a,alpha,beta,conv1d,dt,norm,out}`, state 128, groups 16, inner 6144), hyper-connections, and a PLE ngram table (`per_layer_token_embd` [160 x 320,001,536], `IQ4_NL`, 90 B/row, 28.8 GB) present in **every** quant tier including Q2_K_XL. Q2_K_XL's codec set is `{F32,BF16,Q8_0,Q6_K,Q5_K,Q4_K,IQ2_XS,IQ3_XXS,IQ4_NL}`; resident 50.0 GB fits 64 GB (Q4_K_XL's 82.5 GB does not). `Q5_1` is not in that codec list but is what the file's 36 DeltaNet/SSM tensor groups use directly (`ssm_{a,alpha,beta,conv1d,dt,norm,out}`) regardless of overall quant tier -- so it and `IQ4_NL` are both load-bearing for the target model, and `IQ2_XS`/`IQ3_XXS` are the codecs the Q2_K_XL expert tensors fall back to below `Q4_K`.

**Branch:** `feat/codec-iq4nl-q5-1` (`1edf4a8b`/`b6a8852d`), landed via `land/codec`. First rebase onto main at `3609c7e1` was zero-conflict (main's own ROW 390-393 landings touched `omega/src/msl.rs`/`omega/tests/*`/this file's ROW 393 entry only; this branch's own docs commit for ROW 393 was already identical content and dropped as empty by the rebase). Main advanced six more times while this landing waited on the box gate (`fix/metal-encoder-guard` -> ROW 394, `feat/generate-streaming` -> ROW 395, `fix/arena-cap-scales-with-rows` -> ROW 396, `fix/prefill-scratch-stride` -> ROW 397, `fix/decode-partial-utf8-tail` -> ROW 398, `fix/decode-invalid-run-replacement` -> ROW 399, `feat/load-time-fit-gate` -> ROW 400); the final rebase onto main's tip (`3fc352ca`, ROW 400) applied this branch's code commits (including the `omega/src/metal.rs`/`wgpu_driver.rs` fix commit for the `QuantizedBlock` matches) with zero file overlap against any concurrent landing except this doc file, whose changelog table conflicted, resolved by keeping ROW 396-400 verbatim and renumbering this row from 396 to 401.

**Mechanism, decode shape.** All four are dequant-then-dot: each codec's module (`proxima-gguf/src/quant/{iq4_nl,q5_1,iq2_xs,iq3_xxs}.rs`) exposes a `dequantize` entry point that unpacks its block layout into `f32`, and `proxima-tensor/src/cpu.rs` wires that into the existing `QuantizedBlock` match (row-decode at `cpu.rs:6134-6160`, byte/element-count lookup at `cpu.rs:7399-7402`/`7956-7959`, and a dedicated `matmul_<codec>_f32` dispatch arm at `cpu.rs:8240-8243` alongside `Q4_K`/`Q5_K`/`Q6_K`) -- no new call shape, the four codecs slot into the CPU path the existing codecs already use.

- **`IQ4_NL`** (`iq4_nl.rs`): `Q4_0`-identical byte layout (18 B / 32 elements, one `f16` scale + 16 packed nibble bytes, `ggml-common.h:405-410`) but a non-linear nibble->value lookup instead of `Q4_0`'s fixed `nibble - 8` recenter: `value = scale * KVALUES_IQ4NL[nibble]`, the 16-entry codebook copied verbatim from `ggml-common.h:1077-1079` (`dequantize_row_iq4_nl`, `ggml-quants.c:2428-2444`).
- **`Q5_1`** (`q5_1.rs`): 32-element blocks, `f16` scale `d` + `f16` min `m` + a 5th high bit per element packed separately from the 4 low nibble bits (`block_q5_1`, `ggml-common.h`), `value = d * (qh_bit<<4 | nibble) + m` -- the affine (scale+min) sibling of `Q5_0`'s pure-scale form, needed because the DeltaNet/SSM tensor groups (`ssm_a`/`ssm_alpha`/`ssm_beta`/`ssm_conv1d`/`ssm_dt`/`ssm_norm`/`ssm_out`) in this file are `Q5_1`, independent of the model's overall expert-weight quant tier.
- **`IQ2_XS`** (`iq2_xs.rs`): 256-element super-blocks, 74 B (`block_iq2_xs`, `ggml-common.h:344-351`), 8 sub-blocks of 32 each with a scale nibble pair (`db = d * (0.5 + nibble) * 0.25`, `ggml-quants.c:2230-2231`) and, per 8-element group, a 9-bit index into a 512-entry magnitude grid (`IQ2XS_GRID`, transcribed from `ggml-common.h`'s `iq2xs_grid` table with attribution into `proxima-gguf/src/quant/tables/iq2xs_grid.rs`) plus a 7-bit index into a 128-entry sign table (`KSIGNS_IQ2XS`) that flips each of the group's 8 magnitudes independently.
- **`IQ3_XXS`** (`iq3_xxs.rs`): 256-element super-blocks, same grid+sign shape as `IQ2_XS` at 3.0625 bits/weight instead of 2.3125 (`block_iq3_xxs`, `ggml-common.h`; grid transcribed into `iq3xxs_grid.rs`), one `f16` scale shared across the whole super-block rather than per-sub-block nibbles -- the tables differ in width and entry count from `IQ2_XS`'s, not the addressing scheme.

**GPU-side coverage (this branch's fix commit).** `omega/src/metal.rs` and `omega/src/wgpu_driver.rs`'s `QuantizedBlock` matches were non-exhaustive against the four new variants until this fix: `block_identity_key`/`block_byte_len`/every `execute_plan*` upload arm now list all four alongside the existing packed codecs (byte-slice access only, unconditional), and `packed_operands_of` on both drivers routes them to `None` explicitly (with a comment naming why) rather than falling through a wildcard -- same "no `PackedCodec` unpack-kernel entry yet" rejection `Float32`/`Q3K` already take, so a caller hits `reject_unsupported_gpu_dtype`'s ordinary error instead of an unmatched-pattern compile failure or a silent wrong-shape upload.

**N per gate, this landing.** `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-gguf`: 149 passed, 4 skipped. `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-tensor --features cached-attention-streaming,reduce-epilogue-fusion`: 585 passed, 10 skipped. `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p omega --features metal,instrument`: N passed. `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument`: N passed. `cargo clippy -p proxima-gguf -p proxima-tensor -p omega --all-targets --features metal,instrument -- -D warnings`: clean, EXIT 0. `cargo clippy -p proxima-gguf --no-default-features --features alloc -- -D warnings` (CI alloc tier): clean, EXIT 0 -- the four new modules and their table modules compile under `alloc` with no `std` leak (no new `f16`/table-lookup code depends on ambient platform facilities).

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) No Metal decode bodies for any of the four codecs -- they run CPU-only; a GPU-resident Flash-Next load still needs those kernels or a CPU-side pre-decode-to-resident-codec step, unmeasured and undesigned here. (2) No i-quant *encoders* -- `IQ2_XS`/`IQ3_XXS`/`IQ4_NL` are decode-only because their encode path needs an importance matrix (calibration data), which nothing in this landing computes or consumes; proxima can read these checkpoints, not produce them. (3) No measurement against the actual Flash-Next checkpoint in this landing -- the census's byte/tier numbers above are read from GGUF headers only (`pipe::parse_complete`), not from a load-and-run; the four decoders are exercised here only by their own unit tests' synthetic blocks, not the real 28.8 GB PLE table or a real DeltaNet `Q5_1` tensor.

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- none new (fixed block sizes per `ggml-common.h`, no runtime-tunable knob). structural -- four new `QuantizedBlock` variants (`Iq4Nl`/`Q5_1`/`Iq2Xs`/`Iq3Xxs`), each gated by the codec actually present in a loaded checkpoint, not a cargo feature. **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** state machine N/A (stateless per-block decode); bytes-first YES (`&[u8]` in, `f32` slice out); borrowed views YES (input stays borrowed, no intermediate allocation); zero-copy on the input side YES, output is the caller-owned dequant buffer by construction; SIMD NO (scalar per-element grid/codebook lookup, unmeasured against a SIMD gather); branchless NO (per-sub-block nibble/sign branching); O(1) per token YES (fixed block size, no data-dependent loop bound).

## ROW 402 -- per-tensor weight precision policy at bind, plus a per-expert selection counter on the CPU MoE route

**Owner's direction.** "Not a single parameter, but a parameter per node so we could control which nodes are f32 and which are q1-s" -- the two incumbents that motivate this shape are HOBBIT (arXiv 2411.01433, per-layer mixed-precision quantization chosen by sensitivity) and DynaExq (arXiv 2511.15015, dynamic per-expert precision driven by online activation frequency). This landing builds the two primitives DynaExq's allocation rule would consume -- a bind-time per-name recode and a per-expert selection counter -- without yet writing the allocation rule itself.

**Branch:** `feat/per-tensor-precision-policy` (`52f688d0`, a single WIP commit interrupted mid-session by a box kill), landed via `land/precision`. Split at landing into two logical commits (`feat(interop): per-tensor weight precision policy at bind`, `feat(tensor): per-expert selection counter on the cpu moe route`) since the WIP commit mixed both crates' work. Merge-base `374e358c`; main advanced one row while this branch's session ran (`feat/codec-iq4nl-q5-1` -> ROW 401, `IQ4_NL`/`Q5_1`/`IQ2_XS`/`IQ3_XXS` added to `proxima_tensor::cpu::QuantizedBlock`). Rebase conflicted in exactly one file, `proxima-model-interop/src/error.rs` (main's `MemoryBudgetExceeded` variant landed in the same enum region this branch's `UnsupportedWeightPrecisionTarget` variant occupies) -- resolved by keeping both variants, main's first. No conflict in `bind.rs`'s `PackedOwnedKind`/`quantize_to_kind`/dispatch matches: this branch's own match arms only ever named the eight codecs with a real encoder (`Q8_0`/`Q4_K`/`Q5_K`/`Q6_K`/`Q3_K`/`Q4_0`/`F16`/`BF16`), so main's four new decode-only variants (`Iq4Nl`/`Q5_1`/`Iq2Xs`/`Iq3Xxs`) never needed a new arm there -- an unmatched target routes to the existing wildcard `UnsupportedWeightPrecisionTarget` path rather than a non-exhaustive-match compile failure.

**Mechanism, bind-time recode.** `ServingConfig::weight_precision` (`proxima-model-interop/src/serving.rs`) is an ordered slice of `WeightPrecisionRule { pattern: NamePattern, target: GgmlType }`, first-match-wins against a tensor's on-disk name, exposed both as a struct literal field and via `ServingConfig::with_weight_precision`'s fluent builder (config-as-mirror, principle 4, proven by `weight_precision_config_and_builder_surfaces_agree`). `bind_dense_as`/`bind_matmul_weight_as` route a matched tensor through `recode_tensor` (`bind.rs:1010`) instead of the on-disk-codec path: it dequantizes the source bytes to `f32`, then re-encodes through the existing `proxima_gguf::quant` `ENCODERS` for the rule's `target`, and binds the result under a NEW `BoundWeights` entry named `<target_name>@<codec>` (`recoded@q8_0`, e.g.) -- the original `target_name` entry is left untouched, proven by `sequential_weight_precision_rebinds_produce_distinct_names_and_leave_the_first_entry_untouched`. A `weight_recoded` structured event fires per recode (byte count before/after). Targets with no encoder (`Q2_K`, the `Iq*` family, `Q4_1`/`Q5_1`/`Q8_1`, or any integer/`F64`/`Tq*` type) surface as the typed `InteropError::UnsupportedWeightPrecisionTarget { tensor, target }` rather than silently keeping the on-disk codec, which would make the rule a no-op nobody could see. `bind_all_weights` gained a `weight_precision: &[WeightPrecisionRule]` parameter threaded down to every `bind_dense_as`/`bind_matmul_weight_as` call site; `generate.rs`'s current caller passes `&[]` (byte-identical to the no-rule path, proven by `no_matching_weight_precision_rule_is_byte_identical_to_the_no_rule_path`) -- threading a real rule set through `LoadedModel::load`'s own 22 call sites is not in this landing's scope.

**Mechanism, per-expert selection counter.** `proxima-tensor/src/cpu.rs`'s CPU MoE route gained `record_expert_selection(node, expert)` (a `BTreeMap<(NodeId, u32), ExpertSelectionEntry>` behind a `proxima_lock::Mutex`, count + an EMA of selection recency) called once per routed expert at the MoE evaluator's dispatch site (`cpu.rs:8304`, inside the same loop `matmul_<codec>_f32` already walks per expert). `snapshot_expert_selection_top_n(top_n)` drains the table and returns the top-N by raw count -- these two fields (count, ema) are exactly DynaExq's own inputs for a hotness-ranked allocation decision, not two independent queries. `emit_expert_selection_event` fires an `expert_selection` structured event with the top-8 `(node, expert, count, ema)` tuples, compiled out entirely when the `instrument` feature is off. The event is not wired into the evaluator's own per-step return value -- a caller reaches it only by calling `snapshot_expert_selection_top_n`/`emit_expert_selection_event` directly, not through the forward pass's existing output -- out of scope for this landing.

**Gate fixes, this landing.** (1) `cpu.rs`'s `sort_unstable_by(|l, r| r.2.cmp(&l.2))` in `snapshot_expert_selection_top_n` failed `clippy::unnecessary_sort_by` under `-D warnings`; replaced with `sort_unstable_by_key(|entry| Reverse(entry.2))`, same ordering. (2) Two test struct literals (`generate.rs`'s `model_with` building `BoundWeights`, `serving.rs`'s `exact_activations_agrees_across_literal_and_default_override` building `ServingConfig`) predated this branch's new `precision`/`weight_precision` fields and failed to compile post-rebase; filled with `&[]`, matching every other test literal's convention. (3) `bind.rs`'s own `chunks_exact` call in a new test failed `clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` (stabilized `as_chunks` supersedes it); rewritten as the suggested `as_chunks::<{ q8_0::QK8_0 }>().0.iter()`. (4) `weight_precision_rule_recodes_q4_k_to_q8_0_within_q8_0_error_bound`'s tolerance (`delta / 2`) omitted the block scale's own `f16` storage rounding -- q8_0's scale is `half::f16::from_f32(d)`, whose half-ULP relative error (`2^-11`) is amplified by the largest representable level (127), adding a `127 * delta * 2^-11` term the original bound never accounted for; the corrected bound (`delta * 0.5 + 127 * delta * 2^-11 + f32::EPSILON`) is a real derivation from `q8_0::quantize_block`'s formula, not a loosened tolerance to make a flaky test pass -- confirmed deterministic by re-running the single test standalone before and after the fix.

**N per gate, this landing.** `cargo clippy -p proxima-model-interop --all-targets --features metal,instrument -- -D warnings`: clean, EXIT 0. `cargo clippy -p proxima-tensor --all-targets --features cached-attention-streaming,reduce-epilogue-fusion -- -D warnings`: clean, EXIT 0. `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument`: 137 passed, 37 skipped. `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features std`: 117 passed, 26 skipped. `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-tensor --features cached-attention-streaming,reduce-epilogue-fusion`: 587 passed, 10 skipped.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) `weight_precision` is not threaded through `LoadedModel::load`'s 22 call sites -- a real serving deployment cannot yet set a per-tensor rule end to end, only `bind_all_weights` itself accepts one. (2) The `expert_selection` event/snapshot is not wired into the evaluator's own per-step return -- a caller must poll `snapshot_expert_selection_top_n` out of band, not read it off the forward pass's result. (3) No allocation rule yet -- the counter (count + EMA) and the recode primitive (`<name>@<codec>` rebind) are the two inputs a DynaExq-style rule would consume, but nothing in this landing decides which experts get recoded to what precision from those inputs; that decision, and its own budget/threshold axes, is undesigned here.

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- none new (the EMA's own smoothing constant is a fixed literal in `record_expert_selection`, not yet build-time configurable -- a residual, not a decision). structural -- `NamePattern`/`WeightPrecisionRule`/`GgmlType` target (config, principle 4: struct literal and `with_weight_precision` builder proven to agree); `ExpertSelectionEntry { count, ema }` keyed by `(NodeId, u32)`. **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** state machine N/A (a per-call counter update, not a protocol); bytes-first N/A (recode operates on already-decoded `f32`/on-disk codec bytes, not a wire format); borrowed views YES (`recode_tensor` borrows `file_bytes` for the dequant step, only the re-encoded output is owned); zero-copy NO on the recode path by construction -- recoding is defined as producing new bytes at a new codec, an allocation is the point; SIMD N/A (delegates entirely to `proxima_gguf::quant`'s own encoders); branchless NO (`NamePattern` match per tensor, `BTreeMap` lookup per expert); O(1) per token NO for the counter (`BTreeMap` insert is `O(log n)` in the number of distinct `(node, expert)` pairs, bounded by `expert_count` per node, not token count).

## ROW 403 -- dropping a model releases its device buffers

**Card:** a downstream chat client that loads and drops multiple `LoadedModel`s on one process (swapping checkpoints without restarting) leaked every one of them on Metal: `LoadedModel` carried no `Drop` impl, so a dropped model's resident weight buffers, its whole-mapping no-copy buffer, and its `omega::backend::register_checkpoint_mapping` registration all outlived the struct -- each subsequent load only grew the device's own allocated set, never shrank it.

**Branch:** `fix/model-release-on-drop` (`c15ea84b`), landed via `land/release-2`. Merge-base at ROW 400 (the load-time fit gate). First rebase onto main's `3fc352ca` tip: one real conflict, in `proxima-model-interop/src/generate.rs`'s `LoadedModel` struct: main's ROW 400 landing independently added a `checkpoint_bytes: usize` field (a byte COUNT, with a public `checkpoint_bytes()` accessor for the memory-fit gate) in the exact same struct this branch extends with a `checkpoint_bytes: &'file [u8]` field (the raw mapping VIEW `Drop` hands back to `unregister_checkpoint_mapping`) -- same name, different type, different reader. Kept both: renamed the branch's field to `checkpoint_mapping`, updated its three construction sites (`load_inner`'s two callers via `load`/`load_with_paired_gate_up_reduce`/`load_with_fused_qkv_reduce`, and `load_from_safetensors`, which never registers a mapping but still stores the raw view per that field's own doc) and the `memory_fit_gate_tests::model_with` struct-literal fixture that predates this branch and needed the new field added. `grep -n "checkpoint_bytes\b"` post-resolution matches only main's `usize` field/accessor/constructors; the branch's slice form appears only as `checkpoint_mapping`. Main advanced two more rows while this landing's gates ran (`feat/codec-iq4nl-q5-1` -> ROW 401, `feat/per-tensor-precision-policy` -> ROW 402); a second rebase onto that tip applied both code commits with zero further conflict (neither landing touched `generate.rs`'s `LoadedModel` struct or `omega/src/metal.rs`'s cache-eviction region), conflicting only in this file's own changelog table, resolved by keeping ROW 401-402 verbatim and renumbering this row from 401 to 403.

**Mechanism.** Three cache surfaces in `omega/src/metal.rs`, all thread-local, none of them previously had an eviction path a dropped model could call:

1. `NOCOPY_BUFFERS`/`RESIDENT_BUFFERS` (`BTreeMap<String, ...>`, keyed by weight NAME, never by which model loaded it) -- a second model reusing the same names simply overwrites the first's entries on upload, but a model whose names never recur (a different architecture, or the same model unloaded and never reloaded) left its entries resident forever. New `omega::metal::release_resident_names`/`omega::backend::release_resident_names` evict by name, exactly the set `LoadedModel::resident_names()` (factored out of the three decode-loop call sites that already computed it per step, now shared with `Drop`) reports for THIS checkpoint -- never a blanket clear, so a second model loaded before the first drops keeps its own entries untouched regardless of drop order.
2. `CHECKPOINT_MAPPING` (`RefCell<Option<(usize, usize)>>`, a SINGLE slot, not a map) backs the one whole-mapping no-copy buffer `register_checkpoint_mapping` installs per GGUF load; it already evicts a prior registration the moment a new one lands, but had no unregister at all. New `omega::metal::unregister_checkpoint_mapping`/`omega::backend::unregister_checkpoint_mapping` clear it, but ONLY when the caller's `(pointer, length)` identity still matches what's currently registered -- the exact guard `checkpoint_mapping_release_tests::unregister_only_clears_the_currently_registered_identity` proves: model A loads, model B loads (superseding A's slot per existing behavior), THEN A's `Drop` runs and calls `unregister_checkpoint_mapping(a_bytes)` -- a no-op, since the slot no longer holds A's identity, so B's live mapping survives.
3. `PIPELINE_CACHE` (keyed by compiled-kernel fingerprint, not by checkpoint) is correctly untouched by any of this -- a compiled kernel is reusable across checkpoints of the same shape, and `Drop` never touches it.

`impl Drop for LoadedModel<'_>` (`#[cfg(feature = "metal")]`, a no-op on the CPU-only build since there is no device buffer to release) calls `release_resident_names` then `unregister_checkpoint_mapping` in that order, every drop.

**Real facts, this box** (`generate::tests::release_on_drop_real_model::dropping_a_loaded_model_releases_its_device_buffers`, a real 2.4 GB Q4_K GGUF checkpoint mmap'd from `~/.ollama`, 4 real decode steps on Metal, `--release`): `current_allocated_size` 393_216 bytes (0.38 MB) before load -> 2_497_937_408 bytes (2.33 GB) after generate -> 655_360 bytes (0.64 MB) after drop -- device allocation returns to within 256 KB of the pre-load baseline. `phys_footprint_bytes` 4_883_584 (4.7 MB) -> 45_336_640 (43.2 MB) -> 20_137_984 (19.2 MB) -- drops by more than half but does not return to baseline, exactly as that test's own doc predicts: the OS-level footprint also reflects allocator arenas and thread stacks this drop path does not and should not touch, so this number is read as "collapsed", not "byte-identical to before load".

**Proof.** 3 new `omega` unit tests (`metal,instrument`, real Metal device): `checkpoint_mapping_release_tests::unregister_only_clears_the_currently_registered_identity` (the drop-ordering hazard above), `release_resident_names_evicts_only_the_named_resident_copy`, `release_resident_names_evicts_only_the_named_entry` (both prove eviction is by-name, never a blanket cache clear). `proxima-model-interop::generate::tests::release_on_drop_real_model` (1 new test, `#[ignore]`d host-local real-checkpoint fixture, run explicitly this landing): `dropping_a_loaded_model_releases_its_device_buffers` -- 1 passed, 0 failed, prints the three before/after/drop pairs above.

**Gates:** `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features metal,instrument,reduce-epilogue-fusion -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features wgpu-backend,cuda -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo clippy -p proxima-model-interop --all-targets --features metal,instrument -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p omega --features metal,instrument`: 264 passed, 14 skipped (261 + the 3 new: `unregister_only_clears_the_currently_registered_identity`, `release_resident_names_evicts_only_the_named_resident_copy`, `release_resident_names_evicts_only_the_named_entry`); `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument`: 131 passed, 38 skipped; `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features std`: 111 passed, 26 skipped; `cargo test -p omega --doc --features metal,instrument`: 1 passed, 0 failed (see the doctest fix below -- this run was RED before it, 0 passed/1 failed). Invariant grep: `Drop::drop` reads `self.checkpoint_mapping` (the renamed `&'file [u8]` view), never `self.checkpoint_bytes` (main's unrelated `usize` byte count, read only by its own `checkpoint_bytes()` accessor) -- the two fields coexist on the struct with no call site confusing one for the other.

**Also landed, its own commit:** `fix(omega): import numeric policy in the q3k unpack doc example` -- a pre-existing doctest failure this landing's own `cargo test -p omega --doc` gate surfaced (not introduced by this branch, but this landing's gate is what caught it, so it lands here rather than being punted): `omega/src/msl.rs`'s `emit` doctest used the bare `NumericPolicy::default()` at its second call site while its first call site three lines earlier fully-qualified the same type as `proxima_tensor::NumericPolicy::default()` -- no `use` import brought the bare name into the doctest's own scope. Fixed by qualifying the second call site to match the first. Doctest count: 0 passed/1 failed before, 1 passed/0 failed after.

**Residual, named not hidden.** `HostMemoryLimit::available_bytes` (ROW 400) still never subtracts `currentAllocatedSize` when sizing a NEW load's budget -- this landing makes that number shrink back down correctly on drop, but a fit-gate check racing between two live models on one device still prices against a stale, too-generous ceiling; unifying the two remains open. `phys_footprint_bytes` staying elevated after drop is read, not chased -- see the real-facts paragraph above for why chasing it further would be measuring the allocator, not this landing's own device-buffer contract.

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- none (no new tunable; both `Drop` calls are unconditional, no allowance to size). structural -- new public `omega::metal::release_resident_names`/`omega::metal::unregister_checkpoint_mapping` (and their `omega::backend` re-exports); new `LoadedModel` private field `checkpoint_mapping`; new `impl Drop for LoadedModel<'_>`; no existing public signature changed. **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** state machine -- N/A, a lifecycle hook, not a protocol state machine; bytes-first -- `release_resident_names` takes `&str` names and `unregister_checkpoint_mapping` takes `&[u8]`, no owned copies; borrowed views -- `checkpoint_mapping` borrows `'file` exactly like every other field on this struct, never re-allocates the checkpoint bytes; SIMD/branchless -- N/A, called once per drop, not a hot loop.

## ROW 404 -- two-range plan key buckets cached length with a runtime bound, closing ROW 392's per-token plan miss and buffer churn

**Card.** ROW 392 measured Qwen3.8-27B's two-range decode path re-uploading, reading back, and re-planning ~155 MB/7 GB per token because the `Plan` cache keys on `cached_len`, which strictly increases every step and so can never repeat. Branch `perf/two-range-plan-reuse` (`6605ca16`) fixed the KEYING: `omega::backend::plan_named` rounds `cached_len` up to a `kv_extent` bucket boundary (`ServingConfig::kv_bucket_tokens`) before resolving the symbol, so every step inside one bucket reuses the same compiled `Plan` instead of rebuilding it. That commit's own bucket-padding mechanism was a `cached_range_padding_mask` `Select` node inserted into the graph (`proxima-tensor/src/spec.rs`), masking the padded rows past the real `cached_len` with `-infinity` before softmax -- but that mask node changed `cached_attention_candidates`' fusion-detector shape (an extra `Select` between the score and the softmax fold breaks the exact op sequence the detector pattern-matches), so `cached_attention_candidates` stopped firing on a bucketed program and `fused_cached_attention_root_agrees_between_cpu_and_metal` failed on that commit -- the plan-cache fix and the fused kernel were mutually exclusive.

**Branch `perf/two-range-cached-bound` (WIP `06cfc7f0`, interrupted by a box kill, judged structurally complete but never built).** Replaces the mask node with a CACHED-SIDE runtime bound read by the kernel itself: `cached_range_padding_mask` and its call sites are deleted from `spec.rs`; `mistral_cached_forward_program_with_experts` instead adds an unconditional rank-0 `"cached_len"` `Op::Input` leaf that feeds no arithmetic in the graph. `proxima_tensor::bind::cached_attention_candidates` finds that leaf by NAME (`find_named_input`, new) and appends it as the fused `BoundOpKind::CachedAttention`'s ninth operand -- reusing the SAME operand slot the single-range fusion already used for its own runtime `cached_len`, discriminated by `cached_key_rows`: `== 0` is the single-range shape (the ninth operand is the real `new_upper_inclusive`); `!= 0` is the two-range shape (the ninth operand is the CACHED range's own live row count, substituting for the compiled, bucket-padded `cached_key_rows` wherever the kernel addresses or bounds the cached range). `omega::msl::render_cached_attention`'s `two_range_cached_bound` branch reads it as `long cached_key_rows = (long)in8[0];`, shadowing every existing use of that name in the kernel body (the `bool cached = key < cached_key_rows` split, `new_index`'s offset, `last_key`'s sum) -- one declaration site, not a new gate at each use.

**Plumbing this landing finished across every renderer the WIP's own diff did not reach.** The WIP touched `msl.rs`/`bind.rs`/`spec.rs` only; the discriminator it introduced (`cached_key_rows == 0` vs `!= 0` on a 9-operand op) needed the identical split in four more places, each a real correctness gap if left as `operands.len() == 9` alone:
- `omega/src/metal.rs`: `pack_cached_attention_uniforms`/`pack_uniforms_byte_len` were still keying the EXTENDED (5-word) vs minimal (1-word) `Uniforms` struct on operand count alone -- a two-range-cached-bound op has 9 operands too, so it would have packed/sized the wrong uniform blob against the kernel text's own minimal struct.
- `omega/src/identity.rs`: `kernel_identity`'s `upper_token` collapsed to `"dyn"` for any 9-operand op, which is only correct for the single-range shape (the ninth operand there really is the causal bound); for two-range-cached-bound the REAL `new_upper_inclusive` is a compiled constant, and collapsing it would let two ops with different real bounds share one compiled pipeline with the wrong bound baked in. Added a `_cb` cache-key token so the two 9-operand shapes (and the plain 8-operand shape, which renders the identical `c{}_n{}` token set with a different, `constexpr`-only body) never collide.
- `omega/src/msl.rs`: `entry_name`, `grid_threads`, and the `CachedAttention` cooperative-width arm all had their own copies of the same operand-count-only check (widening the dispatch to the compiled cap, per-query-head grid, block-width staging) -- each is single-range-only machinery and now gates on `cached_key_rows == 0` explicitly. Four bare `dynamic_cached_len` references inside `render_cached_attention` itself were left referring to a variable the WIP's diff had renamed/split, an undefined-identifier compile error; retargeted to `single_range_dynamic`.
- `proxima-tensor/src/cpu.rs`: `run_cached_attention` (the CPU oracle) unconditionally read the ninth operand as `new_upper_inclusive`, so a two-range-cached-bound op's real cached-row count was misread as a causal bound and rejected (`NotLowerable: runtime cached_len operand exceeds its buffer extent`) the moment `cached_key_rows != 0`. Fixed to read the operand as a live CACHED row count on that path, slicing the cached K/V/value buffers to the live prefix (`[0, live_cached_key_rows)`, the real data; `[live_cached_key_rows, compiled cached_key_rows)` is the bucket's own zero-padded tail) before handing them to `stream_cached_attention_split_gqa`, so its exact-length shape check sees a consistent (sliced buffer, live extent) pair instead of the full padded buffer against a truncated extent.
- `proxima-tensor/src/bind.rs`: `cached_attention_candidates` was appending the ninth operand whenever the `"cached_len"` leaf existed, with NO guard on the compiled `cached_key_rows` itself -- at the very first decode step (no tokens cached yet) a two-range op's compiled `cached_key_rows` is genuinely `0`, colliding with the single-range discriminator at the type level (both structurally 9-operand, `cached_key_rows == 0`). Gated the push on `cached_key_shape[0] > 0`: an empty cached range has no padding to exclude and stays 8-operand, matching pre-fix behavior exactly for that one step.
- Test fixtures: `omega/src/msl.rs`'s `cached_attention_op_dynamic` (used by ~11 single-range-dynamic tests) constructed fixtures with a nonzero `cached_key_rows` under the PRE-fix assumption that 9 operands alone meant single-range; folded both constructor arguments into `new_key_rows` (`cached_key_rows: 0` always) so the fixture matches the real single-range invariant while preserving every test's own context-length total. `omega/tests/support/mod.rs`'s shared `real_forward_fixture_with_cached_len` fed the new `"cached_len"` leaf a RANDOM value (the generic unnamed-input fallback, written before the WIP added that leaf) instead of the real length -- silently correct on CPU (which never reads it) and silently wrong on the fused Metal path, exactly the divergence the gate below caught. `proxima-tensor/src/spec.rs`'s `a_cached_decode_step_matches_the_uncached_forward_pass_exactly`/`a_single_range_decode_step_matches_the_two_range_decode_step`/`_with_qk_norm` never bound `"cached_len"` at all (`UnboundInputName`), predating the leaf.

**Gate.** `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features metal,instrument,reduce-epilogue-fusion -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo clippy -p omega --all-targets --features wgpu-backend,cuda -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo clippy -p proxima-model-interop --all-targets --features metal,instrument -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo clippy -p proxima-tensor --all-targets --features cached-attention-streaming,reduce-epilogue-fusion -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p omega --features metal,instrument`: 261 passed, 14 skipped, including `fused_cached_attention_root_agrees_between_cpu_and_metal` (the exact regression ROW 392's mask node introduced). `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument`: 138 passed, 37 skipped, including `two_range_plan_cache_buckets_cached_len_without_changing_generated_tokens`. `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features std`: 117 passed, 26 skipped. `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-tensor --features cached-attention-streaming,reduce-epilogue-fusion`: 587 passed, 10 skipped.

**Measured, `two_range_plan_cache_buckets_cached_len_without_changing_generated_tokens` (a synthetic one-layer MoE fixture, 8-token greedy decode, no real device attached, `OUTPUT_BUFFER_ALLOCATIONS` counter).** `kv_bucket_tokens=1` (unbucketed, ROW 392's pre-fix shape): `plan_misses=8 plan_hits=0`, one fresh miss every step, exactly the shape ROW 392 measured. `kv_bucket_tokens=32` (bucketed): `plan_misses=2 plan_hits=6` -- the SAME 8-step run now misses only when a step crosses a bucket boundary, hitting the cached `Plan` the other 6 steps. `output_buffer_allocations` measured `0` on both arms in this sandbox (no real Metal device, the Gpu-arm allocation counter never fires here at all) -- non-strict signal only, the `plan_hits`/`plan_misses` split is this test's load-bearing, environment-independent proof. Both arms produced IDENTICAL generated token ids (`bucketed.0 == unbucketed.0`), the numerics claim the whole redesign depends on: a bucket's own zero-padded tail rows must be invisible to softmax regardless of which mechanism (mask node or runtime bound) excludes them.

**Invariant grep.** `grep -rn "cached_range_padding_mask" --include="*.rs" .` across the workspace: zero hits after this landing (six stale doc references in `proxima-model-interop/src/generate.rs`, pointing at the deleted function, updated to name the runtime-bound mechanism instead). `two_range_cached_bound` appears in `proxima-tensor/src/cpu.rs`, `omega/src/identity.rs`, `omega/src/msl.rs`, `omega/src/metal.rs` -- one discriminator, four renderers. `KvPadScratch` (the two-range decode loop's bucket-padded KV mirror, unrelated to the mask removal) is untouched, still the production plumbing that pads a copy of the growing KV cache to the bucket boundary before upload.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) The qwen3.5 hybrid architecture's OWN dense-attention layer (`append_qwen35_dense_attention_layer`, `proxima-tensor/src/spec.rs:3301`) is "the same cached-attention/online-softmax shape" as `append_mistral_cached_layer` per its own doc, but is a structurally separate function, and `qwen35_forward_program` (`spec.rs:7707`) never adds a `"cached_len"` `Op::Input` leaf at all. This landing's fix reaches `mistral_cached_forward_program_with_experts` only -- the qwen35 hybrid's dense-attention layers still rebuild a fresh `Plan` every decode step exactly as ROW 392 measured; bucketing them needs the same leaf added to `qwen35_forward_program` plus a `cached_len`-aware operand push in whatever bind-time pattern matches `append_qwen35_dense_attention_layer`'s fused op (unverified whether `cached_attention_candidates` already pattern-matches it or whether it needs its own detector). (2) The kv-capacity-bucket naming test (`dynamic_cached_attention_kernel_identity_is_stable_across_kv_capacity_buckets`) and its sibling fixtures were repointed at `new_key_rows` for their own fixture-sanity assertions; this is a test-only change with no production code path affected, since `cached_attention_op_dynamic` is `omega`-internal test scaffolding never called by `bind.rs`. (3) The 30-minute cargo-mutex wait at task start (another builder held the lock ~5 minutes before this session's gates began) is host contention, not part of this landing's own work.

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- none new (no build-time tunable added; `ATTENTION_CONTEXT_CHUNK_CAP`/`ATTENTION_SPLIT_MAX` are ROW 369/385's existing constants, only their GATING condition changed). structural -- `BoundOpKind::CachedAttention`'s ninth operand now carries two discriminated runtime scalars sharing one slot (`cached_key_rows == 0` / `!= 0`), documented at the variant itself. **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** state machine N/A (a kernel-body/bind-time discriminator, not a protocol); bytes-first N/A; borrowed views YES (`run_cached_attention`'s live-prefix slicing borrows the same buffer, no copy); zero-copy YES (the runtime bound is a single scalar read, `in8[0]`/`buffer_of(...).first()`, never a re-materialized tensor); SIMD N/A (no new kernel body shape, only which compiled constant a runtime read replaces); branchless PARTIAL (`bool cached = key < cached_key_rows` is a per-key runtime compare either way, unchanged by this landing); O(1) per token YES for the plan-cache hit path this closes (a bucketed step reuses the compiled `Plan`, `pipeline_for`, and `Uniforms` layout without a fresh `emit`/compile).

## ROW 405 -- qwen35 dense attention joins the two-range plan key bucketing ROW 404 left as residual

**Card.** ROW 404's own residual (1) named the exact gap: `append_qwen35_dense_attention_layer` (`proxima-tensor/src/spec.rs:3301`) and `qwen35_forward_program` (`spec.rs:7707`) never add the `"cached_len"` `Op::Input` leaf `mistral_cached_forward_program_with_experts` adds, so `bind::cached_attention_candidates`'s `find_named_input` lookup never finds one on the qwen35 hybrid checkpoint's dense-attention layers -- the fused `CachedAttention` op never gets its ninth runtime operand there, and (separately, in `proxima-model-interop/src/generate.rs`) the two-range decode loop's `DenseAttention` cache arm was never padded to the bucketed `kv_bound_extent` the way the `Attention` arm's `KvPadScratch` already is, even though both share the identical `Extent::Symbolic(1)` slot in the compiled program. Qwen3.8-27B's actual target path (dense-attention layers are the ONLY attention layers on that checkpoint, per `full_attention_interval`) still rebuilt a fresh `Plan` every decode step, exactly as ROW 392 measured, despite ROW 404 landing.

**Fix, tensor side.** `qwen35_forward_program` adds the same rank-0 `"cached_len"` `Op::Input` leaf `mistral_cached_forward_program_with_experts` adds, in the same place (right after its own `causal_mask` call), reusing `input_leaf` -- no second mechanism. `bind::cached_attention_candidates`'s `find_named_input` walks the WHOLE program by name, not by a threaded `NodeId`, so this one leaf covers every `DenseAttention` layer in the program; `append_qwen35_dense_attention_layer`'s own (already long) parameter list needed no change.

**Fix, interop side.** `Qwen35DenseAttentionCache::named_blocks` returned the cache's RAW, unpadded length (`cached_len`-sized) while the graph's `k_first_cache`/`k_second_cache`/`k_pass_cache`/`v_cache` leaves declare `Extent::Symbolic(1)` -- the SAME symbol `symbols[1]` binds to the bucketed `kv_bound_extent` for the `Attention` arm. Unpadded, a bucketed step would hand the backend a buffer shorter than the declared extent. Added `Qwen35DenseAttentionPadScratch`/`Qwen35DenseAttentionPadShape`, `KvPadScratch`/`KvPadShape`'s own structure for the `DenseAttention` row widths (`k_first`/`k_second` share `pairs`, matching `KvPadShape::even_odd_len`; `k_pass`/`v` are `attn_head_dim`-based, needing their own `pass_len`/`v_len`), and wired it into the two-range decode loop's fill/named-blocks passes the same way `KvPadScratch` already is. `attn_head_dim` was not previously threaded onto `LoadedModel` (`ModelArchitecture::head_dim` is the PARTIAL-rotary width, not this checkpoint's real per-head width, `Qwen35Architecture::attn_head_dim`'s own doc) -- added `qwen35_attn_head_dim: Option<u32>`, `Some` only on the qwen35 load path, mirroring the existing `qwen35_ssm_shape` field's own precedent for carrying architecture-specific sizing rather than re-deriving it from `layer_roots` every step. `Qwen35LayerRoots::Ssm`'s own cache (`conv_history`/`state`) needs no change: both leaves are `Extent::Static(...)` in `qwen35_forward_program` (`ssm_d_conv - 1`, `ssm_d_state`-sized), never `Extent::Symbolic(1)`, so bucketing `cached_len` never touches them.

**Test.** The card's own fallback: a fake-fixture qwen35 GGUF (one dense-attention-only layer, `full_attention_interval: 1`, `query_heads = kv_heads = 1`, `attention.key_length = 4`, `rope.dimension_count = 2` so `pass_dim = 2` is exercised alongside the rotated halves), not the `feat/synthetic-qwen38-fixture` branch's real 4-layer hybrid checkpoint (~918 MiB, out of this slice's time budget). `qwen35_dense_attention_two_range_plan_cache_buckets_cached_len` drives the SAME 8-step greedy decode twice (`kv_bucket_tokens: 1` vs `32`) `two_range_plan_cache_buckets_cached_len_without_changing_generated_tokens` already does for the MoE/`Attention` fixture, asserting `plan_hits`/`plan_misses` only (per the card's own fake-fixture allowance) plus generated-token-id equality between the two runs (the numerics claim: a bucket's zero-padded tail must be invisible to softmax on the `DenseAttention` arm exactly as it already is on `Attention`).

**Gate.** `cargo clippy -p proxima-tensor --all-targets --features cached-attention-streaming,reduce-epilogue-fusion -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo clippy -p proxima-model-interop --all-targets --features metal,instrument -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-tensor --features cached-attention-streaming,reduce-epilogue-fusion`: 587 passed, 10 skipped. `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument`: 139 passed, 38 skipped (the new test included). `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features std`: 117 passed, 26 skipped.

**Measured, `qwen35_dense_attention_two_range_plan_cache_buckets_cached_len` (synthetic one-layer dense-attention-only fixture, 8-token greedy decode, no real device attached).** `kv_bucket_tokens=1` (unbucketed): `plan_misses=8 plan_hits=0`. `kv_bucket_tokens=32` (bucketed): `plan_hits>0`, `plan_misses` strictly below the unbucketed baseline -- the same shape ROW 404 measured on the MoE/`Attention` fixture, now reproduced on the `DenseAttention` arm. Both runs produced identical generated token ids.

**Residual, named not hidden.** (1) This lands the fake-fixture fallback, not the branch `feat/synthetic-qwen38-fixture`'s real hybrid checkpoint -- no `OUTPUT_BUFFER_ALLOCATIONS == 0` warm-up assertion and no CPU-vs-Metal top-1 token agreement check, since those need the real hybrid checkpoint's own numerics (SSM mixer layers included) to be meaningful; this test's fixture is `full_attention_interval: 1` (dense-attention-only, no SSM layer at all). (2) `qwen35_attn_head_dim` duplicates information already implicit in `layer_roots`' own `DenseAttention` cache row widths after the first append -- carried as an explicit field (matching `qwen35_ssm_shape`'s own precedent) rather than derived from cache state, so it is available before any token is cached (`cached_len == 0`) too.

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- none new. structural -- `LoadedModel::qwen35_attn_head_dim: Option<u32>` is the same "architecture-specific sizing carried at load time" shape `qwen35_ssm_shape` already established; no new discriminated variant. **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** state machine N/A (bind-time leaf + host-side padding, not a protocol); bytes-first N/A; borrowed views YES (`Qwen35DenseAttentionPadScratch::named_blocks` slices its own scratch buffer, no copy at the binding boundary); zero-copy PARTIAL (`fill` still `copy_from_slice`s the growing cache into the padded scratch every step, the same cost `KvPadScratch::fill` already pays); SIMD N/A; branchless N/A; O(1) per token YES for the plan-cache hit path this closes on the `DenseAttention` arm, the same win ROW 404 already banked for `Attention`.

## ROW 406-mask -- qwen35 dense attention masks the bucket padding ROW 405 bound but never excluded from softmax

**Card.** ROW 405 threaded `"cached_len"` into `qwen35_forward_program` and padded `Qwen35DenseAttentionCache`'s bound buffers to the bucketed `kv_bound_extent` so the `DenseAttention` arm could join the two-range plan-cache bucketing win -- but `append_qwen35_dense_attention_layer` itself scored EVERY row of the bound `k_first`/`k_second`/`k_pass`/`v` cache buffers, including the zero-padded rows `Qwen35DenseAttentionPadScratch::fill` appends past the real `cached_len` to reach the bucketed extent. Unlike the `Attention` arm, which excludes that same padding via the fused `BoundOpKind::CachedAttention` op's own `cached_key_rows` runtime bound (ROW 404), the `DenseAttention` graph has no such fusion -- ROW 405 threaded the leaf in for bind-time bucketing but never consumed it inside the layer's own score computation, so a bucketed `DenseAttention` step's softmax saw the padding directly.

**Fix.** `append_qwen35_dense_attention_layer` takes a new `cached_len: NodeId` parameter and masks `score_cached_scaled` to `-infinity` past it, the same way `causal_mask_merged` masks its own merged range: an `Op::Iota` over the cached key index, compared `>` against `cached_len - 1` (the exclusive bound), selects `-infinity` for any padded row before either softmax pass sees it. `qwen35_forward_program`'s own `"cached_len"` leaf (already added by ROW 405 for `find_named_input`'s benefit on the `Attention` arm's fusion) is now ALSO threaded directly into every `append_qwen35_dense_attention_layer` call, since this arm has no fusion detector to find it by name instead.

**Proof.** New `proxima-model-interop` test `qwen35_dense_attention_padding_is_invisible_to_softmax`: the ROW 405 synthetic one-layer `DenseAttention`-only fixture, driven with `LoadedModel::run_decode_loop_observed`'s own `LogitsSink::Collect` hook (not the argmax-only token-id comparison ROW 405's own test used, which cannot distinguish two logit vectors sharing an argmax on this fixture's tiny uniform weights) across the SAME 8-step greedy decode at `kv_bucket_tokens: 1` (no padding, `div_ceil` identity) vs `kv_bucket_tokens: 32` (padded). Measured last-step last-row logits `max_abs_diff` **4.38e-6 pre-fix -> exactly 0.0 post-fix** -- the padding is now provably invisible to softmax at raw-logit precision, not merely at the emitted-token level.

**Gate.** `cargo clippy -j 2 -p proxima-tensor -p proxima-model-interop --all-targets --features metal,instrument -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-tensor --features cached-attention-streaming,reduce-epilogue-fusion`: 587 passed, 10 skipped. `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument`: 140 passed, 38 skipped (the new test included). `cargo nextest run -j 1 -p proxima-model-interop --features std`: 117 passed, 26 skipped. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`: clean.

**Residual, named not hidden -- OPEN, tracked on `feat/prefix-state`.** The `Attention` arm's own `append_mistral_cached_layer` has the identical unmasked structure (every row of the bound cache buffers is scored, padding included) and relies entirely on the fused `BoundOpKind::CachedAttention` op's own runtime bound to exclude it. That fusion reports `cached_attention_ops=0` on qwen3-1.7B GQA -- meaning the fusion detector is not firing on at least that shape, so whether `append_mistral_cached_layer`'s own bucket padding is actually excluded on every real checkpoint, or only on the ones where the fusion happens to fire, is unverified. This landing fixes the `DenseAttention` arm, which has no fusion to fall back on; the `Attention` arm's exposure (if the fusion silently fails to fire) is not this landing's fix and remains open on `feat/prefix-state`.

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- none new. structural -- `append_qwen35_dense_attention_layer` gains one `NodeId` parameter (`cached_len`); no public signature changed, the function is `proxima-tensor`-internal. **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** state machine N/A (a graph-construction helper, not a protocol); bytes-first N/A; borrowed views N/A (graph node references, not buffers); zero-copy YES (the mask is a `Select` over an `Iota`, no cache buffer re-materialized); SIMD N/A (graph-level op, lowered by the existing kernel emitter); branchless YES (`Select`, not a runtime branch); O(1) per token YES, unchanged from ROW 405 -- the mask adds graph nodes, not per-step host work.

## ROW 407 -- synthetic Qwen3.8-27B-shaped GGUF fixture: the hybrid `qwen35` path's own graph compiles and binds against random weights of the real shape/quant mix; CPU decode's actual behavior is UNMEASURED (a diagnostic-tool misuse produced a false "Backend NotImplemented", not a real finding) and Metal decode did not complete inside this row's time budget

**Card:** no card filed (single-session audit-and-fixture task, not a planned campaign slice). **Worktree/branch:** `proxima-wt-synth`, `feat/synthetic-qwen38-fixture`, off `main` at `d32e42a1` (ROW 390's own commit). Per owner directive mid-task, this row's fixture is scoped down from an original "extrapolate to 27B" ask to "prove the hybrid path only" -- a real Qwen3 1.7B/4B/8B size ladder (a separate slice) is the intended source for the 27B extrapolation; this row supplies the per-layer-type numbers that ladder cannot (no real checkpoint anywhere on this box has an SSM/hybrid-attention layer at all, `/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/qwen38-path.md`'s own leading finding).

**Why synthetic.** No Qwen3.8-27B GGUF exists on this box; the closest on-disk file (`qwen3.6:35b-a3b`) declares `general.architecture = "qwen35moe"` (MoE + vision, heterogeneous `head_count_kv`), which `bind.rs`'s own typed guard rejects before it ever reaches `crate::qwen35`. Memory-by-class and the lowering census do not depend on weight VALUES, only on tensor byte layout and the op graph `qwen35_forward_program` builds from hparams -- so random weights of the documented shape are sufficient evidence for both, and insufficient evidence for anything about generated-text quality (never claimed).

**The fixture.** `proxima-model-interop/examples/synth_qwen35_gguf.rs`, built on `proxima_gguf::writer::write_complete` (an existing, already-shipping sans-IO GGUF writer -- `grep GgufWriter\|write_gguf\|fn write proxima-gguf/src` found it at `writer.rs:65`; no new writer needed). 4 layers (owner-directed reduction from the documented 64, after the real checkpoint froze the box once under memory pressure), `full_attention_interval = 4` applied honestly (not distorted to force an even split): 1 Attention layer (index 3) + 3 Ssm layers (indices 0-2). Every tensor shape is transcribed from `proxima_tensor::spec::qwen35_forward_program`'s own `input_leaf` calls (`spec.rs:7808-8087`), not re-derived independently. Hparams: `embedding=5120, query_heads=24` DOCUMENTED (`qwen35.rs:136-137`'s own worked example, `5120/24=213.33`, proves both are real); `attn_head_dim=512`, `rope.dimension_count=64` DOCUMENTED (`qwen35.rs:33-48,136`); `kv_heads=2` and every `ssm.*` hparam (`conv_kernel=4, state_size=128, group_count=16, time_step_rank=32, inner_size=4096`) ASSUMED, taken verbatim as magnitude stand-ins from the real on-disk `qwen3.6:35b-a3b` file's own metadata (no true 27B file's own values are observable); `feed_forward=20480` and `vocab=128` ASSUMED/shrunk (ffn width and vocab size do not change which Metal dispatch branch a packed matvec/attention/scan op reaches). Quant mix: Q4_K for every big matmul weight, Q6_K for the tied-embedding/head, F32 for norms and small `ssm_*` vectors -- the production mix asked for. Output: 963,093,280 bytes (918.48 MiB), 55 tensors, written to `/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/synth-qwen38-27b.gguf` and round-tripped through `parse_complete` before being trusted.

**Landable as a real test.** `proxima-model-interop/tests/qwen35_synth_hybrid.rs` reuses the generator via `#[path]` (no duplicated GGUF-building logic) and drives the same fixture through `LoadedModel::load` + `generate_with_serving_config`, `#[ignore]`d (a debug CPU decode over `embedding=5120, feed_forward=20480` did not finish in 6 minutes -- release is required, the same convention `real_lfm2_checkpoint.rs`/`real_smollm2_checkpoint.rs` use for their own multi-GB fixtures). 2 tests registered (`_decodes_on_cpu`, `_decodes_on_metal` gated `cfg(metal)`); both compile clean under `--features metal,instrument` and `--features std`.

**The device-budget guard, run before any load (owner directive, binding after the box froze once on the real 27B file).** `derived_device_budget_bytes`: weights (measured file size) + KV cache (attention-kind layers, `2 x capacity x kv_heads x attn_head_dim x 4B`, `capacity=256`) + SSM state (Ssm-kind layers, O(1) in sequence length) + a 256 MiB fixed arena allowance. Measured at this fixture's own hparams: `weights=963,093,280 kv_cache=2,097,152 ssm_state=6,586,368 arena_allowance=268,435,456 total=1,240,212,256` (1.155 GiB), asserted `<= 16 GiB` before `LoadedModel::load` is ever called. Passed; no abort triggered.

**Real, typed `ServingConfig` rejections hit and fixed (not qwen35-specific -- every checkpoint's cached decode hits these the same way).** `ServingConfig::default()` (the owner's real llama-server invocation) fails three of its own knobs against this forward, in order: `kv_cache_key_quant/value_quant = Q8_0` (`UnsupportedServingConfig`: the cached K/V reduces are batched over a shared kv-head axis, a shape `proxima_tensor::cpu::run_reduce_quantized`'s blocking check refuses for Q8_0, `cpu.rs:2485`); `flash_attention = true` (no fused flash-attention `Op` variant exists, only the naive multiply-then-reduce graph); `batch_size/ubatch_size = 32/32` (the interpreter evaluates the whole prompt extent as one static dimension, no batching loop). The fully-supported field set is `crate::generate::supported_serving_config`'s own (`pub(crate)`, unreachable from an example/test; mirrored by hand field-for-field, `generate.rs:1497-1513`): `F32` KV storage, `flash_attention=false`, `batch_size=ubatch_size=0`, `reasoning_budget=0`.

**Residual, named not hidden -- this row's actual decode outcome is NOT a clean measurement.** (1) A debug CPU decode ran 6+ minutes without finishing (killed). (2) A release CPU decode, run with `PROXIMA_METAL_OP_PROFILE_STEP=7` set, printed `cpu: forward failed: Backend(NotImplemented { backend: "cpu" })` after ~5 minutes -- traced to `omega/src/backend.rs:748`: `PROXIMA_METAL_OP_PROFILE_STEP`'s diagnostic branch (`generate.rs:2581`) calls `evaluate_op_timed` -> `execute_plan_named_metal_op_timed` (`backend.rs:741-751`) for WHICHEVER backend the current run selected, and that function explicitly returns `NotImplemented{backend:"cpu"}` for any `Plan::Cpu` by design (it is a Metal-only per-op-timing diagnostic). Setting that env var for a CPU (`gpu_layers: 0`) run was this row's own mistake, not a finding about the qwen35 CPU path -- the real CPU behavior of this forward over this fixture is UNMEASURED. (3) The subsequent Metal attempt (same process, same env var) produced no output at all for 5+ minutes (0% CPU, thread state `S`) before this row's time budget forced a kill; whether that is a genuine hang, a slow one-time Metal pipeline-compile pass over ~40 distinct op shapes, or something else is UNMEASURED -- `sample`'s own call-graph dump did not resolve past `main` in the time available. Per-kind dispatch counts, `plan_misses`/`output_buffer_allocations`/`readback_bytes`/`device_allocated` at steps 1/4/8, and the CPU-vs-Metal top-1 agreement number the brief asked for are consequently NOT reported this row -- re-running `synth_qwen35_decode --release` with `PROXIMA_METAL_OP_PROFILE_STEP` unset for the CPU arm and set only for the Metal arm (both binaries already built, `target/release/examples/synth_qwen35_decode`) is the direct next step, not a redesign.

**Gates.** `cargo clippy -p proxima-model-interop --all-targets --features metal,instrument -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo clippy -p proxima-model-interop --all-targets --features std -- -D warnings`: clean (after moving the metal-only `GPU_LAYERS_ALL` import behind its own `cfg`). `cargo nextest run -j 2 -p proxima-model-interop --features metal,instrument -E 'binary(qwen35_synth_hybrid)'`: 0 run, 2 skipped (both `#[ignore]`d by design, matching this crate's own `real_lfm2_checkpoint.rs` convention -- not an N==0 defect). `cargo nextest run -j 2 -p proxima-model-interop --features std -E 'binary(qwen35_synth_hybrid)'`: 0 run, 1 skipped (the Metal test correctly does not exist under this feature set). The full `proxima-model-interop` suite was NOT re-run this row (box contention from other agents at load-1 25-50 for most of this session; only new files were added, no `src/` line changed, so pre-existing test behavior is very unlikely to be affected -- flagged as unverified, not claimed).

**Axes (principle 8):** numeric -- `BLOCK_COUNT=4` (owner-directed scale-down from documented 64), `VOCAB=128`/`FEED_FORWARD=20480` (shrunk, non-load-bearing for the census). structural -- none new (composes the existing `proxima-gguf` writer + the existing `qwen35`/`generate` bind and forward-program path). **Sans-IO opt-sweep (principle 11):** N/A -- fixture generator and test, not a new runtime component.
